title: Nanotechnology approaches in the current therapy of skin cancer.
text_ai: Skin cancer is a high burden disease with a high impact on global health. Conventional therapies have several drawbacks; thus, the development of effective therapies is required. In this context, nanotechnology approaches are an attractive strategy for cancer therapy because they enable the efficient delivery of drugs and other bioactive molecules to target tissues with low toxic effects. These nanocarriers, including liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, and solid lipid nanoparticles, can encapsulate diverse therapeutic agents such as chemotherapeutics, genes, or photosensitizers. Their nanoscale size facilitates enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect in tumor tissues, improving local drug concentrations while minimizing systemic exposure. Moreover, nanotechnology enables targeted delivery through surface functionalization with ligands specific to cancer cell receptors, further boosting efficacy and reducing off-target effects. This review explores recent advancements in nanotechnology applications for skin cancer therapy, focusing on strategies for improved drug delivery, photodynamic therapy, and diagnostic capabilities. We discuss the potential of these innovative approaches to overcome current therapeutic challenges and pave the way for more effective and less invasive treatment modalities.

title: Convergence of drift-diffusion PDEs arising as Wasserstein gradient flows of convex functions
text_ai: We study the quantitative convergence of drift-diffusion PDEs that arise as Wasserstein gradient flows of linearly convex functions over the space of probability measures on ${\mathbb R}^d$. In this setting, the objective is in general not displacement convex, so it is not clear a priori whether global convergence even holds. Despite this, we establish global convergence to the unique minimizer. This is achieved by exploiting the specific structure of linearly convex functions, which, though not displacement convex, still allow for robust analysis of their Wasserstein gradient flows. Our methodology integrates optimal transport theory and functional analysis, via novel Lyapunov functions and tailored functional inequalities. We prove quantitative exponential convergence rates in the 2-Wasserstein distance. These rates apply to a broad class of drift-diffusion PDEs from such potentials, under mild regularity and for initial measures with finite second moments. This work significantly extends existing convergence theory for Wasserstein gradient flows, establishing explicit rates and global convergence in a challenging non-displacement convex regime, thus providing new insights into these fundamental PDEs' long-time behavior.

title: Cognitive system to achieve human-level accuracy in automated assignment of helpdesk email tickets
text_ai: Ticket assignment/dispatch is a crucial part of service delivery business with lot of scope for automation and optimization. In this paper, we present an end-to-end automated helpdesk email ticket assignment system, which is also offered as a service. It leverages advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and deep learning architectures to intelligently parse email content, extract crucial entities, and understand user intent. The system employs a multi-layered classification engine, trained on vast historical helpdesk data, capable of adapting to nuanced language and evolving service categories. A core cognitive component facilitates continuous learning from human expert feedback and operational outcomes, enabling dynamic refinement of its assignment logic. Through rigorous evaluation on real-world datasets, we demonstrate that our proposed solution achieves classification accuracy benchmarked against expert human dispatchers, consistently reaching human-level performance. This significant improvement over traditional rule-based or simpler machine learning models translates into drastically reduced misrouting rates, faster first-response times, and enhanced operational efficiency. Offered as a scalable cloud service, it provides organizations with a robust, self-improving tool to optimize service delivery, allowing human agents to focus on complex problem-solving rather than routine dispatch tasks.

title: Generic algebraic properties in spaces of enumerated groups
text_ai: We introduce and study Polish topologies on various spaces of countable enumerated groups, where an enumerated group is simply a group whose underlying set is the set of natural numbers. Using elementary tools and well known examples from combinatorial group theory, combined with the Baire category theorem, we obtain a plethora of results demonstrating that several phenomena in group theory are generic. Specifically, we demonstrate that having an unsolvable word problem, being non-amenable, and not being finitely presented are all generic properties. These findings extend to various other significant algebraic phenomena, including the existence of specific types of subgroups, quotients, and certain growth rate behaviors. Our work reveals that, from a topological perspective, many properties considered "pathological" are, in fact, typical. This offers a new lens to understand the prevalence and distribution of complex algebraic structures within countable groups.

title: Derivation and maintenance of mouse haploid embryonic stem cells.
text_ai: Ploidy represents the number of chromosome sets in a cell. Although gametes have a haploid genome (n), most mammalian cells have diploid genomes (2n). The diploid status of most cells correlates with the number of probable alleles for each autosomal gene and makes it difficult to target these genes via mutagenesis techniques. However, haploid cells, possessing a single set of chromosomes, offer a unique advantage for genetic studies as only one allele needs to be targeted. Mouse haploid embryonic stem cells (mHSCs) are pluripotent stem cells that maintain a stable haploid karyotype in vitro. This characteristic makes them ideal for efficient genetic screens, allowing for straightforward identification of loss-of-function phenotypes. Here, we detail comprehensive protocols for the derivation of mHSCs from parthenogenetically activated oocytes and their subsequent stable maintenance, crucially addressing methods to prevent spontaneous diploidization. We also describe techniques for their genetic manipulation and differentiation. These mHSCs represent a powerful and versatile platform for functional genomics, drug discovery, and the study of gene function.

title: Napoleonic Constructions in the Hyperbolic Plane
text_ai: In the Euclidean setting, Napoleon's Theorem states that if one constructs an equilateral triangle on either the outside or the inside of each side of a given triangle and then connects the barycenters of those three new triangles, the resulting triangle happens to be equilateral. This paper extends this construction to the hyperbolic plane, a non-Euclidean geometry of constant negative curvature. We adapt the definitions of equilateral triangles and barycenters to the hyperbolic metric. Our investigation reveals that, unlike its Euclidean counterpart, the resulting triangle formed by connecting these barycenters is generally *not* equilateral. However, we identify specific conditions on the initial triangle's parameters and hyperbolic curvature under which the final triangle exhibits equilateral or other regular characteristics. This analysis offers novel insights into the behavior of Euclidean constructions in non-Euclidean spaces, highlighting the profound impact of geometric axioms on fundamental theorems.

title: On the Analysis of Puncturing for Finite-Length Polar Codes: Boolean Function Approach
text_ai: This paper investigates the impact of puncturing on finite-length polar codes in which a puncturing pattern $\pv^{N}=(p_0,...,p_N)$ is applied to a length-$N$ polar code.. We first introduce two virtual channels to stochastically model the punctured (untransmitted) bits, which are respectively called {\em useless channel model} (UCM) and {\em deterministic channel model} (DCM). These models enable a rigorous analysis of effective bit-channel characteristics under puncturing. Leveraging these virtual channels, we introduce a novel analytical framework based on Boolean functions to precisely characterize the capacity and reliability of punctured polar codes. This approach facilitates the exact computation of bit-channel capacities for any given puncturing pattern, offering a powerful tool for code design. We demonstrate that the Boolean function representation provides significant insights into the polarization phenomenon in punctured scenarios, revealing how puncturing strategies affect overall code performance. Our analysis yields a systematic method for selecting optimal puncturing patterns for finite-length polar codes, maximizing throughput and maintaining desired error rates. Numerical results validate the accuracy of our models and the effectiveness of the proposed design.

title: How Dense is Your Gas? On the recoverability of LVG model parameters
text_ai: We explore the recoverability of gas physical conditions with the Large Velocity Gradient (LVG) model, using the public code RADEX and the molecules HCN and CO. Examining a wide parameter range with a series of models of increasing complexity we use both grid and Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) methods to recover the input conditions, and quantify the inherent and noise induced uncertainties in the model results. Our analysis reveals that while kinetic temperature ($T_k$) and molecular column density ($N$) are generally well-constrained, gas density ($n_{H_2}$) frequently exhibits significant degeneracies, exacerbated by realistic observational noise and limited transitions. This broadens posterior distributions and increases parameter uncertainty. Combining HCN and CO significantly improves parameter recovery, effectively disentangling $T_k$ from $n_{H_2}$. HCN's higher critical density constrains denser gas components, complementing CO's broader sensitivity. Both MCMC and grid methods highlight intrinsic LVG model limitations, though MCMC offers more comprehensive uncertainty quantification. Our findings underscore the critical importance of diverse molecular transitions and careful signal-to-noise ratio consideration for reliable physical condition inference, especially for robustly determining absolute gas density.

title: The conundrum of stock versus bond prices
text_ai: In a general way, stock and bond prices do not display any significant correlation. Yet, if we concentrate our attention on specific episodes marked by a crash followed by a rebound, then we observe that stock prices have a strong connection with interest rates on the one hand, and with bond yield spreads on the other hand. This observed shift during market stress presents a conundrum, suggesting altered asset pricing. We propose heightened risk aversion, liquidity shocks, and central bank interventions forge a temporary, robust linkage. This paper employs a novel dynamic econometric framework to analyze these interdependencies across historical crash-rebound cycles. Using comprehensive equity, interest rate, and bond yield data, our findings reveal that stock prices, generally decoupled, become highly sensitive to policy rates and credit risk premia in crises. Specifically, widening corporate bond spreads, signaling deteriorating credit and reduced liquidity, disproportionately impact stock valuations negatively in downturns; their narrowing drives equity rebounds. These results provide nuanced understanding of asset price dynamics under stress, highlighting fixed income markets as critical leading indicators and transmission mechanisms for systemic risk to equities. Implications arise for asset allocation and risk management during financial instability.

title: Are Bitcoins price predictable? Evidence from machine learning techniques using technical indicators
text_ai: The uncertainties in future Bitcoin price make it difficult to accurately predict the price of Bitcoin. Accurately predicting the price for Bitcoin is therefore important for decision-making process of investors and market players in the cryptocurrency market. Despite this critical need, traditional econometric models often struggle to capture the non-linear and complex dynamics inherent in cryptocurrency markets. This study addresses this gap by systematically investigating Bitcoin price predictability using advanced machine learning techniques. We employ Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests (RF), Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, integrating a diverse set of well-established technical indicators derived from historical price and volume data as crucial input features. Using high-frequency historical data from major cryptocurrency exchanges, we rigorously evaluate these models' predictive performance across various time horizons. Our empirical results demonstrate that certain machine learning models, notably LSTM and Gradient Boosting, significantly outperform traditional benchmarks and simpler models in predicting short-term Bitcoin price direction and magnitude. Furthermore, the strategic inclusion of technical indicators proves instrumental in substantially enhancing model accuracy and robustness. These findings provide valuable insights into employing sophisticated machine learning approaches to navigate the volatile Bitcoin market, offering a more informed basis for investment strategies and risk management.

title: Identification of materials with strong magneto-structural coupling using computational high-throughput screening
text_ai: Important phenomena such as magnetostriction, magnetocaloric, and magnetoelectric effects arise from, or could be enhanced by, the coupling of magnetic and structural degrees of freedom. The coupling of spin and lattice also influence transport and structural properties in magnetic materials in particular around phase transitions. The experimental discovery of novel materials exhibiting strong magneto-structural coupling, crucial for advanced technologies, is often time-consuming. This work introduces a computational high-throughput screening strategy to efficiently identify such compounds. Leveraging first-principles density functional theory (DFT), we systematically evaluated a large database of inorganic materials. Our screening methodology focused on quantifying key metrics indicative of robust spin-lattice interactions, including magnetovolume effects, magnetic anisotropy energies, and phonon mode softening across magnetic phase transitions. This approach successfully pinpointed several promising candidates, comprising both known systems with potentially enhanced coupling and previously uncharacterized materials. These predictions offer a targeted guide for future experimental synthesis and characterization, accelerating next-generation functional materials development.

title: Automated Bridge Component Recognition using Video Data
text_ai: This paper investigates the automated recognition of structural bridge components using video data. Although understanding video data for structural inspections is straightforward for human inspectors, the implementation of the same task using machine learning methods has not been fully realized. Challenges arise from the inherent complexities of real-world video footage, including varying environmental conditions, diverse component geometries, and the scarcity of large, annotated datasets tailored for bridge infrastructure. To address these, we propose a novel deep learning framework. Our approach integrates a specialized convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture optimized for robust object detection and semantic segmentation of common bridge components like girders, bearings, and deck slabs directly from video streams. A meticulously annotated dataset, encompassing diverse bridge types and environmental conditions, was compiled for training and validation. Experimental results demonstrate high accuracy and robustness in identifying these components across diverse video inputs, outperforming baseline object detection models. This research significantly advances automated bridge inspection, offering a scalable and efficient solution for condition assessment and maintenance.

title: Spectral Efficiency Maximization for DMA-enabled Multiuser MISO with Statistical CSI
text_ai: Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) offer the potential to achieve large-scale antenna arrays with low power consumption and reduced hardware costs, making them a promising technology for future communication systems. This paper investigates the spectral efficiency (SE) of DMA-enabled multiuser multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems in both uplink and downlink transmissions, using only statistical channel state information (CSI) to maximize the ergodic sum rate of multiple users. We formulate a non-convex optimization problem to jointly optimize DMA reflection coefficients and beamforming vectors for uplink and downlink, maximizing the ergodic sum rate under statistical CSI. DMA's phase-only, discrete control introduces significant non-linearity. An efficient alternating optimization algorithm iteratively refines DMA configuration and beamforming vectors. It leverages statistical channel properties to maximize average SINR. Simulations show substantial SE gains over conventional and baseline DMA strategies with statistical CSI. It exhibits robust performance across diverse channel conditions, balancing hardware complexity and achievable data rates. These findings underscore DMA-enabled systems' potential to enhance future wireless network capacity and efficiency.

title: Optimizing squeezing in a coherent quantum feedback network of optical parametric oscillators
text_ai: Advances in the emerging field of coherent quantum feedback control (CQFC) have led to the development of new capabilities in the areas of quantum control and quantum engineering, with a particular impact on the theory and applications of quantum optical networks. Building on this, the generation of squeezed states of light is paramount for quantum metrology and continuous-variable quantum computing. Optical parametric oscillators (OPOs) are key sources, but optimizing their squeezing often requires stringent conditions or cascaded architectures. This paper investigates integrating OPOs into a coherent quantum feedback network to enhance squeezing. We develop a comprehensive theoretical model for a network of interconnected OPOs, analyzing how coherent feedback loops maximize output squeezing across various configurations. Our analysis demonstrates that specific feedback topologies and optimized coupling strengths significantly improve the degree of squeezing, surpassing standalone OPOs or simple feed-forward schemes. These findings offer a robust theoretical basis for designing compact, efficient, and tunable sources of highly squeezed light, crucial for advancing quantum information processing and precision measurements.

title: Discovering Relationships between Object Categories via Universal Canonical Maps
text_ai: We tackle the problem of learning the geometry of multiple categories of deformable objects jointly. Recent work has shown that it is possible to learn a unified dense pose predictor for several categories of related objects. However, training such models requires to initialize inter-category correspondences by hand. To overcome this critical limitation, we propose a novel unsupervised framework for automatically discovering these underlying geometric relationships. Our core contribution is the introduction of Universal Canonical Maps (UCMs), a shared, category-agnostic latent representation designed to intrinsically capture common structural properties across diverse deformable object types. By learning to embed instances from different categories into this universal canonical space, our method automatically identifies semantically consistent correspondences and shared deformation modes. This approach eliminates the arduous requirement for manual inter-category correspondence initialization, thereby significantly reducing annotation effort and improving scalability. Extensive experiments on challenging multi-category datasets demonstrate that our UCMs effectively learn robust universal maps, leading to superior performance in dense pose prediction and enabling novel applications such as cross-category shape transfer and analogy making, even for previously unseen category pairs.

title: Direct observation of multiple topological phases in the iron-based superconductor Li(Fe,Co)As
text_ai: Topological insulators/semimetals and unconventional iron-based superconductors have attracted major attentions in condensed matter physics in the past 10 years. However, there is little overlap between these two fields, although the combination of topological states and superconducting states will produce more exotic topologically superconducting states and Majorana bound states (MBS), a promising candidate for realizing topological quantum computations. Here, we report the direct observation of multiple topological phases in the iron-based superconductor Li(Fe,Co)As using high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). Our detailed electronic structure measurements reveal the presence of prominent Dirac-like surface states and a bulk topological phase transition driven by cobalt doping. Specifically, we observe a clear band inversion at the Z point and the emergence of topological surface states that span the bulk superconducting gap. These findings provide compelling experimental evidence for the coexistence of both topological and superconducting properties within this single material system. This makes Li(Fe,Co)As an exceptional platform for exploring the intricate interplay between topology and unconventional superconductivity, offering a promising avenue for the realization and manipulation of Majorana bound states crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Discontinuation of disease-modifying therapy in patients with multiple sclerosis over age 60.
text_ai: The risk-benefit ratio of continuing immunomodulating disease-modifying therapy (DMT) in older multiple sclerosis (MS) patients is unknown. To evaluate clinical and patient-reported outcomes after stopping DMT in older MS patients. Retrospective, observational study identifying patients from our MS clinics who were aged over 60 and on DMT > 2 years. We identified 125 eligible patients; 87 chose to discontinue DMT. Baseline demographics, MS phenotype, EDSS, prior relapse activity, and patient-reported outcomes (PROs) were collected. Median follow-up was 3.5 years post-discontinuation. Clinical outcomes included annualized relapse rate (ARR), confirmed disability progression (CDP), and new MRI lesion activity. Among 87 discontinuing patients (mean age 67.2 ± 4.5 years; 65% progressive MS), 12 (13.8%) relapsed and 8 (9.2%) showed CDP. The post-discontinuation ARR (0.04) was not significantly different from the pre-discontinuation ARR (0.03). New MRI lesions occurred in 9 (10.3%). PROs, including fatigue and quality of life, remained largely stable. Our findings suggest that discontinuing DMT in carefully selected older MS patients with stable disease may be safe, with a low risk of increased disease activity. This supports a personalized approach to DMT management in this population, considering individual disease activity, comorbidity, and patient preferences.

title: Confined Dense Circumstellar Material Surrounding a Regular Type II Supernova: The Unique Flash-Spectroscopy Event of SN 2013fs
text_ai: With the advent of new wide-field, high-cadence optical transient surveys, our understanding of the diversity of core-collapse supernovae has grown tremendously in the last decade. However, the pre-supernova evolution of massive stars, that sets the physical backdrop to these violent events, is theoretically not well understood and difficult to probe observationally. Flash spectroscopy, capturing the early interaction of the supernova ejecta with its immediate surroundings, offers a unique window into this elusive phase. Here, we present a detailed analysis of the exceptional flash-spectroscopy sequence of SN 2013fs, a regular Type II supernova observed within hours of explosion. Our observations reveal strong, narrow emission lines of Hα, He I, and other species, indicating the presence of very dense circumstellar material (CSM) located remarkably close to the progenitor star. Modeling these spectra suggests that the CSM is confined to within ~10^15 cm from the progenitor, with a mass exceeding 0.1 solar masses, implying an exceptionally high mass-loss rate (>10^-2 M☉/yr) in the final year before explosion. This confined, dense CSM points to a sudden and intense mass-loss episode shortly before core-collapse, challenging existing steady-wind models for Type II supernova progenitors. SN 2013fs thus provides a crucial observational constraint, demonstrating the necessity of considering eruptive pre-supernova activity in massive star evolution.

title: CL-HOI: Cross-Level Human-Object Interaction Distillation from Vision Large Language Models
text_ai: Human-object interaction (HOI) detection has seen advancements with Vision Language Models (VLMs), but these methods often depend on extensive manual annotations. Vision Large Language Models (VLLMs) can inherently recognize and reason about interactions at the image level but are computationally heavy and not designed for instance-level HOI detection. To bridge this critical gap, we introduce CL-HOI (Cross-Level Human-Object Interaction), a novel distillation framework designed to transfer the rich, implicit interaction understanding from VLLMs into efficient, instance-level HOI detectors. CL-HOI employs a unique cross-level distillation strategy, where VLLMs are prompted to generate textual descriptions and bounding box detections, from which high-quality pseudo-labels for HOI triplets are automatically inferred. This process effectively bypasses the need for extensive manual annotations, making it highly scalable. Our extensive experiments on challenging benchmarks, HICO-DET and V-COCO, demonstrate that CL-HOI significantly outperforms state-of-the-art weakly-supervised and few-shot HOI methods. Moreover, it achieves competitive performance with fully-supervised approaches while drastically reducing computational overhead and annotation reliance, marking a significant step towards practical and scalable HOI detection.

title: Nuclear spin pair coherence in diamond for atomic scale magnetometry
text_ai: The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre, as a promising candidate solid state system of quantum information processing, its electron spin coherence is influenced by the magnetic field fluctuations due to the local environment. In pure diamonds, the environment consists of hundreds of C-13 nuclear spins randomly spreading in several nanometers range forming a spin bath. While this dense C-13 spin bath typically acts as a primary source of decoherence for the NV electron spin, it simultaneously presents a unique opportunity to harness individual or coupled nuclear spins for atomic-scale quantum sensing. Focusing specifically on strongly coupled pairs of C-13 nuclear spins within this bath, we exploit their enhanced robustness and relative isolation from the broader ensemble. These nuclear spin pairs exhibit remarkably long coherence times, which can be further protected through dynamic decoupling and advanced quantum control protocols. By coherently manipulating the entangled states of these pairs, their collective response to external magnetic fields can be precisely interrogated. This approach enables highly sensitive magnetometry with unprecedented spatial resolution, effectively probing magnetic fields at the atomic scale. We demonstrate the coherent control and interrogation of such C-13 nuclear spin pairs, showcasing their efficacy as robust, high-resolution magnetic sensors. This strategy leverages the inherent advantages of nuclear spin pair coherence to overcome limitations of single-spin sensing, offering a novel pathway for precision measurements in diverse scientific domains.

This unprecedented baseline length (7200 km) offers exceptional sensitivity to the atmospheric mass splitting, $\Delta m^2_{32}$, and provides a powerful lever arm to probe the neutrino mass hierarchy and potential CP violation in the lepton sector. The significant matter effects encountered over such a distance enhance the sensitivity to the mass ordering. We detail the design of a high-intensity muon neutrino beam derived from pion decay at KAON, with characteristics optimized for detection at Superkamiokande. The primary oscillation channels investigated would include $

title: Oscillations in three-reaction quadratic mass-action systems
text_ai: It is known that rank-two bimolecular mass-action systems do not admit limit cycles. With a view to understanding which small mass-action systems admit oscillation, in this paper we study rank-two networks with bimolecular source complexes but allow target complexes with higher molecularities. Specifically, we investigate three-reaction quadratic mass-action systems within this generalized framework, identifying minimal architectural requirements for oscillation. Using detailed stability analysis of the system's fixed points and applying the Bendixson-Dulac criterion, we systematically explore the parameter space for the existence of limit cycles. We also employ numerical continuation techniques to identify Hopf bifurcations and track the emergence of periodic orbits. Our findings reveal that, unlike their purely bimolecular counterparts, certain configurations of these three-reaction systems indeed admit stable limit cycles. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions on the reaction rate constants and initial concentrations for the occurrence of Hopf bifurcations, leading to sustained oscillations. Specifically, we identify minimal network motifs and parameter regimes where such oscillatory dynamics are observed, demonstrating that the introduction of higher-molecularity target complexes fundamentally alters the dynamical landscape. This work provides a crucial step towards mapping the boundaries of oscillatory behavior in small chemical reaction networks, highlighting the critical role of reaction stoichiometry beyond pure bimolecularity in enabling complex dynamics.

title: AudioSR: Versatile Audio Super-resolution at Scale
text_ai: Audio super-resolution is a fundamental task that predicts high-frequency components for low-resolution audio, enhancing audio quality in digital applications. Previous methods have limitations such as the limited scope of audio types (e.g., music, speech) and specific bandwidth settings they can handle (e.g., 4kHz to 8kHz). To address these limitations, we introduce AudioSR, a novel, versatile framework for audio super-resolution. Leveraging a multi-scale transformer architecture trained on an unprecedentedly diverse and large-scale dataset, AudioSR generalizes across a vast spectrum of audio types (speech, music, environmental sounds) and flexibly handles various bandwidth expansion factors (e.g., 4kHz to 32kHz). Our extensive evaluations demonstrate AudioSR significantly surpasses existing methods in perceptual quality and objective metrics across diverse benchmarks, consistently achieving state-of-the-art performance. This versatility and scalability position AudioSR as a foundational advancement for practical, high-quality audio enhancement applications.

title: Graph-Aware Language Model Pre-Training on a Large Graph Corpus Can Help Multiple Graph Applications
text_ai: Model pre-training on large text corpora has been demonstrated effective for various downstream applications in the NLP domain. In the graph mining domain, a similar analogy can be drawn for pre-training graph models on large graphs in the hope of benefiting downstream graph applications, which has also been explored by several recent studies. However, explicitly integrating language model capabilities with graph structural awareness during pre-training on a truly large and diverse graph corpus remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel framework for Graph-Aware Language Model Pre-Training (GAMLPT) designed to learn rich, transferable representations by jointly encoding both intricate structural relationships and abundant textual attributes inherent in graph data. We leverage a massive, heterogeneous graph corpus to pre-train our model, employing objectives that capture both local graph topology and global semantic coherence of associated text. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our GAMLPT model significantly enhances performance across multiple downstream graph applications, including node classification, link prediction, and graph classification, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. This work establishes a powerful new paradigm for combining linguistic and structural understanding in graph learning.

title: CIMTx: An R package for causal inference with multiple treatments using observational data
text_ai: CIMTx provides efficient and unified functions to implement modern methods for causal inferences with multiple treatments using observational data with a focus on binary outcomes. The methods include regression adjustment, inverse probability of treatment weighting, Bayesian additive regression trees, regression adjustment with multivariate spline of the generalized propensity score, vector matching and targeted maximum likelihood estimation. The package is designed to provide a user-friendly interface for applying and comparing these diverse methodologies, thereby streamlining the process of estimating causal effects in complex observational studies. CIMTx facilitates robust analysis by incorporating functionalities for propensity score estimation, covariate balance checks, and effect estimation under various assumptions. By unifying these advanced techniques, CIMTx empowers researchers and practitioners to rigorously evaluate the impact of multiple interventions, offering flexibility and promoting transparent reporting of causal estimates. The package is freely available on CRAN, contributing to accessible and reproducible causal inference research.

title: Voyager 2 solar plasma and magnetic field spectral analysis for intermediate data sparsity
text_ai: The Voyager probes are the furthest, still active, spacecraft ever launched from Earth. During their 38-year trip, they have collected data regarding solar wind properties (such as the plasma velocity and magnetic field intensity). Unfortunately, a complete time evolution of the measured physical quantities is not available. This inherent data sparsity, particularly at intermediate levels, necessitates specialized methodologies for robust spectral analysis. This work presents a comprehensive spectral analysis of Voyager 2 solar wind plasma and magnetic field data, specifically addressing the challenges posed by irregularly sampled and gapped datasets. We employ advanced spectral estimation techniques, including optimized Lomb-Scargle periodograms and wavelet transforms, which are robust against missing data and capable of resolving power spectral densities across a broad range of frequencies. Our analysis aims to characterize the turbulent properties of the solar wind, identify dominant wave phenomena, and investigate energy transfer mechanisms in both the heliosheath and the nascent interstellar medium. By carefully accounting for the intermediate data sparsity, we derive reliable power law indices and spectral breaks, revealing crucial insights into the evolution of plasma turbulence as Voyager 2 traverses distinct astrophysical environments. These findings contribute significantly to our understanding of fundamental heliospheric processes and the interaction of the solar system with the local interstellar medium, under conditions previously inaccessible to continuous observation.

title: Discrete-to-continuum limits of interacting particle systems in one dimension with collisions
text_ai: We study a class of interacting particle systems in which $n$ signed particles move on the real line. At close range particles with the same sign repel and particles with opposite sign attract each other. The repulsion and attraction are described by the same singular interaction force $f$. The particles evolve according to Newton's laws, with the singular nature of $f$ ensuring elastic collisions that preserve particle ordering. We rigorously investigate the discrete-to-continuum limit under hydrodynamic scaling, where the number of particles $n \to \infty$ and interaction parameters are scaled appropriately. In this limit, the empirical measure of the particle system converges to a macroscopic description governed by a novel system of coupled partial differential equations. This continuum model consists of two pressureless Euler equations for the densities of positive particles $\rho_+(x,t)$ and negative particles $\rho_-(x,t)$. A key contribution is the rigorous derivation and characterization of a unique, non-local collision term arising directly from the singular interaction force and elastic collisions at the microscopic level. This term effectively models momentum transfer and inter-species interaction. Our results establish a robust mathematical framework for analyzing the collective dynamics of such systems, offering insights into phenomena like pattern formation and wave propagation in complex interacting particle systems.

title: Single-Particle Green Functions in Exactly Solvable Models of Bose and Fermi Liquids
text_ai: Based on a class of exactly solvable models of interacting bose and fermi liquids, we compute the single-particle propagators of these systems exactly for all wavelengths and energies and in any number of spatial dimensions. Our exact results reveal detailed spectral properties, including precise quasiparticle lifetimes and spectral functions exhibiting non-Lorentzian line shapes and power-law singularities, particularly in low-dimensional systems and at strong coupling. For Fermi liquids, we rigorously demonstrate the breakdown of the conventional quasiparticle picture beyond the Landau regime, elucidating emergent non-Fermi liquid characteristics. In Bose liquids, the analysis provides exact insights into condensate depletion and collective excitations, offering direct comparison to Bogoliubov theory and its limitations. These analytical solutions offer invaluable benchmarks for validating approximate theoretical frameworks and numerical simulations, thus advancing our fundamental understanding of correlation effects in quantum many-body systems.

title: Rashba interferometers: Spin-dependent single and two-electron interference
text_ai: Quantum transport in semiconductor nanostructures can be described theoretically in terms of the propagation and scattering of electron probability waves. Within this approach, elements of a phase-coherent electric circuit play a role similar to quantum-optical devices that can be characterised by scattering matrices. A crucial element in modern spintronics is the Rashba spin-orbit interaction, coupling an electron's spin to its momentum. This allows electrical spin manipulation and induces a spin-dependent phase accumulation as electrons traverse a region with strong Rashba coupling. This phase accumulation is exploited in Rashba interferometers, making interference patterns sensitive to spin orientation. Such devices allow investigation of the Aharonov-Casher effect, non-local spin current generation, and the creation of spin filters, offering pathways for all-electrical spin control. The scattering matrix formalism adeptly models single-particle spin precession and dephasing within these coherent structures. Extending this framework to two-electron systems reveals intriguing possibilities for spin-dependent entanglement and correlation effects. We explore how Rashba interaction influences two-electron interference patterns in coupled interferometers, where one electron's spin state can modulate another's transport properties. This includes analyzing Pauli exclusion and Coulomb interaction effects on two-particle scattering outcomes, highlighting their role in spin-entangled electron pairs.

title: Best Practices for Alchemical Free Energy Calculations
text_ai: Alchemical free energy calculations are a useful tool for predicting free energy differences associated with the transfer of molecules from one environment to another. The hallmark of these methods is the use of "bridging" potential energy functions representing \emph{alchemical} intermediate states that cannot exist as real chemical species. While offering significant predictive power, the accuracy and reliability of these calculations are highly sensitive to methodological choices. This paper synthesizes best practices for all stages of alchemical free energy calculations, covering critical aspects such as force field selection, alchemical pathway design, conformational sampling, and statistical analysis. We provide practical guidelines for researchers on ensuring convergence, quantifying uncertainties, and validating predictions. Adherence to these recommendations enhances the precision, accuracy, and reproducibility of alchemical free energy calculations, strengthening their utility in molecular design and drug discovery applications.

title: Conformational selection and induced changes along the catalytic cycle of E. coli DHFR
text_ai: Protein function often involves changes between different conformations. Central questions are how these conformational changes are coupled to the binding or catalytic processes during which they occur, and how they affect the catalytic rates of enzymes. An important model system is the enzyme dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) from E. coli. This enzyme catalyzes the reduction of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate, a crucial step in nucleotide biosynthesis, making it a key target for antibacterial drugs. *E. coli* DHFR is known to interconvert between several distinct conformational substates, such as the 'closed', 'occluded', and 'open' forms. We investigate the dynamic interplay between these pre-existing conformational ensembles and ligand-induced structural rearrangements throughout the enzyme's catalytic cycle. Our analysis reveals that while the enzyme populates specific states via conformational selection even in the absence of substrates, the binding of dihydrofolate and NADPH induces significant shifts in these conformational equilibria, guiding the enzyme through its catalytic progression. Specifically, we delineate how the transition from the 'open' to 'closed' state facilitates substrate binding and hydride transfer, while subsequent changes are essential for product release. These findings highlight a sophisticated mechanism where both intrinsic dynamics and induced fit mechanisms are tightly coupled to optimize catalytic efficiency, providing a detailed understanding of how conformational changes drive and regulate the enzymatic turnover of *E. coli* DHFR.

title: Graphical Modelling in Genetics and Systems Biology
text_ai: Graphical modelling has a long history in statistics as a tool for the analysis of multivariate data, starting from Wright's path analysis and Gibbs' applications to statistical physics at the beginning of the last century. More recently, their utility has expanded significantly into the life sciences, particularly in genetics for deciphering complex trait architectures, identifying causal variants, and reconstructing gene regulatory networks. In systems biology, graphical models provide a powerful framework for dissecting intricate molecular interactions, such as protein-protein interaction networks, metabolic pathways, and signal transduction cascades, facilitating the integration of diverse omics data. This paper reviews the evolution and application of various graphical modelling techniques, including Bayesian networks and Gaussian graphical models, within these domains. We discuss their strengths in elucidating mechanistic insights, predicting system behavior, and inferring causality from high-dimensional biological data. We also address computational challenges and statistical considerations, highlighting emerging trends and future directions for graphical modelling in contemporary genetic and systems biology research.

title: Financial Burdens of Out-of-Pocket Spending Among Medicare Fee-for-Service Beneficiaries: Role of the "Big Four" Chronic Health Conditions.
text_ai: While Medicare is the universal source of health care coverage for Americans aged 65 years or older, the program requires significant cost sharing in terms of out-of-pocket (OOP) spending. This financial burden is particularly pronounced for beneficiaries managing chronic health conditions, who often incur substantial costs for ongoing care, medications, and specialized services. This study examines the financial impact of OOP spending among Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) beneficiaries, focusing on the "Big Four" chronic health conditions: heart disease, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Using administrative claims data, we analyzed the relationship between the presence of these conditions and the likelihood of experiencing high OOP spending, defined as a percentage of household income. Our findings reveal that beneficiaries with one or more of the "Big Four" conditions face significantly elevated OOP expenditures, contributing to disproportionate financial strain. The cumulative effect of multiple chronic conditions further intensifies this burden. These results highlight critical vulnerabilities in Medicare's cost-sharing structure, particularly for beneficiaries with complex health needs, and suggest policy implications for reducing financial hardship.

title: Cocommutative q-cycle coalgebra structures on the dual of the truncated polynomial algebra
text_ai: In order to construct solutions of the braid equation we consider bijective left non-degenerate set-theoretic type solutions, which correspond to regular q-cycle coalgebras. We obtain a partial classification of the different q-cycle coalgebra structures on the dual coalgebra of $K[y]/\langle y^n\rangle$, the truncated polynomial algebra. Specifically, we classify the cocommutative q-cycle coalgebra structures on $K[y]/\langle y^n\rangle^*$. Our findings reveal a finite set of such structures for each $n$, uniquely determined by a primitive element and the structural constants of the dual basis. These cocommutative q-cycle coalgebras are co-Frobenius, possessing a unique simple comodule up to isomorphism, and their internal structure links to the arithmetic properties of $n$. This work offers concrete examples of regular q-cycle coalgebras, providing new avenues for constructing and understanding solutions to the braid equation within finite-dimensional cocommutative Hopf algebras.

title: Effects of Stellar Feedback on Stellar and Gas Kinematics of Star-Forming Galaxies at 0.6<z<1.0
text_ai: Recent zoom-in cosmological simulations have shown that stellar feedback can flatten the inner density profile of the dark matter halo in low-mass galaxies. A correlation between the stellar/gas velocity dispersion ($\sigma_{star}$, $\sigma_{gas}$) and the specific star formation rate (sSFR) is predicted as an observational test of the role of stellar feedback in re-shaping the dark matter density profile. In this study, we investigate this prediction using spatially resolved kinematic data from integral field spectroscopy (IFS) for a sample of 78 star-forming galaxies at 0.6 < z < 1.0 from the KMOS3D survey. We derive $\sigma_{star}$ from stellar absorption lines and $\sigma_{gas}$ from nebular emission lines (H$\alpha$, [NII]), alongside sSFRs from multi-wavelength SED fitting. Our analysis reveals a significant anti-correlation between both $\sigma_{star}$ and $\sigma_{gas}$ and the sSFR. Galaxies exhibiting higher sSFRs consistently show lower central velocity dispersions. This observed trend aligns with theoretical models where intense stellar feedback, associated with elevated star formation activity, efficiently transfers energy to surrounding baryonic and dark matter components. Such energy injection is hypothesized to reduce the central gravitational potential by expelling gas, leading to the observed flattening of the inner dark matter density profile and consequently lower velocity dispersions. Our findings provide strong observational support for the critical role of stellar feedback in modifying the inner mass distribution and kinematic states of star-forming galaxies during a key epoch of galaxy evolution.

title: Seroepidemiology of Toxoplasma gondii in wild ruminants in Spain.
text_ai: Toxoplasmosis is a parasitic zoonosis caused by Toxoplasma gondii which infects warm-blooded species worldwide. Serum samples from a large cohort of red deer (*Cervus elaphus*), fallow deer (*Dama dama*), roe deer (*Capreolus capreolus*), mouflon (*Ovis aries musimon*), aoudad (*Ammotragus lervia*), Iberian ibex (*Capra pyrenaica*), and chamois (*Rupicapra pyrenaica*) were collected across diverse regions and analyzed using an indirect ELISA. The overall seroprevalence for *T. gondii* was XX.X%. Inter-species variation was significant; red deer and mouflon showed highest seroprevalence, chamois and roe deer the lowest. Spatial analysis revealed distinct geographical clusters of higher seroprevalence, often associated with environmental or anthropogenic factors. These findings highlight the widespread circulation of *T. gondii* in Spanish wild ruminants, demonstrating their significant role as intermediate hosts and potential public health risk through game meat. This study provides crucial data for risk assessments and wildlife management strategies.

title: Image Quality Assessment Guided Deep Neural Networks Training
text_ai: For many computer vision problems, the deep neural networks are trained and validated based on the assumption that the input images are pristine (i.e., artifact-free). However, digital images are subject to a wide range of distortions in real application scenarios, while the practical issues regarding image quality in high level visual information understanding have been largely ignored. This oversight often leads to a significant performance drop when networks encounter real-world degraded inputs. To address this, we propose a novel 'Image Quality Assessment Guided Deep Neural Networks Training' framework. Our method integrates image quality metrics directly into the optimization pipeline, fostering robust, quality-aware features. By explicitly accounting for distortions during training, the network gains enhanced generalization. Extensive experiments demonstrate our IQA-guided training significantly improves model robustness and performance across diverse computer vision tasks on degraded images, bridging a critical gap in deep learning.

title: PeV Neutrinos and a 3.5 keV X-Ray Line from a PeV Scale Supersymmetric Neutrino Sector
text_ai: Recent measurements of PeV energy neutrinos at IceCube and a 3.5 keV X-ray line in the spectra of several galaxies are both tantalizing signatures of new physics. This paper shows that one or both of these observations can be explained within an extended supersymmetric neutrino sector. Specifically, we propose that the 3.5 keV X-ray line arises from the radiative decay of a keV-scale sterile sneutrino, which constitutes a fraction of the observed dark matter. This sterile sneutrino is naturally accommodated within an extended R-parity conserving supersymmetric model featuring right-handed neutrino superfields. Concurrently, the PeV neutrinos are explained by the decay of a much heavier, PeV-scale right-handed sneutrino or sterile neutrino, produced in high-energy astrophysical environments. This heavy state decays into standard model particles, including active neutrinos, with branching ratios consistent with IceCube observations. The model predicts a specific mass hierarchy and interaction strengths for these new supersymmetric particles. We demonstrate that these phenomena can be simultaneously explained, offering a unified framework for these seemingly disparate anomalies. Furthermore, the model has implications for cosmology, leptogenesis, and future collider searches, providing a compelling direction for probing physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: BodyMetric: Evaluating the Realism of Human Bodies in Text-to-Image Generation
text_ai: Accurately generating images of human bodies from text remains a challenging problem for state of the art text-to-image models. Commonly observed body-related artifacts include extra or missing limbs, unrealistic poses, blurred body parts, etc. Currently, evaluation of such artifacts relies heavily on time-consuming human judgments, limiting the ability to benchmark models at scale. To address this, we introduce BodyMetric, a novel, automated framework for quantifying human body realism in text-to-image generation. BodyMetric integrates specialized metrics for anatomical correctness, pose naturalness, and limb integrity. It leverages robust pose estimation and semantic segmentation to precisely identify and quantify common body artifacts. We demonstrate BodyMetric's strong correlation with human perceptual judgments, significantly outperforming general-purpose metrics in specificity and accuracy for body realism. Our evaluation using BodyMetric reveals significant limitations in current state-of-the-art models, particularly in complex multi-person scenes and dynamic poses. BodyMetric provides a robust, scalable benchmark for future advancements in human body generation, offering insights for developers to facilitate rapid iteration towards more realistic, artifact-free systems.

title: Quenched Lattice QCD with Domain Wall Fermions and the Chiral Limit
text_ai: Quenched QCD simulations on three volumes, $8^3 \times$, $12^3 \times$ and $16^3 \times 32$ and three couplings, $\beta=5.7$, 5.85 and 6.0 using domain wall fermions provide a consistent picture of quenched QCD. This consistency manifests in the robust scaling of the hadron spectrum, decay constants, and chiral condensate as lattice spacing is reduced and physical volume varied. The exceptional chiral symmetry of domain wall fermions proves vital for a precise investigation of the chiral limit. We meticulously analyze pion mass and decay constant behavior as the bare quark mass approaches zero, observing characteristic non-analyticities consistent with quenched chiral logarithms, which significantly modify standard chiral perturbation theory predictions. Finite volume effects are systematically explored, confirming their expected suppression for sufficiently large volumes. Continuum limit extrapolations for key observables provide a comprehensive understanding of the quenched QCD vacuum. This study underscores both the efficacy of the domain wall fermion formulation and the inherent challenges in precisely extracting physical quantities from the quenched approximation, particularly in the chiral regime.

title: Relativistic diffusion
text_ai: We discuss a relativistic diffusion in the proper time in an approach of Schay and Dudley. We derive (Langevin) stochastic differential equations in various coordinates.We show that in some coordinates the stochastic differential equations become linear. We obtain momentum probability distribution in an explicit form.We discuss a relativistic particle diffusing in an external electromagnetic field. The linearity of these equations in specific coordinate systems significantly simplifies their analytical treatment, enabling exact solutions for the particle's trajectory and momentum evolution. Consequently, we employ the associated Fokker-Planck equation, which also benefits from this linearity, to derive the explicit form of the momentum probability distribution. This distribution, in the absence of external fields, is shown to reduce to a generalized Jüttner distribution, confirming consistency with thermodynamic equilibrium. When a relativistic particle diffuses in an external electromagnetic field, the Lorentz force terms are naturally incorporated into the stochastic dynamics. We comprehensively analyze the interplay between relativistic effects, field strength, and diffusion, demonstrating how the external field influences the mean-square displacement and the steady-state momentum distribution. This robust framework provides a rigorous and analytically tractable method for understanding relativistic Brownian motion, offering new insights into particle transport phenomena in extreme astrophysical environments and high-energy physics where both relativistic kinematics and stochasticity are paramount.

We derive (Langevin) stochastic differential equations in various coordinates.We show that in some coordinates the stochastic differential equations become linear. We obtain momentum probability distribution in an explicit form.We discuss a relativistic particle diffusing in an external electromagnetic field.

title: Theory of analytical energy derivatives for the variational quantum eigensolver
text_ai: The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and its variants, which is a method for finding eigenstates and eigenenergies of a given Hamiltonian, are appealing applications of near-term quantum computers. Although the eigenenergies are certainly important quantities which determines properties of a given system, their derivatives with respect to parameters of the system, such as positions of nuclei if we target a quantum chemistry problem, are also crucial to analyze the system. Conventionally, these derivatives are computed numerically, which can be computationally expensive and suffer from finite difference approximations. This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical framework for calculating *analytical* energy derivatives for the VQE. We derive explicit expressions for first and second-order energy derivatives with respect to arbitrary system parameters, leveraging the Hellmann-Feynman theorem and parameter-shift rules for quantum circuits. Our approach circumvents the need for finite difference schemes, offering enhanced accuracy and computational efficiency, particularly for complex Hamiltonians and many-parameter systems. This development paves the way for efficient geometry optimizations, molecular dynamics simulations, and property calculations on near-term quantum hardware.

title: NICE^k Metrics: Unified and Multidimensional Framework for Evaluating Deterministic Solar Forecasting Accuracy
text_ai: Accurate solar energy output prediction is key for integrating renewables into grids, maintaining stability, and improving energy management. However, standard error metrics such as Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Skill Scores (SS) fail to capture the multidimensional nature of solar irradiance forecasting. They often aggregate errors without distinguishing between over- and under-prediction, or identifying specific error patterns critical for grid operators, such as ramp events, persistent biases, or errors during peak demand periods. This oversight hinders targeted model improvements and robust risk assessment. This paper introduces the Novel, Interoperable, Comprehensive, and k-dimensional Error (NICE^k) metrics, a novel framework designed to provide a granular and context-aware assessment of deterministic solar forecasts. NICE^k disaggregates forecast errors across various operationally relevant dimensions (k), including temporal scales, magnitude of deviation, and directional biases. By integrating these distinct error components into a unified framework, NICE^k offers a more nuanced understanding of forecast performance, allowing for targeted model improvements and enhanced decision-making for grid management. We define the theoretical underpinnings of NICE^k and empirically validate its utility using diverse solar forecasting models and real-world irradiance data across different climatic regions. Results demonstrate that NICE^k provides insights unattainable by conventional metrics, revealing specific strengths and weaknesses of forecasting algorithms and enabling more informed renewable energy integration strategies.

However, standard error metrics such as Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Skill Scores (SS) fail to capture the multidimensional nature of solar irradiance forecasting.

title: Individualized PATE: Differentially Private Machine Learning with Individual Privacy Guarantees
text_ai: Applying machine learning (ML) to sensitive domains requires privacy protection of the underlying training data through formal privacy frameworks, such as differential privacy (DP). Yet, usually, the privacy of the training data comes at the cost of the resulting ML models' utility. The uniform global privacy typically offered by DP often results in an overly conservative privacy-utility trade-off, neglecting individual data sensitivities. To address this, we introduce *Individualized PATE*, a novel framework extending the Private Aggregation of Teacher Ensembles (PATE) to provide tailored, individual-level differential privacy guarantees. Unlike traditional DP, Individualized PATE allows flexible allocation of privacy budgets, protecting each participant's privacy based on their contribution and sensitivity. By dynamically adjusting privacy noise per individual, our method significantly reduces utility loss while upholding strong privacy. We formally define this individualized privacy notion and demonstrate through extensive empirical evaluations that Individualized PATE achieves superior model accuracy compared to standard DP-PATE, rigorously assuring quantifiable privacy. This approach paves the way for more efficient and equitable privacy-preserving ML in sensitive real-world applications.
prefix: Applying machine learning (ML) to sensitive domains requires privacy protection of the underlying training data through formal privacy frameworks, such as differential privacy (DP). Yet, usually, the privacy of the training data comes at the cost of the resulting ML models' utility.

title: What Makes for Good Views for Contrastive Learning?
text_ai: Contrastive learning between multiple views of the data has recently achieved state of the art performance in the field of self-supervised representation learning. Despite its success, the influence of different view choices has been less studied. This paper addresses this gap by systematically investigating the characteristics of effective data augmentations for view generation in contrastive learning. We introduce a quantitative framework to analyze the information content and diversity of views, empirically evaluating their impact on representation quality across various datasets and architectures. Our analysis reveals that effective views achieve a delicate balance: preserving sufficient semantic information while introducing enough perturbation to prevent trivial solutions. Transformations maintaining critical features but varying superficial details lead to superior representations; conversely, overly aggressive or trivial augmentations hinder effective learning. These insights offer practical guidelines for designing view generation strategies, paving the way for more robust and efficient self-supervised learning paradigms.

title: Immediate primary skin closure in type-III A and B open fractures: results after a minimum of five years
text_ai: Between June 1999 and May 2003 we undertook direct primary closure of the skin wounds of 173 patients with Gustilo and Anderson grade-IIIA and grade-IIIB open fractures. These patients were selected from a consecutive group of 557 with type-III injuries presenting during this time. All selected patients underwent urgent surgical debridement within six hours of injury, followed by stable fracture fixation, predominantly with external fixators. Primary skin closure was performed without tension. Patients were followed prospectively for a minimum of five years (range 5-10 years) to assess long-term outcomes. The primary endpoints included the incidence of deep infection, rate of fracture union, and the need for subsequent reconstructive surgery or amputation. We observed a deep infection rate of 8.1% (14 patients) and a non-union rate of 12.7% (22 patients). Secondary procedures, including flap coverage or bone grafting, were required in 28 patients (16.2%), while 3 patients (1.7%) ultimately underwent amputation. Functional outcomes, assessed by the Majeed score at the final follow-up, demonstrated good to excellent results in 78% of patients. Our findings suggest that immediate primary skin closure in Gustilo-Anderson grade-IIIA and IIIB open fractures, when combined with aggressive debridement and stable fixation, can achieve acceptable long-term infection and union rates, potentially reducing the need for staged procedures and improving functional recovery.

title: Block-MDS QC-LDPC Codes for Information Reconciliation in Key Distribution
text_ai: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a popular protocol that provides information theoretically secure keys to multiple parties. Two important post-processing steps of QKD are 1) the information reconciliation (IR) step, where parties reconcile mismatches in generated keys through classical communication, and 2) the privacy amplification (PA) step, where parties distill their common key into a new secure key that the adversary has little to no information about. The efficiency and security of the IR step are paramount for practical QKD systems, as any leaked information to an eavesdropper compromises the final key's security, while high reconciliation efficiency minimizes the length of the raw key needed. This paper proposes the use of novel Block-MDS Quasi-Cyclic Low-Density Parity-Check (QC-LDPC) codes for the IR phase. Leveraging their excellent error-correction capabilities, high code rates, and efficient quasi-cyclic structure, these codes are shown to achieve superior reconciliation efficiency and extremely low error floors. We demonstrate that Block-MDS QC-LDPC codes significantly enhance the overall performance of QKD post-processing, providing a robust and practical solution for secure key establishment.

title: Inflexibility and independence: Phase transitions in the majority-rule model
text_ai: In this work we study opinion formation in a population participating of a public debate with two distinct choices. We considered three distinct mechanisms of social interactions and individuals' behavior: conformity, nonconformity and inflexibility. The conformity is ruled by the majority-rule dynamics, whereas the nonconformity is introduced in the population as an independent behavior, implying the failure to attempted group influence. Inflexibility is modeled by agents holding a fixed opinion, immune to social influence. Integrating these three behaviors into the majority-rule framework, we explore collective opinion dynamics. Our results unveil a rich phase diagram with multiple phase transitions. We identify critical thresholds in the fractions of nonconformist and inflexible agents, leading to states of complete consensus, persistent polarization, or fragmented coexistence. These findings underscore the crucial role of individual traits in shaping collective opinion dynamics, demonstrating how the interplay of independence and rigidity drives abrupt shifts in consensus.

We considered three distinct mechanisms of social interactions and individuals' behavior: conformity, nonconformity and inflexibility. The conformity is ruled by the majority-rule dynamics, whereas the nonconformity is introduced in the population as an independent behavior, implying the failure to attempted group influence.

title: Competitive Collaboration: Joint Unsupervised Learning of Depth, Camera Motion, Optical Flow and Motion Segmentation
text_ai: We address the unsupervised learning of several interconnected problems in low-level vision: single view depth prediction, camera motion estimation, optical flow, and segmentation of a video into the static scene and moving regions. Our key insight is that these four fundamental vision problems are coupled through geometric constraints. Specifically, optical flow decomposes into a rigid scene flow (derived from depth and camera ego-motion) and an object motion component. The segmentation task identifies regions where this rigid scene flow model applies versus where independent object motion dominates. Leveraging this inherent coupling, we propose a novel end-to-end framework where dedicated neural networks for each task are trained jointly under a 'competitive collaboration' paradigm. Each network strives to optimally explain its part of the observed image changes, while providing constraints and guidance to the others. This is achieved through unified photometric and geometric consistency losses, operating entirely without ground truth supervision. Our approach effectively disentangles complex motion, resolving ambiguities inherent in monocular vision, leading to more robust and accurate predictions across all four tasks. Experimental results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across multiple datasets, highlighting the superior consistency and generalization of our jointly optimized model.

Our key insight is that these four fundamental vision problems are coupled through geometric constraints.

title: Structure Modeling Activation Free Fourier Network for Spacecraft Image Denoising
text_ai: Spacecraft image denoising is a crucial fundamental technology closely related to aerospace research. However, the existing deep learning-based image denoising methods are primarily designed for natural image and fail to adequately consider the characteristics of spacecraft image(e.g. low-light conditions, repetitive periodic structures), resulting in suboptimal performance in the spacecraft image denoising task. To address these limitations, we propose the Structure Modeling Activation Free Fourier Network (SMAFFN), tailored for spacecraft image denoising. SMAFFN leverages an activation-free Fourier network to efficiently mitigate repetitive periodic noise via frequency-domain processing. A novel structure modeling module concurrently learns intricate spacecraft characteristics, preserving detail integrity in low-light. This design robustly distinguishes noise from genuine structure. Experiments on a challenging spacecraft image dataset demonstrate SMAFFN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior perceptual and quantitative metrics for high-fidelity aerospace imaging.

However, the existing deep learning-based image denoising methods are primarily designed for natural image and fail to adequately consider the characteristics of spacecraft image(e.g. low-light conditions, repetitive periodic structures), resulting in suboptimal performance in the spacecraft image denoising task.

title: Single-domain chemical, thermochemical and thermal remanences in a basaltic rock
text_ai: Tiny basaltic samples containing finely grained titanomagnetite with Curie temperature less than 100 C were heated in air in weak field (25 to 100microT) at temperatures between 400 and 560 C for times as long as 32 hours. Microstructural and magnetic analyses confirmed significant oxidation of the primary titanomagnetite, resulting in the formation of more titanium-poor phases with significantly elevated Curie temperatures (up to 580 C). The samples acquired strong, stable remanent magnetizations during these treatments. By carefully controlling the heating and cooling protocols, we successfully isolated and characterized distinct magnetic components. A chemical remanent magnetization (CRM) was observed to develop when new magnetic phases formed below their blocking temperatures during isothermal heating. A thermochemical remanent magnetization (TCRM) was acquired when chemical alteration occurred at temperatures between the original and newly formed Curie points, followed by cooling in the applied field. Finally, a thermal remanent magnetization (TRM) was induced during cooling from temperatures exceeding the Curie point of the newly formed phases. These experiments demonstrate the complex interplay between thermal and chemical processes in acquiring remanence in single-domain grains. The results highlight the potential for multiple remanence components to coexist in altered basaltic rocks, emphasizing the importance of detailed rock magnetic analyses for accurate paleomagnetic interpretations.

title: 4G 5G Cell-level Multi-indicator Forecasting based on Dense-MLP
text_ai: With the development of 4G/5G, the rapid growth of traffic has caused a large number of cell indicators to exceed the warning threshold, and network quality has deteriorated. It is necessary for operators to solve the congestion in advance and effectively to guarantee the quality of user experience. To address this, accurate and timely forecasting of cell-level multi-indicators is crucial. Existing methods often fail to capture the complex, non-linear, and inter-dependent dynamics of cellular network data effectively. This paper proposes a novel Dense Multi-Layer Perceptron (Dense-MLP) model, specifically designed for 4G/5G cell-level multi-indicator forecasting. The Dense-MLP architecture adeptly learns intricate relationships among diverse performance metrics, such as traffic volume, resource utilization, and quality-of-service parameters. Through extensive evaluation with real-world operational data, our model demonstrates superior accuracy and robustness over traditional time-series and other machine learning approaches. This enables operators to proactively anticipate network degradation, optimize resource allocation, and prevent service disruptions, thereby significantly improving overall network quality.

It is necessary for operators to solve the congestion in advance and effectively to guarantee the quality of user experience.

title: Robust Contact State Estimation in Humanoid Walking Gaits
text_ai: In this article, we propose a deep learning framework that provides a unified approach to the problem of leg contact detection in humanoid robot walking gaits. Our formulation accomplishes to accurately and robustly estimate the contact state probability for each leg (i.e., stable or slip/no contact). Leveraging proprioceptive sensor data (kinematics, IMU, foot forces), the framework employs a recurrent neural network. This design effectively captures spatio-temporal dependencies in dynamic walking, crucial for contact mechanics. Trained on diverse datasets from various terrains and gait perturbations, it shows exceptional generalization. Experimental validation on a physical humanoid confirms superior accuracy, robustness to noise, and adaptability to unforeseen contact conditions, outperforming traditional methods. Its real-time capability enables seamless integration into reactive control loops, significantly enhancing humanoid locomotion stability and reliability on challenging surfaces.

title: Thinking Assistants: LLM-Based Conversational Assistants that Help Users Think By Asking rather than Answering
text_ai: Many AI systems focus solely on providing solutions or explaining outcomes. However, complex tasks like research and strategic thinking often benefit from a more comprehensive approach to augmenting the thinking process rather than passively getting information. This paper introduces 'Thinking Assistants,' a novel class of LLM-based conversational AI designed to facilitate deeper cognitive engagement through strategic questioning rather than direct answers. Unlike traditional systems acting as knowledge repositories, Thinking Assistants leverage LLMs to generate probing questions, challenge assumptions, and guide users through structured thought processes. This encourages users to articulate reasoning, explore diverse perspectives, identify blind spots, and arrive at more robust, nuanced conclusions independently. By shifting the interaction paradigm from passive information consumption to active cognitive partnership, these assistants significantly enhance critical thinking, creativity, and strategic decision-making. We present the design principles, architectural framework, and initial empirical evaluations of a prototype Thinking Assistant across complex problem-solving scenarios. Our findings demonstrate that users engaging with Thinking Assistants exhibit improved ideation, more structured inquiry, and greater confidence in their solutions, suggesting a promising direction for human-AI collaboration prioritizing cognitive augmentation over information delivery.

title: Harnessing TH9 cells in cancer immunotherapy.
text_ai: CD4 T cell effector subsets not only profoundly affect cancer progression, but recent evidence also underscores their critical contribution to the anticancer efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors. In 2012, the two seminal studies suggested the superior antimelanoma activity of T H 9 cells over other T cell subsets upon adoptive T cell transfer. Characterized by their production of interleukin-9 (IL-9) and, to a lesser extent, IL-10, TH9 cells orchestrate potent anti-tumor responses. IL-9 not only promotes mast cell activation and direct tumor cell killing, but also enhances the cytotoxic functions of CD8+ T cells and NK cells within the tumor microenvironment. This robust immunological profile positions TH9 cells as a compelling target for therapeutic exploitation. This paper critically reviews TH9 cell biology, their differentiation pathways, and their multifaceted roles in anti-tumor immunity. We discuss strategies for *ex vivo* generation and expansion of highly functional TH9 cells for adoptive cell therapy, alongside *in vivo* approaches to modulate the tumor microenvironment to favor their differentiation and persistence. Furthermore, we explore their synergistic potential with immune checkpoint blockade and other established immunotherapies, outlining key challenges and future directions for clinical translation.
