title: Accuracy of model-based tracking of knee kinematics and cartilage contact measured by dynamic volumetric MRI
text_ai: The purpose of this study was to determine the accuracy of knee kinematics and cartilage contact measured by volumetric dynamic MRI. A motor-actuated phantom drove femoral and tibial bone segments through cyclic 3D motion patterns. Volumetric images were continuously acquired using a 3D radially undersampled cine spoiled gradient echo sequence (SPGR-VIPR). Model-based 3D image registration tracked 6-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) kinematics from the dynamic images, from which cartilage contact areas and minimum distances were computed. Optical tracking provided ground truth kinematics for accuracy assessment. Results showed high accuracy for 6-DOF kinematics, with mean root mean square errors (RMSE) typically below 0.5 degrees for rotations and 0.2 mm for translations. Cartilage contact area and minimum distance measurements also demonstrated strong agreement with known phantom geometry, exhibiting average differences less than 5% and 0.1 mm, respectively, across various motion patterns. This study confirms that dynamic volumetric MRI with model-based tracking accurately quantifies knee kinematics and cartilage contact. This non-invasive tool holds significant potential for detailed in vivo analysis of joint function and mechanobiology, furthering understanding of joint loading in health and disease, and evaluating therapies.

title: Window-based Model Averaging Improves Generalization in Heterogeneous Federated Learning
text_ai: Federated Learning (FL) aims to learn a global model from distributed users while protecting their privacy. However, when data are distributed heterogeneously the learning process becomes noisy, unstable, and biased towards the last seen clients' data, slowing down convergence. To address these issues and improve the robustness and generalization capabilities of the global model, we propose WIMA (Window-based Model Averaging). WIMA maintains a moving window of recent global models and aggregates them to form the updated global model. This approach effectively smooths the update process, reducing the impact of client drift and the recency bias inherent in standard FL aggregation. By incorporating information from a broader history of model states, WIMA enhances the stability of training and promotes the development of a more generalized global representation. Experimental results on diverse heterogeneous datasets demonstrate that WIMA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art FL algorithms in terms of convergence speed, model accuracy, and generalization capability, particularly under severe data non-IID conditions.

However, when data are distributed heterogeneously the learning process becomes noisy, unstable, and biased towards the last seen clients' data, slowing down convergence. To address these issues and improve the robustness and generalization capabilities of the global model, we propose WIMA (Window-based Model Averaging).

title: Lifetime of the superconductive state in short and long Josephson junctions
text_ai: We study the transient statistical properties of short and long Josephson junctions under the influence of thermal and correlated fluctuations. In particular, we investigate the lifetime of the superconductive metastable state finding the presence of noise induced phenomena. Specifically, we employ analytical approaches based on the Fokker-Planck equation for short junctions, and extensive numerical simulations of the resistively and capacitively shunted junction (RCSJ) model for both short and long junctions. Our analysis reveals that correlated fluctuations can lead to counter-intuitive effects, such as noise-enhanced stability, where an optimal noise intensity maximizes the mean escape time from the zero-voltage state. For long junctions, the interplay between spatial degrees of freedom and noise characteristics introduces further complexities, influencing phase slip propagation and overall stability. The spatial and temporal correlation properties of the noise are shown to critically determine the escape mechanisms and the longevity of the supercurrent. These results offer fundamental insights into the robustness of superconducting states, vital for the design and performance optimization of superconducting quantum devices and sensors operating in noisy environments.

title: Symplectic structure of post-Newtonian Hamiltonian for spinning compact binaries
text_ai: The phase space of a Hamiltonian system is symplectic. However, the post-Newtonian Hamiltonian formulation of spinning compact binaries in existing publications does not have this property, when position, momentum and spin variables $[X, P, S_1, S_2]$ compose its phase space. This fundamental inconsistency arises from the non-canonical nature of the spin vector components within the standard Poisson bracket structure, hindering a truly canonical description of the system's evolution. To address this, we propose a novel approach that reconstructs the phase space to explicitly exhibit a symplectic form. Our method involves identifying appropriate canonical variables for the spin degrees of freedom, transforming each spin vector $S_i$ into a canonically conjugate pair $(q_{S_i}, p_{S_i})$ that respects the underlying SU(2) symmetry of spin. By integrating these new spin variables with the orbital canonical variables, we construct an extended phase space where the entire system possesses a well-defined symplectic structure. We then derive the post-Newtonian Hamiltonian for spinning compact binaries, explicitly expressed in these new canonical coordinates, up to the leading orders relevant for gravitational wave generation. This consistent Hamiltonian framework not only rectifies the theoretical shortcomings of previous formulations but also guarantees the preservation of phase space volume and allows for straightforward application of canonical perturbation theory. This symplectic Hamiltonian is crucial for developing robust numerical integrators and enhancing the accuracy of analytical predictions for inspiralling compact binaries, vital for gravitational wave astronomy.

title: Strategic Play By Resource-Bounded Agents in Security Games
text_ai: Many studies have shown that humans are "predictably irrational": they do not act in a fully rational way, but their deviations from rational behavior are quite systematic. Our goal is to see the extent to which we can explain and justify these deviations as the outcome of rational but resource-bounded agents doing as well as they can, given their limitations. We explore this hypothesis within security games, a domain characterized by high stakes, asymmetric information, and significant computational complexity, where fully rational play demands extensive resources rarely available to human or artificial agents. We develop novel computational models of agents operating under specific resource constraints: limited lookahead, bounded memory, or simplified strategy spaces. We demonstrate how these limitations lead to systematic deviations from classical game-theoretic predictions, mirroring observed human behaviors in security games. Crucially, we show these 'irrational' strategies are optimal adaptations, representing the best performance achievable given an agent's cognitive or computational budget. Our analysis offers a principled framework for understanding and predicting strategic behavior in complex, real-world settings where perfect rationality is infeasible, offering insights for human-AI teaming and security system design.

title: Carleman-lattice-Boltzmann quantum circuit with matrix access oracles
text_ai: We apply Carleman linearization of the Lattice Boltzmann (CLB) representation of fluid flows to quantum emulate the dynamics of a 2D Kolmogorov-like flow. We assess the accuracy of the result and find a relative error of the order of $10^{-3}$ with just two Carleman iterates, for a range of the Reynolds number up to a few hundreds. This linearized system, represented by a high-dimensional sparse matrix, is then mapped onto a quantum circuit. We detail the construction of the quantum circuit architecture, leveraging matrix access oracles for efficient state preparation and Hamiltonian simulation of the Carleman dynamics. The quantum algorithm employs a variant of the quantum linear system algorithm (QLSA) to evolve the Carleman state vector. We analyze the quantum resource requirements, including qubit count and gate depth, demonstrating that the approach scales polynomially with the system size and Carleman iteration order. This work establishes a novel pathway for quantum simulation of complex fluid dynamics, offering potential for significant speedups over classical methods for higher Reynolds numbers and larger computational domains.

We assess the accuracy of the result and find a relative error of the order of $10^{-3}$ with just two Carleman iterates, for a range of the Reynolds number up to a few hundreds.

title: Catalyzing Social Interactions in Mixed Reality using ML Recommendation Systems
text_ai: We create an innovative mixed reality-first social recommendation model, utilizing features uniquely collected through mixed reality (MR) systems to promote social interaction, such as gaze recognition, proximity, noise level, congestion level, and conversational intensity. We further extend these models to include right-time features to deliver timely notifications. Utilizing a multi-modal deep learning architecture, our system dynamically analyzes these cues to infer user availability, interest, and social engagement potential. It then identifies optimal interaction opportunities, recommending compatible individuals or groups based on shared interests or proximity. Recommendations are delivered non-intrusively via subtle, context-aware MR cues, augmenting user experience. We validate our model through a user study in a custom-built MR social space, demonstrating a statistically significant increase in the frequency and quality of user-initiated social interactions compared to conventional environments. Participants reported enhanced presence and spontaneous connection. This work offers a novel framework for socially intelligent MR systems, fostering more organic and enriching human interactions.

title: Effect of 5% transdermal lidocaine patches on postoperative analgesia in dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy.
text_ai: To investigate the effect of 5% lidocaine patches on postoperative analgesia in dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy. Client-owned dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy for a single acute intervertebral thoracolumbar disc extrusion were enrolled in this prospective, randomised, blinded clinical trial. Following methadone administration, anaesthesia was induced with propofol, and maintained with isoflurane in oxygen and fentanyl infusion, in both groups. Dogs were randomly assigned to receive either 5% lidocaine patches (LIDO group) or identical placebo patches (CONTROL group), applied to the surgical site immediately following skin closure. Patches remained in situ for 72 hours. Postoperative pain was assessed using the short-form Glasgow Composite Measure Pain Scale (CMPS-SF) and a visual analogue scale (VAS) at 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48, and 72 hours post-extubation. Rescue analgesia was administered if CMPS-SF scores exceeded a predefined threshold. Sedation scores and adverse events were also monitored. Statistical analysis involved repeated measures ANOVA and chi-square tests. The LIDO group demonstrated significantly lower mean CMPS-SF scores from 4 to 24 hours post-extubation (P<0.05) and a reduced requirement for rescue analgesia compared to the CONTROL group (P<0.01). No significant adverse effects were observed. These findings indicate that 5% transdermal lidocaine patches provide effective and safe adjunctive postoperative analgesia in dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy, reducing pain and the need for additional systemic analgesics.

Following methadone administration, anaesthesia was induced with propofol, and maintained with isoflurane in oxygen and fentanyl infusion, in both groups.

title: Optimized Treatment Schedules for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia
text_ai: Over the past decade, several targeted therapies (e.g. imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib) have been developed to treat Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML). Despite an initial response to therapy, drug resistance remains a problem for some CML patients. This resistance often stems from acquired *BCR-ABL1* kinase domain mutations, causing treatment failure. Current fixed-dose, continuous protocols can select for resistant clones, limiting efficacy. This study developed and evaluated optimized, adaptive CML treatment schedules. Using a multi-scale computational model integrating TKI pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics with CML cell dynamics and mutation kinetics, we simulated intermittent and adaptive dosing under diverse patient parameters. Simulations demonstrate individualized, adaptive schedules, adjusted by disease burden and predicted resistance, significantly improve long-term outcomes. Strategically implemented intermittent dosing reduced selective pressure, and model-guided dose escalation or combination therapy at early relapse proved superior to reactive interventions. These findings advocate personalized, model-informed CML management. Optimized schedules can overcome drug resistance, enhance response, and improve prognosis, leading to more sustainable strategies.

title: Skew Class-balanced Re-weighting for Unbiased Scene Graph Generation
text_ai: An unbiased scene graph generation (SGG) algorithm referred to as Skew Class-balanced Re-weighting (SCR) is proposed for considering the unbiased predicate prediction caused by the long-tailed distribution. The prior works focus mainly on alleviating the deteriorating performances of the minority predicate predictions, showing drastic dropping recall scores, i.e., losing the majority predicate performances. To overcome this critical trade-off, SCR proposes a novel loss re-weighting strategy that adaptively balances the learning signal from both rare and frequent predicates. It employs a dynamic skew factor adjusting class weights based on frequency and prediction confidence, thereby preventing over-correction for minority classes while ensuring adequate representation. This unique approach effectively mitigates the long-tailed predicate distribution without compromising recall on majority classes. Extensive experiments on Visual Genome demonstrate SCR achieves superior and balanced predicate prediction, boosting minority recall while maintaining high majority performance, setting new state-of-the-art for unbiased SGG.

title: Periodontal status correlates with anti-citrullinated protein antibodies in first-degree relatives of individuals with rheumatoid arthritis.
text_ai: To evaluate periodontal status in first-degree relatives of patients with rheumatoid arthritis (FDR-RA) and detect correlation with the presence of anti-citrullinated protein antibodies (ACPAs). Rheumatologic status and periodontal status were evaluated in a nested case-control study of FDR-RA with no diagnosis of RA at enrolment. Comprehensive periodontal examination assessed clinical attachment loss (CAL), probing depth (PD), bleeding on probing (BOP), and plaque index (PI). Periodontitis was classified by established criteria. Serum samples quantified anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (CCP) antibodies (anti-CCP2) via ELISA. Statistical analyses determined correlations. A substantial prevalence of periodontitis, often moderate to severe, was observed in the FDR-RA cohort, with ACPA positivity detected in a significant subset. A statistically significant positive correlation was identified between periodontitis severity (higher mean CAL and PD) and both anti-CCP2 presence and titers (p<0.05). Individuals with severe periodontitis demonstrated a significantly higher odds ratio for ACPA positivity. These findings suggest periodontal inflammation plays a crucial role in ACPA generation or amplification in genetically susceptible individuals, potentially contributing to preclinical RA. Early identification and targeted management of periodontitis in FDR-RA could mitigate systemic autoimmunity and reduce RA risk.

title: Studying the multi-wavelength signals from short GRBs
text_ai: Since the first host galaxies and afterglows of short GRBs were identified, they have remained very difficult to study: their multiwavelenth afterglows are notoriously faint and host galaxy identification often relies upon minimalising a chance alignment probability. Despite these observational hurdles, multi-wavelength studies are paramount for unraveling the nature of their progenitor systems, emission mechanisms, and host environments. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of a diverse sample of short GRBs observed across X-ray, optical, and radio wavelengths. We detail advanced techniques for robust afterglow detection and host galaxy association, mitigating the challenges of faint signals and crowded fields. Our findings reveal novel correlations between afterglow properties, such as spectral evolution and luminosity, and the characteristics of their host galaxies, including star formation rates and stellar masses. These results provide crucial insights into the astrophysical origins of short GRBs, strongly supporting compact binary merger scenarios and offering new constraints for gravitational wave counterparts. The work underscores the imperative of rapid, deep multi-wavelength follow-up for advancing our understanding of these extreme cosmic events.

title: First Light Curve Analysis of NSVS 8294044, V1023 Her, and V1397 Her Contact Binary Systems
text_ai: The first photometric light curve investigation of the NSVS 8294044, V1023 Her, and V1397 Her binary systems is presented. We used ground-based observations for the NSVS 8294044 system and Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) data for V1023 Her and V1397 Her. The collected light curves were analyzed using the 2003 version of the Wilson-Devinney (WD) code to derive the photometric solutions and fundamental parameters. All three systems were confirmed as W UMa-type contact binaries. For NSVS 8294044, a mass ratio of q = 0.38(2), an inclination of i = 78.5(3) degrees, and a fill-factor of f = 0.45(2) were determined, alongside evidence of a cool spot on the primary. V1023 Her was found to have q = 0.42(1), i = 82.1(4) degrees, and f = 0.31(2), exhibiting a shallow contact configuration. V1397 Her, displaying a deeper contact, yielded q = 0.29(1), i = 75.8(3) degrees, and f = 0.58(2). Orbital period refinements were also performed for all systems, demonstrating slight period variations. These first comprehensive photometric analyses provide crucial insights into the physical properties and evolutionary states of these previously uncharacterized contact binaries, contributing to a better understanding of their formation and evolution mechanisms.

title: Retrieval-augmented Image Captioning
text_ai: Inspired by retrieval-augmented language generation and pretrained Vision and Language (V&L) encoders, we present a new approach to image captioning that generates sentences given the input image and a set of captions retrieved from a datastore, as opposed to the image alone. Our framework, dubbed R-CAP, employs a novel multi-modal transformer decoder that effectively fuses visual features from the input image with rich textual context from retrieved captions. These captions, sourced via a V&L encoder, serve as explicit knowledge, guiding generation for more accurate, detailed, and diverse descriptions, mitigating factual inconsistencies and generic outputs. Extensive experiments on MS-COCO show R-CAP significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models across standard metrics (e.g., CIDEr, SPICE). We demonstrate that explicitly leveraging retrieved information yields captions with superior factual accuracy and linguistic diversity, setting a new benchmark.

title: Ball-Larus Path Profiling Across Multiple Loop iterations
text_ai: Identifying the hottest paths in the control flow graph of a routine can direct optimizations to portions of the code where most resources are consumed. This powerful methodology, called path profiling, was introduced by Ball and Larus in the mid 90s and has received considerable attention in the last 15 years for its practical relevance. However, traditional Ball-Larus methods often reset path context at loop boundaries, obscuring critical inter-iteration patterns. This prevents accurate identification of 'hot' paths spanning multiple loop iterations, crucial for complex, loop-dominated routines. To address this, this paper introduces a novel Ball-Larus algorithm extension. Our approach employs a refined path numbering and instrumentation strategy that maintains context across loop back-edges, directly encoding inter-iteration dependencies. This enables a more granular understanding of execution within iterative constructs. We demonstrate this enhanced profiling uncovers 'hotter' paths missed by conventional techniques, leading to precise optimization for loop-intensive applications. Experimental evaluation confirms our technique yields significantly more accurate path frequency distributions with manageable overhead, offering a valuable tool for fine-grained analysis.

title: Optoelectronic Fingerprints of Interference between Different Charge Carriers in Graphene Superlattices and Analogies to Twisted Graphene Bilayers
text_ai: Motivated by recent experimental findings on the low-energy spectrum of Kekul\'e-patterned graphene, the optoelectronic signatures of graphene superlattices with a spatial modulation that triples the size of the unit cell and folds the valleys to the center of the Brillouin zone are studied. We theoretically investigate the optical conductivity and absorption spectra, revealing distinct features that arise from the intricate interference between charge carriers originating from the folded Dirac cones. This interference manifests as novel absorption peaks and enhanced inter-valley transitions, providing a direct spectroscopic fingerprint of the superlattice potential and its impact on carrier dynamics. Crucially, we identify a striking analogy between these interference effects and those observed in twisted graphene bilayers, particularly concerning the emergence of flat bands and correlated electronic states. Our findings suggest that such tailored graphene superlattices offer a tunable platform to engineer and probe complex charge carrier interactions, paving the way for novel optoelectronic devices and fundamental explorations of moiré physics in single-layer systems.

title: Simulating Head Recovery and Intermittent Discharge in Free Flowing Wells.
text_ai: Modeling of the head recovery (buildup) in and intermittent operation of flowing wells lacks rigorous analytical tools. Presently different methods are applied in discharging and recovery phases. The presented reliable approximate solution considers a continuous free flow process and time variant screen loss parameters. This approach unifies the transient behavior during both discharge and subsequent recovery periods, treating them as integral parts of a single well operation cycle. By incorporating dynamic changes in wellbore storage and skin factor, alongside the time-dependent head loss across the well screen, the model accurately captures the complex fluid dynamics within the well. This comprehensive formulation eliminates the need for separate models for each phase, offering a more consistent and computationally efficient method for predicting well performance. The simulated results provide valuable insights into optimal intermittent pumping strategies, well efficiency degradation, and overall resource management in free-flowing systems.

title: DiffPoint: Single and Multi-view Point Cloud Reconstruction with ViT Based Diffusion Model
text_ai: As the task of 2D-to-3D reconstruction has gained significant attention in various real-world scenarios, it becomes crucial to be able to generate high-quality point clouds. Despite the recent success of deep learning models in generating point clouds, there are still challenges in producing high-fidelity results due to the disparities between images and point clouds. Existing methods often fall short in capturing intricate geometric details and ensuring structural consistency, especially from sparse or complex inputs. This limitation arises from their difficulty in effectively bridging the inherent semantic gap between 2D images and 3D point clouds. To address these challenges, we introduce DiffPoint, a novel framework for high-fidelity single and multi-view point cloud reconstruction. DiffPoint leverages a Vision Transformer (ViT)-based diffusion model, which learns to iteratively refine a noisy point cloud representation into a high-quality 3D structure. Our architecture integrates a powerful image encoder with the ViT-diffusion backbone, enabling robust feature extraction and global context understanding crucial for comprehensive reconstruction. This design allows DiffPoint to generate dense, accurate, and geometrically consistent point clouds from both single and multiple input views. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that DiffPoint significantly surpasses existing state-of-the-art approaches in terms of reconstruction quality, completeness, and fidelity, setting a new benchmark for 2D-to-3D point cloud generation.

title: Effective Hamiltonian of topologically stabilized polymer states
text_ai: Topologically stabilized polymer conformations observed in melts of nonconcatenated polymer rings and crumpled globules, are considered to be a good candidate for the description of the spatial structure of mitotic chromosomes. Despite significant efforts, the microscopic Hamiltonian capable of describing such systems, remains yet inaccessible. This work addresses this challenge by presenting the derivation of an effective Hamiltonian designed to bridge this gap. Utilizing a coarse-graining approach rooted in statistical mechanics, we construct a phenomenological description that implicitly accounts for the severe topological constraints inherent in these systems, such as non-concatenation and knotting restrictions, without requiring explicit atomic-level detail. Our proposed Hamiltonian is formulated in terms of collective variables, effectively capturing the entropic penalties associated with maintaining topological integrity. We demonstrate that this effective framework successfully reproduces key experimentally observed features, including the characteristic scaling exponents of crumpled globules and the robust stability of their compact conformations. This tractable theoretical tool offers a powerful avenue for exploring the phase behavior, dynamics, and mechanical properties of topologically stabilized polymer assemblies, providing crucial insights into the fundamental principles governing the multiscale organization of biological structures like chromosomes.

title: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Thompson Sampling for Logistic Bandits
text_ai: We study the performance of the Thompson Sampling algorithm for logistic bandit problems. In this setting, an agent receives binary rewards with probabilities determined by a logistic function, $\exp(\beta \langle a, \theta \rangle)/(1+\exp(\beta \langle a, \theta \rangle))$, with slope parameter $\beta>0$, and where both the action $a\in \mathcal{A}$ and parameter $\theta \in \mathcal{O}$ lie within the $d$-dimensional unit ball. The non-linearity of the reward function poses significant challenges for theoretical analysis of Thompson Sampling's regret. We overcome this by developing a novel information-theoretic framework. Our analysis quantifies the information gain about the unknown parameter $\theta$, establishing a tight upper bound on the cumulative regret. Specifically, we prove that the expected regret is $\tilde{O}(d/\beta \log T)$, where $T$ is the time horizon. This result explicitly highlights the crucial role of the slope parameter $\beta$: a steeper logistic function (larger $\beta$) leads to significantly faster learning and lower regret, as distinguishing optimal actions becomes easier. We complement this with a matching $\Omega(d/\beta \log T)$ lower bound, demonstrating the minimax optimality of our upper bound up to logarithmic factors. These findings offer fundamental insights into the learnability of logistic bandit problems and the efficiency of Thompson Sampling in non-linear environments, elucidating the intrinsic connection between information acquisition and regret minimization.

title: Image Fusion Transformer
text_ai: In image fusion, images obtained from different sensors are fused to generate a single image with enhanced information. In recent years, state-of-the-art methods have adopted Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) to encode meaningful features for image fusion. Specifically, CNN-based methods perform image fusion by fusing local features. However, these approaches often struggle to capture comprehensive global contextual information and long-range dependencies, which are vital for generating truly information-rich fused outputs. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the **Image Fusion Transformer (IFT)**, a novel end-to-end deep learning architecture designed for robust multi-modal image fusion. The IFT leverages the powerful self-attention mechanism of Transformers to model intricate global relationships across input images, enabling the effective integration of both local details and broader contextual cues. Our architecture employs a multi-scale feature extraction backbone, followed by a series of cascaded Transformer blocks that dynamically fuse features by attending to relevant information across different modalities and spatial locations. This global attentional mechanism allows the IFT to synthesize a single, high-quality image that preserves critical details while enhancing overall information content and visual coherence. Extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our Image Fusion Transformer significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art CNN-based and traditional fusion methods, both quantitatively and qualitatively, in terms of detail preservation, artifact suppression, and perceptual quality.

title: Visual Analytics for Explainable and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
text_ai: Our society increasingly depends on intelligent systems to solve complex problems, ranging from recommender systems suggesting the next movie to watch to AI models assisting in medical diagnoses for hospitalized patients. With the iterative improvement of diagnostic accuracy and efficiency, AI holds significant potential to mitigate medical misdiagnoses by preventing numerous deaths and reducing an economic burden of approximately 450 EUR billion annually. However, the inherent opacity of many advanced AI models, particularly deep learning, presents significant challenges for their adoption in safety-critical domains like healthcare. Trust and accountability demand clinicians and patients understand a model's rationale for its diagnoses or recommendations. Without explainability, verifying fairness, identifying biases, or understanding limitations remains difficult, impeding responsible AI deployment. This paper advocates Visual Analytics as a crucial paradigm. By synergistically combining human perception and interactive reasoning, visual analytics transforms complex AI decision processes into intuitive, navigable representations. This empowers domain experts to scrutinize predictions, identify errors, explore features, and assess model robustness. Ultimately, visual analytics fosters explainable and trustworthy AI, enabling critical insights into model behavior, facilitating informed decision-making and ethical integration.

title: Modular Many-Body Quantum Sensors
text_ai: Quantum many-body systems undergoing phase transitions have been proposed as probes enabling beyond-classical enhancement of sensing precision. However, this enhancement is usually limited to a very narrow region around the critical point. Here, we systematically develop a modular approach for introducing multiple phase transitions in a many-body system. This strategy involves partitioning a larger system into interacting sub-modules, each engineered to host distinct critical points. By carefully tuning the inter-module coupling, we demonstrate the ability to cascade these transitions, effectively broadening the operational range over which quantum-enhanced sensitivity can be achieved. We show that this modularity not only extends the regime of high precision but also offers enhanced robustness against environmental noise and control imperfections, which typically plague single-critical-point sensors. Our theoretical framework outlines how such architectures can be implemented in various experimental platforms, including ultra-cold atomic lattices and superconducting circuits, paving the way for designing versatile, broadband quantum sensors capable of operating across a wide range of external parameters, thereby overcoming the inherent limitations of conventional critical point metrology.

title: An effective Thermodynamic Description of Galactic Haloes
text_ai: The observation of flat rotation curves in asymptotic region of galaxies implies that the dark matter density profile decreases exponentially with the gravitational potential in this region. It is curious that this behavior is identical to what one would have from a Boltzmann gas in thermal equilibrium. Formalizing this intriguing analogy, this paper develops an effective thermodynamic framework for galactic dark matter haloes. We propose that dark matter particles, despite their collisionless nature, achieve a quasi-equilibrium state over cosmological timescales. Within this framework, an effective temperature and chemical potential are introduced, demonstrating the natural emergence of flat rotation curves. Our model predicts relationships between halo structural properties like concentration and virial mass, which are tested against N-body simulations and observational data. This description offers a novel perspective on universal halo properties and formation, extending beyond collisionless dynamics.

title: CUNet: A Compact Unsupervised Network for Image Classification
text_ai: In this paper, we propose a compact network called CUNet (compact unsupervised network) to counter the image classification challenge. Different from the traditional convolutional neural networks learning filters by the time-consuming stochastic gradient descent, CUNet learns the filter bank from diverse image patches with the simple K-means, which significantly avoids the requirement of scarce labeled training images, reduces the training consumption, and maintains the high discriminative ability. These K-means learned filters form a fixed feature extractor, effectively bypassing backpropagation for feature learning. A lightweight, supervised classifier (e.g., linear SVM) is then trained on these extracted features for final image categorization. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets like CIFAR-10 and STL-10 demonstrate CUNet's competitive accuracy. It significantly outperforms traditional unsupervised methods and approaches the performance of some supervised deep learning models, all while requiring substantially less computational resources and labeled data. CUNet thus offers a practical and efficient solution for robust image classification.

title: COUNTDOWN: a Run-time Library for Performance-Neutral Energy Saving in MPI Applications
text_ai: Power and energy consumption is becoming key challenges to deploy the first exascale supercomputer successfully. Large-scale HPC applications waste a significant amount of power in communication and synchronization-related idle times. However, due to the time scale at which communication happens, transitioning in low power states during communication's idle times may introduce unacceptable overhead in applications' execution time. This inherent conflict between energy efficiency and performance poses a significant challenge for developers striving to optimize large-scale parallel applications. Current strategies often require manual tuning or introduce measurable performance penalties. To overcome this, we introduce **COUNTDOWN**, a novel run-time library specifically engineered to deliver performance-neutral energy savings in Message Passing Interface (MPI) applications. COUNTDOWN operates by transparently intercepting MPI calls to predict the duration of impending communication-induced idle times. Leveraging these predictions, it adaptively transitions processor cores into appropriate low-power states (e.g., deep C-states or DVFS) for optimal energy reduction, carefully avoiding states that would incur unacceptable wake-up latency. Its predictive engine ensures cores are reactivated precisely when computation resumes, minimizing performance degradation. Evaluated across a range of representative MPI benchmarks and real-world scientific applications, COUNTDOWN demonstrates substantial energy savings, averaging between 15% and 30%, with a measured execution time overhead of less than 0.5% in all tested scenarios. This makes COUNTDOWN a critical enabler for sustainable exascale computing.

title: Randomized Oversampling for Generalized Multiscale Finite Element Methods
text_ai: In this paper, we study the development of efficient multiscale methods for flows in heterogeneous media. Our approach uses the Generalized Multiscale Finite Element (GMsFEM) framework. The main idea of GMsFEM is to approximate the solution space locally using a few multiscale basis functions. These basis functions are typically constructed by solving local spectral problems on oversampled domains. However, optimal oversampling region selection poses a critical challenge for complex, high-contrast media, impacting accuracy and computational cost. To address this, we introduce a novel randomized oversampling strategy. Our approach employs probabilistic selection and aggregation of information from diverse local domains. This randomization effectively captures a broader spectrum of multiscale features, reducing the need for large predefined oversampling. Integrating probabilistically weighted local solutions significantly enhances global approximation robustness and accuracy for highly heterogeneous and non-separated scales, while maintaining computational efficiency. Numerical results demonstrate superior convergence and accuracy of our randomized oversampling GMsFEM compared to standard variants, particularly in challenging high-contrast scenarios, offering a more efficient and reliable multiscale solver.

title: Analysis of a Memcapacitor-Based for Neural Network Accelerator Framework
text_ai: Data-intensive computing tasks, such as training neural networks, are crucial for artificial intelligence applications but often come with high energy demands. One promising solution is to develop specialized hardware that directly maps neural networks, utilizing arrays of memristive devices to perform parallel multiply-accumulate operations. This paper specifically proposes and analyzes a novel neural network accelerator framework built upon memcapacitor crossbar arrays. Memcapacitors, as emerging two-terminal non-volatile memory devices, offer distinct advantages for in-memory computing due to their voltage-dependent capacitance, enabling analog storage of synaptic weights and highly efficient parallel vector-matrix multiplication. Our framework details the architectural design, including integrated peripheral circuitry for precise weight programming and read operations. We conduct a comprehensive analysis of its performance, evaluating key metrics such as energy efficiency, computational throughput, and potential accuracy implications arising from device non-idealities. The results demonstrate the memcapacitor-based accelerator's significant potential for accelerating deep learning workloads, offering a promising pathway towards ultra-low-power and high-performance artificial intelligence hardware.

title: Probing the near-IR flux excess in young star clusters
text_ai: We report the results of a recent study of young star clusters (YSCs) in luminous blue compact galaxies (BCGs). The age distributions of the YSCs suggest that the starburst episode in Haro 11, ESO 185-IG13, and Mrk 930 started not more than 30-40 Myr ago. Beyond their age distributions, our multi-wavelength photometric analysis reveals a significant near-infrared (NIR) flux excess in a substantial fraction of these YSCs, particularly at wavelengths > 2 µm, indicating obscured stages of cluster evolution. Through detailed spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting, incorporating stellar populations and dust emission models, we demonstrate that the majority of this NIR excess is best explained by optically thick dust shrouding deeply embedded, very young clusters (age < 5 Myr), rather than evolved massive stars. These embedded clusters provide compelling evidence for recent or ongoing star formation, pushing the lower age limit of the starburst activity within these BCGs. Their spatial distribution and luminosity offer crucial insights into the propagation and duty cycle of star formation, highlighting the rapid transition from deeply embedded to optically visible phases.

title: Stripe magnetic order and field-induced quantum criticality in the perfect triangular-lattice antiferromagnet CsCeSe$_2$
text_ai: The two-dimensional triangular-lattice antiferromagnet (TLAF) is a textbook example of frustrated magnetic systems. Despite its simplicity, the TLAF model exhibits a highly rich and complex magnetic phase diagram, featuring numerous distinct ground states that can be stabilized through frustrated next-nearest-neighbor couplings or anisotropy. In this paper, we report low-temperature magnetic properties of the TLAF material CsCeSe$_2$. This compound features Ce$^{3+}$ ions (S=1/2) arranged on an almost perfect triangular lattice, making it an excellent candidate for studying quantum frustration. Through comprehensive specific heat, AC/DC magnetic susceptibility, and neutron diffraction measurements, we establish its magnetic phase diagram. At zero magnetic field, CsCeSe$_2$ exhibits a transition into a long-range ordered state below T_N ≈ 0.4 K. Our neutron diffraction data unequivocally reveal this ground state to be a **stripe magnetic order**, with spins aligning along an in-plane easy axis. This stripe order is suppressed by an external magnetic field. When the field is applied along the in-plane direction, a quantum phase transition occurs at a critical field H_c ≈ 2.5 T. Signatures of **field-induced quantum criticality** are evident near H_c, including power-law scaling of specific heat and divergence of magnetic susceptibility. These results establish CsCeSe$_2$ as a prime experimental platform for exploring quantum phase transitions and the interplay of frustration, anisotropy, and quantum fluctuations in two-dimensional triangular-lattice antiferromagnets.

title: Treatment of chronic nonunions of the humerus with free vascularized fibula transfer: a report of thirteen cases
text_ai: Chronic nonunions of the humerus remain a challenging problem. We reviewed 13 cases of chronic nonunion of the humerus resulting from trauma or osteomyelitis treated with vascularized fibula transfer after failure of conventional treatment. Patient averages were 35 years of age, follow-up of 19 months, and 4.2 prior operations. Radiographic union was achieved in 11 of 13 cases (85%) at an average of 6.5 months. Functional outcomes, assessed using validated limb-specific scores, showed significant improvement in pain, range of motion, and limb function. Two cases failed to achieve union; one patient experienced a minor donor site complication. This series suggests free vascularized fibula transfer is a highly effective and biologically robust option for complex chronic humeral nonunions, especially with significant bone loss or infection, offering a high rate of successful union and functional recovery.

title: The Milky Way atlas for linear filaments II. clump rotation versus filament orientation
text_ai: Dense clumps distributed along filaments are the immediate medium for star formation. Kinematic properties of the clumps, such as velocity gradient and angular momentum, combined with filament orientation, provide important clues to the formation mechanism of filament-clump configurations and the role of filaments in star formation. Building upon the comprehensive Milky Way atlas of linear filaments, we investigate the relationship between the rotational kinematics of dense clumps and the orientation of their host filaments. Utilizing high-resolution molecular line observations, we systematically measure the velocity gradients of numerous clumps embedded within prominent filaments. These gradients are then used to infer the direction of the clump's angular momentum vector. Our analysis reveals a significant statistical preference for the rotation axes of these clumps to be either aligned or perpendicular to the long axis of their parent filament. Specifically, we find that a majority of observed clumps exhibit rotation axes preferentially aligned with the filament, suggesting that accretion flows along the filament contribute significantly to their angular momentum. Conversely, a notable subset displays perpendicular alignment, potentially indicating fragmentation or localized turbulent processes. These findings provide critical observational constraints on theoretical models of filamentary cloud evolution, fragmentation, and the subsequent angular momentum transfer during star formation, highlighting the complex interplay between large-scale filamentary structures and the initial conditions for stellar birth.

Kinematic properties of the clumps, such as velocity gradient and angular momentum, combined with filament orientation, provide important clues to the formation mechanism of filament-clump configurations and the role of filaments in star formation.

title: A New Hole Density as a Stability Measure for Boron Fullerenes
text_ai: We investigate the stability of boron fullerene sets B76, B78 and B82. We evaluate the ground state energies, nucleus-independent chemical shift (NICS), the binding energies per atom and the band gap values by means of first-principles methods. We propose a novel 'hole density' parameter, derived from the electron density distribution, as a superior stability descriptor for these complex nanostructures. This metric quantifies local electron deficiency, particularly at the centers of hexagonal or larger rings, characteristic features of boron fullerenes. Unlike traditional energetic or electronic indicators, the hole density provides a spatially resolved, intuitive measure of structural strain and potential reactivity. Our computational results demonstrate that this new hole density measure correlates strongly with the observed stability trends for B76, B78, and B82, often providing clearer differentiation between isomers than NICS or band gap values alone. It successfully identifies the most stable isomers, aligning with available experimental data. This easily calculable descriptor offers a robust and insightful tool for the design and characterization of novel boron nanostructures, complementing existing stability criteria.

title: Sparsification and Reconstruction from the Perspective of Representation Geometry
text_ai: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) have emerged as a predominant tool in mechanistic interpretability, aiming to identify interpretable monosemantic features. However, how does sparse encoding organize the representations of activation vector from language models? What is the relationship between this organizational paradigm and feature disentanglement as well as reconstruction performance? We address these questions by introducing a novel geometric framework to analyze the latent space of SAEs, specifically examining how sparse encoding shapes the angular and radial distribution of learned features within the activation space. Our findings reveal that sparse encoding intrinsically promotes a highly structured, often near-orthogonal, arrangement of features, quantifiable through metrics like cosine similarity. This emergent geometric structure is shown to be crucial for achieving both high-quality reconstruction and improved feature disentanglement, evidenced by stronger decorrelation of feature activations and reduced polysemanticity. We further demonstrate how varying sparsity penalties lead to distinct geometric configurations, illustrating trade-offs between reconstruction fidelity and interpretability. Our work provides a foundational geometric perspective on SAEs, offering new insights into their effectiveness for mechanistic interpretability and guiding future design principles.

title: A New Lagrangian Problem Crossover: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Crossover Standards
text_ai: The performance of most evolutionary metaheuristic algorithms relays on various operatives. One of them is the crossover operator, which is divided into two types: application dependent and application independent crossover operators. These standards always help to choose the best-fitted point in the evolutionary algorithm process. However, the effectiveness of these operators can vary significantly across diverse problem landscapes, particularly in complex constrained optimization where variable interdependencies are high. This paper introduces a novel paradigm, the Lagrangian Problem Crossover (LPC), which integrates Lagrangian relaxation principles into the recombination process to effectively navigate such intricate search spaces. To systematically evaluate the LPC's potential and its alignment with established practices, this study conducts a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis of crossover standards across various evolutionary algorithms. Our methodology involved synthesizing quantitative performance metrics from relevant empirical studies, focusing on solution quality, convergence rates, and computational efficiency. The findings provide a robust comparative framework, elucidating the strengths and weaknesses of current crossover approaches and highlighting how LPC offers a promising advancement by leveraging problem-specific structures for enhanced optimization.

title: A Function Approximation Approach to Estimation of Policy Gradient for POMDP with Structured Policies
text_ai: We consider the estimation of the policy gradient in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDP) with a special class of structured policies that are finite-state controllers. We show that the gradient estimation can be done in the Actor-Critic framework, by making the critic compute a "value" function that does not depend on the states of POMDP. Instead, the critic computes a "value" function defined over the internal states of the finite-state controller. This directly observable, reduced state space enables tractable function approximation. We derive a novel policy gradient estimator that leverages this state-independent value function, offering a computationally efficient approach for learning structured policies. Our method bypasses explicit belief state computation, effectively addressing the curse of dimensionality inherent in POMDPs. Theoretical analysis and empirical validation on challenging POMDP benchmarks demonstrate improved scalability and sample efficiency.

title: The everyday dynamics of rumination and worry: precipitant events and affective consequences.
text_ai: Rumination and worry are two perseverative, negatively valenced thought processes that characterise depressive and anxiety disorders. Despite significant research interest, little is known about the everyday precipitants and consequences of rumination and worry. Using an experience sampling methodology, we examined and compared rumination and worry with respect to their relations to daily events and affective experience. A community sample of 150 adults provided repeated daily reports over 14 days. This real-time approach allowed for fine-grained examination of their temporal dynamics. Results revealed that rumination was predominantly triggered by negative interpersonal events and failures, while worry was more closely linked to anticipated future threats and ambiguous situations. Both processes predicted subsequent increases in negative affect, but rumination showed a stronger link to sustained negative mood, whereas worry was more acutely tied to anxiety. These findings highlight distinct everyday triggers and affective sequelae, offering insights for context-specific interventions.

title: Improving Zero-Day Malware Testing Methodology Using Statistically Significant Time-Lagged Test Samples
text_ai: Enterprise networks are in constant danger of being breached by cyber-attackers, but making the decision about what security tools to deploy to mitigate this risk requires carefully designed evaluation of security products. One of the most important metrics for a protection product is how well it is able to stop malware, specifically on "zero"-day malware that has not been seen by the security community before. However, current methodologies often utilize instantaneous or short-term sample collections, which may not accurately reflect the long-term efficacy of security solutions against evolving zero-day threats, potentially leading to misleading evaluations. This paper introduces a novel testing methodology leveraging statistically significant time-lagged test samples. By systematically curating and analyzing malware collected over an extended period, our approach provides a more robust and ecologically valid assessment of a product’s ability to detect and neutralize previously unknown executables. We demonstrate that this method offers a more precise and predictive measure of zero-day defense, highlighting significant discrepancies compared to traditional instantaneous sampling. This work critically advances the scientific rigor of security product evaluations, enabling more informed decisions for enterprise security architects.

title: Character-based Neural Machine Translation
text_ai: We introduce a neural machine translation model that views the input and output sentences as sequences of characters rather than words. Since word-level information provides a crucial source of bias, our input model composes representations of character sequences into representations of words (as determined by whitespace boundaries), and then these are translated using a joint attention/translation model. This hybrid architecture effectively leverages character-level flexibility to handle out-of-vocabulary (OOV) words and morphologically rich languages, while preserving essential word-level semantic information. We evaluate our model on standard translation benchmarks for English-German and English-Czech. Our experiments show competitive performance against strong word-based NMT baselines, particularly excelling with rare words and complex morphology. It inherently addresses OOV challenges, reduces subword tokenization needs, and thus offers a more universal solution for diverse linguistic phenomena with a significantly smaller effective vocabulary.

title: The susceptibility of the square lattice Ising model: New developments
text_ai: We have made substantial advances in elucidating the properties of the susceptibility of the square lattice Ising model. We discuss its analyticity properties, certain closed form expressions for subsets of the coefficients, and give an algorithm of complexity O(N^6) to determine its first N coefficients. This significantly extends the range of accessible coefficients, offering unprecedented precision in probing the model's critical behavior. We exploit these high-order series expansions to precisely characterize the logarithmic divergence of the susceptibility near the critical temperature. Our analysis yields highly accurate estimates for critical exponents and amplitudes, providing compelling numerical evidence that corroborates theoretical predictions and deepens our understanding of the model's intricate analytic structure. This robust framework advances the study of exactly solvable models and offers a powerful tool for investigating critical phenomena in related lattice systems.

title: Hidden momentum and the Abraham-Minkowski debate
text_ai: We use an extended version of electrodynamics, which admits the existence of magnetic charges and currents, to discuss how different models for electric and magnetic dipoles do or do not carry hidden momentum under the influence of external electromagnetic fields. Our analysis encompasses both conventional electric dipoles (modeled as separated static charges or current loops) and their magnetic counterparts, including hypothetical magnetic current loops and magnetic monopoles. We demonstrate that the presence and magnitude of hidden momentum are critically dependent on the specific internal structure of the dipole and the nature of the external fields, particularly considering cross-coupling effects within the extended framework. This investigation provides a novel perspective on the long-standing Abraham-Minkowski debate concerning the momentum of electromagnetic fields in matter. By explicitly accounting for the mechanical momentum associated with the internal dipole structure, our approach offers a clearer distinction between electromagnetic momentum residing in the fields and mechanical momentum carried by the material constituents. We show how total momentum conservation is consistently maintained, revealing new insights into momentum partitioning within complex electromagnetic systems and offering a pathway towards resolving ambiguities in the definition of field momentum in media.

title: Revealing hidden talents: The development, use, and benefit of VESPARCH.
text_ai: School attainment tests and Cognitive Abilities Tests are used in the United Kingdom to set targets for educational outcome. Whilst these are good predictors, they depend not only on basic ability but also on learnt knowledge and skills, such as reading. To address these limitations, we developed VESPARCH, a novel, non-verbal assessment instrument designed to measure underlying cognitive potential irrespective of acquired knowledge or linguistic proficiency. Its development involved extensive psychometric validation, ensuring robust reliability and construct validity across diverse student populations. VESPARCH employs a series of abstract visual reasoning tasks and pattern recognition challenges, administered digitally to enhance accessibility and minimize examiner bias. This methodology allows for the identification of innate problem-solving abilities and cognitive flexibility, often obscured by traditional, verbally-dependent assessments. Pilot studies and subsequent widespread implementation in UK educational settings have demonstrated VESPARCH's efficacy in identifying students with high cognitive aptitude who might otherwise be overlooked due to socio-economic factors, language barriers, or specific learning differences. By providing a more accurate insight into individual cognitive strengths, VESPARCH empowers educators to implement targeted support and enrichment strategies, fostering equitable educational outcomes and revealing previously unrecognised talents. This paper details the comprehensive development, practical application, and significant benefits of VESPARCH, advocating for its role in a more inclusive assessment landscape.

title: Gluten-Free Products: From Dietary Necessity to Premium Price Extraction Tool.
text_ai: Every year, the Italian National Health Service (NHS) provides about 200,000 celiac people (based on 2017 data) living in Italy with financial support of about 250 million euro to cover the cost of their specific dietary constrains. This substantial public investment highlights the medical necessity of gluten-free (GF) diets for diagnosed individuals. However, the market for GF products has expanded significantly beyond this core group, driven by perceived health benefits among non-celiac consumers. This study investigates whether this market expansion, coupled with the inherent production complexities, has transformed GF products from a medical necessity into a mechanism for premium price extraction. We analyze price differences between conventional and GF equivalents across various product categories in Italian supermarkets, utilizing a comprehensive dataset of over 500 products. Our findings reveal a consistent and substantial price premium for GF items, often exceeding 150% even after accounting for ingredient costs and production overheads. Furthermore, qualitative analysis of marketing strategies indicates a deliberate positioning of GF products as a lifestyle choice rather than solely a therapeutic requirement, appealing to a broader, affluent consumer base willing to pay more. This research exposes the dual nature of the GF market, where a legitimate medical need coexists with sophisticated pricing strategies that disproportionately affect those reliant on these products while generating significant profits from the wellness trend.

title: On the interplay between notions of additive and multiplicative largeness and its combinatorial applications
text_ai: Many natural notions of additive and multiplicative largeness arise from results in Ramsey theory. In this paper, we explain the relationships between these notions for subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ and in more general ring-theoretic structures. We show that multiplicative largeness begets additive largeness in three ways and give a collection of examples demonstrating the optimality of these results. Specifically, we demonstrate that strong multiplicative recurrence implies additive syndeticity, specific product set properties generate arithmetic progressions, and multiplicatively structured sets within certain density classes yield piecewise syndeticity. Our analysis extends these relationships to general commutative rings, detailing their manifestation in broader algebraic settings. The proofs employ techniques from topological dynamics, nonstandard analysis, and additive combinatorics, leveraging ultrafilter theory and recent sumset theory. These findings yield significant combinatorial applications, including novel density theorems for configurations in $\mathbb{N}$ and insights into sumset/product set structures in finite fields and rings. We further show how our framework constructs sets with tailored additive and multiplicative characteristics, advancing understanding of number systems.

title: Mental well-being among the oldest old: revisiting the model of healthy ageing in a Finnish context.
text_ai: Purpose : This study aimed to examine how participants aged 80 years old or over describe their mental well-being-exploring the suitability of the model of healthy ageing when outlining the mental well-being concept. Methods : Six structured focus group interviews with 28 participants were conducted in Western Finland in 2017. Data were transcribed verbatim and subjected to inductive thematic analysis. Results : Participants highlighted the importance of meaningful social connections, a sense of purpose, maintaining autonomy despite physical limitations, and the ability to adapt and find joy in everyday life. Acceptance of age-related changes, including declining physical health and loss, also emerged as crucial. While elements of the traditional healthy ageing model (e.g., social engagement, cognitive function) resonated, the oldest old articulated a more nuanced, internally driven definition of well-being, often prioritizing spiritual and emotional resilience over purely biomedical indicators. The findings suggest the existing model may benefit from greater emphasis on subjective meaning-making, coping strategies, and the redefinition of 'health' in advanced age. Conclusion : This study highlights the multi-faceted nature of mental well-being among the oldest old in Finland, advocating for an enriched model of healthy ageing that acknowledges the unique challenges and adaptive capacities of this demographic. These insights are vital for developing age-friendly policies and interventions supporting holistic well-being in later life.

title: Efficient State Space Model via Fast Tensor Convolution and Block Diagonalization
text_ai: Existing models encounter bottlenecks in balancing performance and computational efficiency when modeling long sequences. Although the state space model (SSM) has achieved remarkable success in handling long sequence tasks, it still faces the problem of large number of parameters. This parameter burden, particularly with increasing state dimensions, leads to significant memory consumption and computational overhead, limiting scalability. To overcome these, we propose a novel efficient state space model (ESSM) integrating fast tensor convolution and block diagonalization. Fast tensor convolution replaces costly matrix multiplications in the SSM's recurrent dynamics with highly efficient convolutional operations, significantly reducing computational complexity for extremely long sequences. Concurrently, block diagonalization for the state transition matrix drastically reduces learnable parameters by exploiting modularity and sparsity, inherently facilitating parallel computation. The synergy yields an SSM variant with superior computational efficiency and a substantially smaller memory footprint. Empirical evaluations on diverse long sequence benchmarks demonstrate our ESSM matches or exceeds existing SSMs and competitive architectures in performance, while achieving significant improvements in speed and parameter efficiency. This offers a scalable and resource-efficient framework for advanced long sequence modeling.

title: Training and Serving System of Foundation Models: A Comprehensive Survey
text_ai: Foundation models (e.g., ChatGPT, DALL-E, PengCheng Mind, PanGu-$\Sigma$) have demonstrated extraordinary performance in key technological areas, such as natural language processing and visual recognition, and have become the mainstream trend of artificial general intelligence. This has led more and more major technology giants to dedicate significant human and financial resources to actively develop their foundation model systems, which drives continuous growth of these models' parameters. This continuous parameter growth introduces significant challenges across their entire lifecycle, from initial training to subsequent deployment and serving. Effectively managing these colossal models necessitates robust and scalable systems. Training demands sophisticated distributed learning frameworks, advanced optimization, and efficient data management to overcome computational and memory bottlenecks. Serving requires specialized inference systems for low latency, high throughput, and cost-efficiency, often leveraging model compression, quantization, and dedicated hardware. A comprehensive overview of the underlying training and serving infrastructure for foundation models remains critically lacking. This paper fills this gap by surveying cutting-edge methodologies, architectures, and systems, categorizing key techniques, identifying challenges, and outlining future directions.

title: METTL3-mediated m6A methylation negatively modulates autophagy to support porcine blastocyst development‡.
text_ai: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) catalyzed by METTL3 regulates the maternal-to-zygotic transition in zebrafish and mice. However, the role and mechanism of METTL3-mediated m6A methylation in blastocyst development remains unclear. Here, we show that METTL3-mediated m6A methylation sustains porcine blastocyst development via negatively modulating autophagy. We observed that METTL3 expression and global m6A levels were significantly elevated during porcine blastocyst formation. Knockdown of METTL3 significantly impaired blastocyst development, characterized by reduced cell numbers and compromised quality, accompanied by a global decrease in m6A levels. Further investigation revealed METTL3 depletion significantly increased autophagic flux, evidenced by elevated LC3-II/LC3-I ratios and ATG5/ATG7 expression. Mechanistically, m6A modification of key autophagy-related genes, including ATG7 and ATG5, was found to dampen autophagic activity by modulating their expression or stability. Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy significantly rescued developmental defects induced by METTL3 knockdown, confirming autophagy modulation's critical role. Our findings uncover a novel regulatory axis where METTL3-mediated m6A methylation negatively modulates autophagy, a process crucial for maintaining cellular homeostasis, to ensure successful porcine blastocyst development. This study provides new insights into epigenetic mechanisms governing early embryonic development and offers potential strategies for improving reproductive efficiency.

title: Compact Plasmonic Logic Gates Enabled by Magnetoelectric Light Funneling for On-Chip Optical Computing in the Telecom Band
text_ai: The realization of all-optical logic gates (AOLGs) is important for advancing photonic integrated circuit (PIC) design and optical data communication. Various photonic structures and design techniques, including two-dimensional photonic crystals, silicon waveguides, plasmonic waveguides, diffractive neural networks, and inverse design techniques, are actively being explored to achieve multifunctional, high-performance optical logic gates with fast data processing capabilities. Despite these advancements, achieving highly compact, low-loss, and reconfigurable all-optical logic gates (AOLGs) operating efficiently in the telecom band remains a critical challenge for high-density on-chip integration. While plasmonic waveguides offer unparalleled sub-wavelength light confinement, crucial for miniaturization, they often contend with significant propagation losses and complex control mechanisms that hinder their practical deployment. This paper introduces a novel paradigm for compact plasmonic logic gates enabled by precisely engineered magnetoelectric light funneling. We theoretically demonstrate that by integrating tailored magnetoelectric metamaterials with plasmonic waveguides, light can be efficiently guided, modulated, and redirected at the nanoscale. This mechanism facilitates the creation of robust and reconfigurable AND, OR, and NOT logic functions with footprints orders of magnitude smaller than the operating wavelength. Our designs exhibit high extinction ratios and low insertion losses, crucial for practical implementation in the telecom band. These compact plasmonic logic gates represent a significant advancement towards realizing high-speed, ultra-dense on-chip optical computing architectures, overcoming current limitations in photonic integration.

title: Select, then Balance: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Exogenous-Aware Spatio-Temporal Forecasting
text_ai: Spatio-temporal forecasting aims to predict the future state of dynamic systems and plays an important role in multiple fields. However, existing solutions only focus on modeling using a limited number of observed target variables. In real-world scenarios, exogenous variables can be integrated into the model as additional input features and associated with the target signal to promote forecast accuracy. Integrating exogenous variables, however, introduces challenges like redundancy, noise, and varying spatio-temporal relevance, which can degrade performance. To effectively leverage this information, we propose "Select, then Balance" (STB), a novel plug-and-play framework for exogenous-aware spatio-temporal forecasting. STB employs a two-stage approach: first, an adaptive selection module identifies relevant exogenous features for specific spatio-temporal contexts, effectively filtering noise; subsequently, a dynamic balancing mechanism optimally weighs and integrates these selected features, ensuring their proportional contribution. Its modular design allows seamless integration with diverse backbone spatio-temporal models without architectural modifications. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that STB consistently enhances forecast accuracy and robustness, outperforming state-of-the-art methods and validating its efficacy and generalizability.

title: Public Discourse Sandbox: Facilitating Human and AI Digital Communication Research
text_ai: Social media serves as a primary communication and information dissemination platform for major global events, entertainment, and niche or topically focused community discussions. Therefore, it represents a valuable resource for researchers who aim to understand numerous questions. However, obtaining data can be difficult, expensive, and often unreliable due to the presence of bots, fake accounts, and manipulated content. These challenges significantly impede the rigorous and ethical study of digital communication dynamics, impacting our understanding of phenomena like misinformation spread, polarization, and community formation. To address these critical limitations, this paper introduces the 'Public Discourse Sandbox' (PDS), a novel, controlled, and ethically-designed research environment. The PDS allows researchers to simulate authentic online communication scenarios, providing a platform where human participants and AI agents can interact in structured, observable settings. This unique capability facilitates the generation of high-fidelity, labeled datasets free from the noise and ethical ambiguities of real-world social media. The sandbox design specifically supports investigations into the nuances of human-AI collaboration and conflict, the impact of AI-generated content on human perception, and the efficacy of different moderation strategies. By offering a reproducible and controllable experimental space, the PDS empowers scholars to explore complex questions surrounding digital discourse, test theoretical models, and develop interventions with unprecedented precision, ultimately advancing the field of digital communication research.

title: Outpatient commitment in mental health services from a municipal view.
text_ai: Outpatient commitment (OC) is a legal decision for compulsory mental health care when the patient stays in his or her own home. Municipal health-care workers have a key role for patients with OC decision, but little is known about how the legislation system with OC works from the municipality's point of view. This qualitative study therefore aimed to explore municipal health-care workers' experiences and perspectives regarding the practical implementation and challenges of outpatient commitment. Semi-structured interviews with 15 municipal health-care professionals (social workers, nurses, case managers) from diverse municipalities were conducted, with data analyzed thematically. Findings revealed significant complexities in OC's operationalization, including ambiguous legal mandates, inter-agency coordination difficulties, and substantial resource limitations. Participants also reported ethical dilemmas balancing patient autonomy with compulsory treatment and the emotional toll of managing high-needs cases. Varying training and support levels further influenced effective OC delivery. The study underscores the urgent need for clearer legislative guidance, enhanced inter-sectoral collaboration, and targeted professional development to support municipal health-care workers. These insights are crucial for developing more effective and ethically sound outpatient commitment practices, improving patient care, and optimizing municipal resource utilization.

title: Mol-R1: Towards Explicit Long-CoT Reasoning in Molecule Discovery
text_ai: Large language models (LLMs), especially Explicit Long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1 and QWQ, have demonstrated powerful reasoning capabilities, achieving impressive performance in commonsense reasoning and mathematical inference. Despite their effectiveness, Long-CoT reasoning models are often criticized for their limited ability and low efficiency in knowledge-intensive domains such as molecule discovery. To address this critical gap, we introduce **Mol-R1**, a novel framework leveraging explicit long-CoT reasoning for molecule discovery. Mol-R1 integrates a knowledge-aware reasoning engine with a multi-step inference process, systematically navigating complex chemical spaces. Unlike general-purpose CoT models, Mol-R1 incorporates domain-specific heuristics and chemical reaction pathways, decomposing high-level design objectives (e.g., target property prediction, novel scaffold generation) into interpretable, chemically-sound steps. This explicit pathway enhances candidate proposals and provides transparent justifications for design choices, boosting efficiency and reliability. Our experiments demonstrate Mol-R1 outperforms state-of-the-art methods in molecule discovery tasks, including *de novo* design and lead optimization, achieving superior hit rates and diversity with unparalleled interpretability in its reasoning trajectory. This work paves the way for more robust and trustworthy AI systems in chemical research and drug development.

title: Saving Science by Doing Less of It?
text_ai: In the current issue of The New Atlantis, Daniel Sarewitz, professor of science and society at Arizona State University, argues that science is broken because it is managed and judged by scientists themselves, operating under Vannevar Bush's famous 1945 declaration that scientific progress depends on the "free play of free intellects … dictated by their curiosity." Sarewitz argues that this unchecked autonomy fosters a system prone to overproduction, perverse incentives, and a replication crisis. This diminishes science's capacity to address pressing societal challenges and erodes public trust, as unfettered curiosity often obscures transformative discoveries with a deluge of incremental findings. This paper critically examines Sarewitz's diagnosis, exploring the radical implication that 'saving science' may necessitate a deliberate strategic shift towards a more focused, problem-oriented, and externally guided approach. We investigate mechanisms by which a more curated scientific enterprise, prioritizing impact and reproducibility, could re-align research with societal needs and restore its epistemological robustness. We argue that such a recalibration, involving 'doing less' of certain types of research, is crucial for re-committing to science's foundational purpose and long-term societal value.
