title: The POKEMON Speckle Survey of Nearby M Dwarfs. III. The Stellar Multiplicity Rate of M Dwarfs within 15 pc
text_ai: M dwarfs are ubiquitous in our galaxy, and the rate at which they host stellar companions, and the properties of these companions, provides a window into the formation and evolution of the star(s), and of any planets that they may host. This paper, the third in the POKEMON series, presents a comprehensive analysis of the stellar multiplicity rate for a volume-limited sample of 170 M dwarfs within 15 parsecs. Using high-resolution speckle imaging, we systematically surveyed these targets for companions at angular separations from 0.03 to 5 arcseconds (approximately 1-75 AU). Our observations reveal a stellar multiplicity rate of 27% ± 3% for the full sample, identifying 46 companions. We find that binary and higher-order systems are common, with a significant fraction of companions located within 20 AU. The distribution of companion separations peaks at around 10 AU, consistent with previous studies but providing enhanced statistics for nearby M dwarfs. We also investigate the mass ratio distribution, finding a preference for roughly equal-mass companions in close systems. These results offer crucial constraints on theories of low-mass star formation, suggesting fragmentation processes efficiently produce close M dwarf binaries. Furthermore, understanding the architecture of these systems is vital for assessing the habitability and dynamical stability of exoplanets in M dwarf multiple systems.

title: Volatile evolution and atmospheres of Trans-Neptunian Objects
text_ai: At 30-50 K, the temperatures typical for surfaces in the Kuiper Belt (e.g. Stern & Trafton 2008), only seven species have sublimation pressures higher than 1 nbar (Fray & Schmitt 2009): Ne, N$_2$, CO, Ar, O$_2$, CH$_4$, and Kr. Of these, N$_2$, CO, and CH$_4$ have been detected or inferred on the surfaces of Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs). These highly volatile species, particularly N$_2$ and CO, are critical for forming and sustaining tenuous TNO atmospheres. Their stability results from a dynamic balance between surface ice sublimation and various escape mechanisms, including thermal (e.g., Jeans escape) and non-thermal processes driven by solar radiation and energetic particles. Internal heating, from radiogenic decay or tidal forces, can significantly enhance outgassing, fostering transient or sustained atmospheric activity. Long-term atmospheric evolution is intrinsically linked to volatile depletion, sequestration, and potential replenishment via cryovolcanism or impacts. This paper reviews current volatile inventories, models atmospheric formation and loss processes, and explores the resulting evolutionary pathways for these distant worlds.

title: Probing the mechanical properties of DNA nanostructures with metadynamics
text_ai: Molecular dynamics simulations are often used to provide feedback in the design workflow of DNA nanostructures. However, even with coarse-grained models, convergence of distributions from unbiased simulation is slow, limiting applications to equilibrium structural properties. Given the increasing interest in dynamic, reconfigurable, and deformable devices, methods that enable efficient quantification of large ranges of motion, conformational transitions, and mechanical deformation are critically needed. To address this, we apply metadynamics, an enhanced sampling method, which efficiently explores free energy landscapes of mechanical deformation in DNA nanostructures. Judicious collective variable selection, capturing essential bending, twisting, and stretching modes, accelerates sampling and overcomes kinetic barriers. This enables accurate determination of force-response curves, elastic moduli, and deformation pathways, providing insights into the mechanical resilience and flexibility of DNA origami and wireframe designs. Metadynamics systematically probes anisotropic mechanical properties, revealing distinct responses to external forces crucial for rational design and engineering. This robust framework for predicting DNA-based device dynamics and mechanical robustness facilitates reconfigurable biomolecular machine development.

title: Exploring Generative AI for Sim2Real in Driving Data Synthesis
text_ai: Datasets are essential for training and testing vehicle perception algorithms. However, the collection and annotation of real-world images is time-consuming and expensive. Driving simulators offer a solution by automatically generating various driving scenarios with corresponding annotations, but the simulation-to-reality (Sim2Real) domain gap remains a challenge. Recent advancements in generative artificial intelligence (GAI), particularly diffusion models and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), present promising avenues for mitigating this discrepancy. By learning the underlying statistical properties of real-world data, GAI models can transform synthetic simulator outputs into more photorealistic images, thereby reducing the domain gap and improving the transferability of perception algorithms trained on synthetic data. This paper explores the efficacy of various generative AI architectures in enhancing synthetic driving datasets for Sim2Real transfer. We investigate methods for domain adaptation, focusing on image-to-image translation techniques to imbue simulated scenes with realistic textures, lighting, and environmental nuances characteristic of real-world driving conditions. Our study evaluates the performance of perception models trained on GAI-enhanced synthetic data against those trained on purely synthetic or real-world datasets across diverse tasks such as object detection and semantic segmentation. The findings demonstrate that strategically applied generative AI significantly improves the realism and utility of synthetic driving data, offering a scalable and cost-effective approach to augment limited real-world datasets and accelerate the development of robust autonomous driving systems.

Driving simulators offer a solution by automatically generating various driving scenarios with corresponding annotations, but the simulation-to-reality (Sim2Real) domain gap remains a challenge.

title: Prompt GeV emission in the synchrotron self-Compton model for Gamma-Ray Bursts
text_ai: The detection in 10 bursts of an optical counterpart emission (i.e. during the prompt GRB phase) that is 10-10000 brighter than the extrapolation of the burst spectrum to optical frequencies suggests a synchrotron self-Compton origin for the GRB emission, synchrotron producing the optical counterpart emission. In this scenario, the same population of relativistic electrons responsible for the optical synchrotron photons then inverse-Compton scatters these photons to higher energies, naturally producing the observed X-ray and gamma-ray emission, including the prompt GeV component. We explore the parameter space of this synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) model to investigate the conditions required for robust prompt GeV emission, consistent with observations from Fermi-LAT. Our analysis demonstrates that the SSC mechanism can efficiently produce a substantial and prompt GeV flux, often co-temporal with the lower energy prompt emission, provided specific parameters for the magnetic field strength, electron energy distribution, and bulk Lorentz factor are met. We derive the expected GeV light curves and spectra, showing how they can discriminate between different physical regimes within the GRB outflow. This unified multi-wavelength framework not only explains the observed bright optical counterparts but also provides critical constraints on the properties of the emitting region, such as electron acceleration efficiency and magnetic field strength, offering a comprehensive understanding of the prompt high-energy processes in Gamma-Ray Bursts.

title: From Uncertainty to Anxiety: How Uncertainty Fuels Anxiety in a Process Mediated by Intolerance of Uncertainty.
text_ai: Uncertainty about future events may lead to worry, anxiety, even inability to function. The highly related concept-intolerance of uncertainty (IU)-emerged in the early 1990s, which is further developed into a transdiagnostic risk factor in multiple forms of anxiety disorders. This paper investigates the precise mechanistic role of IU in mediating the relationship between perceived uncertainty and anxiety. We hypothesized that individuals with higher IU would be more susceptible to experiencing anxiety in the face of ambiguity, as IU transforms the inherent uncertainty of situations into heightened threat perceptions. To test this, a cross-sectional study was conducted with 350 university students who completed self-report measures of perceived uncertainty, IU, and state-trait anxiety. Structural equation modeling revealed a robust direct effect of perceived uncertainty on anxiety, and critically, a significant indirect effect through IU. Specifically, higher levels of perceived uncertainty predicted greater IU, which, in turn, predicted increased anxiety symptoms, fully supporting the hypothesized mediation model. These findings underscore the central mechanistic role of IU in the pathway from environmental uncertainty to clinical anxiety, offering vital insights for refining cognitive models of anxiety and developing targeted interventions focused on reducing IU to mitigate anxiety vulnerability and improve functional outcomes.
prefix: Uncertainty about future events may lead to worry, anxiety, even inability to function. The highly related concept-intolerance of uncertainty (IU)-emerged in the early 1990s, which is further developed into a transdiagnostic risk factor in multiple forms of anxiety disorders.

title: PRIMG : Efficient LLM-driven Test Generation Using Mutant Prioritization
text_ai: Mutation testing is a widely recognized technique for assessing and enhancing the effectiveness of software test suites by introducing deliberate code mutations. However, its application often results in overly large test suites, as developers generate numerous tests to kill specific mutants, increasing computational overhead. This paper introduces **PRIMG**, a novel framework designed to address this challenge by integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with an intelligent mutant prioritization strategy. PRIMG first analyzes the generated mutants to identify a prioritized subset based on factors such as complexity, reachability, or representativeness. Subsequently, it leverages the code understanding and generative capabilities of LLMs to generate targeted test cases specifically for these prioritized mutants. The core hypothesis is that tests effective against a prioritized subset of mutants are also likely to kill a broader range of related mutants, thereby achieving high mutation coverage with a significantly smaller test suite. Our empirical evaluation of PRIMG on various open-source projects demonstrates its ability to generate highly effective test suites that achieve mutation scores comparable to those from exhaustive generation methods, but with a substantial reduction in test suite size and associated computational overhead. This approach offers a practical and efficient paradigm for leveraging mutation testing in real-world software development, making the technique more scalable and less resource-intensive.
prefix: Mutation testing is a widely recognized technique for assessing and enhancing the effectiveness of software test suites by introducing deliberate code mutations. However, its application often results in overly large test suites, as developers generate numerous tests to kill specific mutants, increasing computational overhead.

title: Generative AI as a Geopolitical Factor in Industry 5.0: Sovereignty, Access, and Control
text_ai: Industry 5.0 marks a new phase in industrial evolution, emphasizing human-centricity, sustainability, and resilience through the integration of advanced technologies. Within this evolving landscape, Generative AI (GenAI) and autonomous systems are not only transforming industrial processes but also emerging as pivotal geopolitical instruments. Their rapid evolution and deployment raise critical questions concerning national security, economic competitiveness, and global power dynamics. Nations face profound challenges to their **sovereignty**, particularly from reliance on foreign-developed GenAI models and infrastructure that can compromise data integrity, intellectual property, and autonomous decision-making. The imperative for technological independence and robust data governance is paramount. Furthermore, uneven **access** to advanced GenAI capabilities and foundational models risks exacerbating global inequalities, concentrating economic and strategic advantages within a few technological hegemons. The struggle for **control** over GenAI's development, ethical frameworks, and deployment across critical sectors directly impacts national leverage and future industrial trajectories. This paper analyzes these emergent geopolitical dimensions, exploring the intricate relationships between GenAI proliferation, national sovereignty, equitable access, and the imperative for robust control mechanisms in Industry 5.0.
prefix: Industry 5.0 marks a new phase in industrial evolution, emphasizing human-centricity, sustainability, and resilience through the integration of advanced technologies. Within this evolving landscape, Generative AI (GenAI) and autonomous systems are not only transforming industrial processes but also emerging as pivotal geopolitical instruments.

title: The Oldest Stars of the Extremely Metal-Poor Local Group Dwarf Irregular Galaxy Leo A
text_ai: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star photometry of Leo A in B, V, and I. Our new field of view is offset from the centrally located field observed by Tolstoy et al. (1998) in order to expose the halo population of this galaxy. The resulting color-magnitude diagram (CMD) reaches below the main sequence turn-off (MSTO) for stars older than 10 Gyr, enabling robust determination of the oldest stellar populations. We identify a significant population of extremely metal-poor (EMP) stars, characterized by a blue horizontal branch (BHB) and an old main sequence turn-off (MSTO) at V ~ 26.5 mag. Detailed comparison with theoretical isochrones confirms stars with ages exceeding 12 Gyr and metallicities as low as [Fe/H] < -2.5. This provides direct evidence for an ancient, metal-poor stellar component extending into Leo A's outer regions, significantly predating the star formation burst observed in the galaxy's core. We derive the star formation history (SFH) for this halo field using CMD fitting, confirming that a substantial fraction of star formation occurred more than 10 Gyr ago. This early, less vigorous epoch of star formation is crucial for understanding Leo A's initial chemical enrichment and reionization history. The spatial distribution of these ancient stars suggests a more extended, spheroidal component, distinct from younger, more centrally concentrated stellar populations. Our analysis reveals that cumulative star formation for ages > 10 Gyr constitutes approximately 15% of the total stellar mass formed in this region, emphasizing the importance of early epochs. The inferred metallicity distribution for the oldest stars is consistent with a very slow, inefficient chemical enrichment process in the early universe, characteristic of low-mass, isolated dwarf galaxies. These findings underscore Leo A's status as a true ancient dwarf, possessing a significant population of primordial stars that trace its earliest assembly. The presence of a widespread, ancient, and extremely metal-poor stellar halo provides strong constraints on dwarf galaxy formation and evolution models, particularly concerning gas accretion and feedback in low-mass systems. Our results suggest Leo A experienced an early, quiescent phase of star formation, followed by later, more prominent bursts. This study offers critical insights into the formation mechanisms of the least massive and most metal-poor Local Group galaxies, linking their stellar populations to the cosmic reionization era and earliest epochs of structure formation.

title: Race does not predict the development of metastases in men with nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
text_ai: BACKGROUND: Although race is associated with prostate cancer progression in early stage disease, once men have advanced disease, it is unclear whether race continues to predict a poor outcome. OBJECTIVE: We investigated the association between self-reported race and distant metastasis development in a large nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC) cohort. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 1,582 men with nmCRPC from a multi-institutional database. Follow-up was from nmCRPC diagnosis until development of distant metastases or last follow-up. Clinicopathological variables, including age, baseline PSA, Gleason score, prior treatments, and self-reported race, were collected. The primary endpoint was metastasis-free survival (MFS). Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models were employed to assess race's association with MFS, adjusted for relevant covariates. RESULTS: The median follow-up was 36 months. 428 (27.0%) men developed distant metastases. Black men (18.0%) presented with higher median PSA (12.5 vs. 9.8 ng/mL, p=0.01) and higher-grade disease (Gleason 8-10: 45% vs. 38%, p=0.03) at nmCRPC diagnosis. Despite these differences, univariable analysis showed no significant association between race and MFS (HR: 1.08, 95% CI: 0.85-1.37, p=0.52). In multivariable analysis, adjusting for age, PSA, Gleason score, and prior treatments, race remained a non-significant predictor of metastasis development (HR: 1.02, 95% CI: 0.79-1.31, p=0.88). CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that self-reported race does not independently predict the development of distant metastases in men with nmCRPC. This challenges prior assumptions, suggesting other factors, not race, may drive observed disparities in earlier disease stages. These results highlight the need for race-neutral risk stratification in advanced prostate cancer, informing clinical trial design and patient counseling.
prefix: BACKGROUND: Although race is associated with prostate cancer progression in early stage disease, once men have advanced disease, it is unclear whether race continues to predict a poor outcome.

title: Survival of Salmonella spp. in Composting using Vial and Direct Inoculums Technique
text_ai: The survival of Salmonella spp. as pathogen indicator in composting was studied. The inoculums technique was used to gives the known amounts of Salmonella spp. involved in composting. The inoculums of Salmonella spp. solution was added directly into the compost material. The direct inoculum was compared with inoculums in vial technique. For this investigation, *Salmonella enterica* serovar Typhimurium was inoculated into batches of mixed organic waste compost. Initial inoculum concentrations were approximately 10^7 CFU/g for both methods. Composting was conducted in controlled reactors, maintaining aerobic conditions, monitoring thermophilic phase temperatures and moisture content over 21 days. Samples from both directly inoculated compost and compost containing *Salmonella*-laden vials were collected at regular intervals to enumerate viable *Salmonella* populations using selective plating. Results indicated a significant reduction in *Salmonella* counts. During the thermophilic phase (exceeding 55°C), *Salmonella* populations declined rapidly. The direct inoculum method demonstrated a faster inactivation rate, achieving a >5-log reduction within 7-10 days. *Salmonella* within protective vials exhibited slightly prolonged survival, with a similar >5-log reduction achieved within 14 days, suggesting insulation from the immediate composting environment. However, regardless of the inoculation method, *Salmonella* was consistently reduced to undetectable levels (<10 CFU/g) by the end of the composting cycle. This study highlights the effectiveness of controlled composting in inactivating *Salmonella* and underscores the importance of inoculation methodology when assessing pathogen survival kinetics, as direct exposure appears to accelerate elimination compared to protected vial systems, which may underestimate composting's true inactivation potential.

title: In-ear EEG biometrics for feasible and readily collectable real-world person authentication
text_ai: The use of EEG as a biometrics modality has been investigated for about a decade, however its feasibility in real-world applications is not yet conclusively established, mainly due to the issues with collectability and reproducibility. This paper proposes in-ear EEG as a novel approach to overcome these limitations. Its discreet, user-friendly nature enables readily collectable and repeatable biometric data acquisition in unconstrained environments, benefiting from reduced motion artifacts and close electrode proximity. We investigated in-ear EEG biometrics using a custom electrode system, collecting data from multiple subjects across sessions and cognitive tasks. Advanced signal processing and robust feature extraction were applied, followed by machine learning classification for subject-dependent authentication. Results demonstrate robust performance, achieving an average Equal Error Rate (EER) of 3.5% and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.98. Crucially, intra-subject reproducibility was significantly higher than traditional scalp EEG, indicating potential for consistent long-term use and resilience to minor head movements. These findings underscore in-ear EEG's significant potential as a viable, practical, and highly collectable biometric modality, paving the way for unobtrusive and reliable real-world personal authentication.

title: Visual-perceptual training with motor practice of the observed movement pattern improves anticipation in emerging expert cricket batsmen.
text_ai: This study addressed the paucity of evidence of whether visual anticipation can be improved in emerging experts in striking sports. Twelve emerging expert batsmen from a state cricket squad were equally randomised into intervention and control groups. They were pre-and-post tested on a video temporal occlusion test of a fast bowler, as well as transfer tests of different fast and slow bowlers. The intervention group completed a six-week visual-perceptual training program, integrating temporally occluded video clips of bowlers with concurrent motor practice of observed movement patterns. The control group received an equivalent duration of standard technical coaching. Both groups completed 12 sessions. Post-intervention, the experimental group demonstrated significantly improved anticipation accuracy on the video temporal occlusion test (p < .01) compared to the control group, which showed no significant change. Crucially, these improvements transferred to novel fast and slow bowlers in the transfer tests (p < .05), indicating enhanced generalizability of perceptual skill. The control group showed no significant changes across any tests. These findings suggest that combining visual-perceptual training with motor practice effectively enhances anticipation in emerging expert batsmen, providing a robust training methodology for developing perceptual-motor skills critical for striking sports.

They were pre-and-post tested on a video temporal occlusion test of a fast bowler, as well as transfer tests of different fast and slow bowlers.

title: Neuromorphic meets neuromechanics, part I: the methodology and implementation.
text_ai: One goal of neuromorphic engineering is to create 'realistic' robotic systems that interact with the physical world by adopting neuromechanical principles from biology. Critical to this is the methodology to implement the spinal circuitry responsible for the behavior of afferented muscles. This paper presents a comprehensive methodology for modeling and implementing biologically plausible spinal cord circuits that govern the behavior of afferented muscles within a neuromorphic framework. We detail the theoretical underpinnings and practical considerations for integrating spiking neural networks with realistic musculoskeletal dynamics. Our approach faithfully represents proprioceptive feedback, including detailed models of muscle spindle and Golgi tendon organ afferents, crucial for stable and adaptive motor control. We outline the design and parameterization of key spinal cord circuits—motor neuron pools, interneuron populations for reciprocal inhibition, and central pattern generators—ensuring computational efficiency and biological fidelity. The implementation strategy leverages a hybrid co-simulation environment, coupling a real-time neuromorphic simulator (e.g., SpiNNaker or Loihi) for neural processing with a high-fidelity rigid-body dynamics engine for physical interaction. This architecture facilitates direct, low-latency mapping of neural spikes to dynamic muscle activation (using a modified Hill-type model) and precise conversion of mechanical states (e.g., muscle length, force) into realistic afferent signals. We address critical challenges of latency management, data synchronization across heterogeneous platforms, and robust communication interface design between these disparate computational domains. The resulting framework provides a rigorous, scalable platform for investigating complex, adaptive motor behaviors emerging from fundamental neuromechanical interactions, advancing bio-inspired robotic control and offering a novel neuroscientific tool.
prefix: One goal of neuromorphic engineering is to create 'realistic' robotic systems that interact with the physical world by adopting neuromechanical principles from biology. Critical to this is the methodology to implement the spinal circuitry responsible for the behavior of afferented muscles.

title: Multi-Institutional Predictors of Antibiotic Resistance in Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department with Urosepsis Secondary to Ureteral Obstruction.
text_ai: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with a urinary tract infection with kidney or ureteral stones is a urologic emergency often achieve early clinical stability but remain hospitalized while awaiting results from urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses. This often leads to empiric broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, contributing to antimicrobial resistance and potentially suboptimal patient outcomes. Identifying early predictors of antibiotic resistance in this specific patient population is crucial for guiding appropriate empiric treatment and optimizing antibiotic stewardship. **Methods:** This multi-institutional retrospective cohort study aimed to identify demographic, clinical, and microbiological predictors of antibiotic resistance in patients presenting to the emergency department (ED) with urosepsis secondary to ureteral obstruction. Data from 876 consecutive adult patients admitted across four tertiary care centers between January 2018 and December 2022 were analyzed. Patients with positive urine culture and clinical signs of sepsis attributed to ureteral obstruction were included. Demographics, comorbidities, prior antibiotic exposure, healthcare-associated risk factors, and urine culture susceptibility profiles were collected. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of resistance to common empiric antibiotics (e.g., fluoroquinolones, third-generation cephalosporins, piperacillin-tazobactam). **Results:** Of the cohort, 28.5% exhibited resistance to at least one empiric antibiotic. Independent predictors included recent hospitalization (OR 2.3, 95% CI 1.8-2.9), prior antibiotic use within 90 days (OR 1.9, 95% CI 1.5-2.4), and history of recurrent urinary tract infections (OR 1.7, 95% CI 1.3-2.1). Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) producing *Escherichia coli* was the most common resistant pathogen. **Conclusion:** These findings provide key clinical markers for predicting antibiotic resistance in patients presenting with urosepsis secondary to ureteral obstruction. Integrating these readily available predictors into initial ED assessment can facilitate more tailored empiric antibiotic selection, reducing broad-spectrum use, shortening hospital stays, and improving patient outcomes while promoting antibiotic stewardship.
prefix: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with a urinary tract infection with kidney or ureteral stones is a urologic emergency often achieve early clinical stability but remain hospitalized while awaiting results from urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses.

title: The 2018 classification of periodontal diseases: Its predictive value for tooth loss.
text_ai: Predictive models and assessment tools for disease susceptibility and progression are necessary to enhance personalized medicine. The aim of this study is to assess the predictive accuracy of using the 2018 classification to predict likelihood of tooth loss. A total of 134 patients were screened 10 years after periodontal therapy. Patients were retrospectively classified using the 2018 system (Stages I-IV, Grades A-C) from baseline clinical and radiographic data. Tooth loss over 10 years was the primary outcome. Cox regression models assessed associations, adjusting for confounders. A significant association was found: higher stages (III and IV) and grades (B and C) at baseline showed significantly elevated tooth loss risk (e.g., HR for Stage IV vs. I = 4.2, p < 0.001). The classification demonstrated good predictive ability, particularly for high-risk individuals. These findings confirm the 2018 classification's substantial predictive value for long-term tooth loss post-therapy. Its systematic use offers a robust prognostic tool for risk stratification, enabling personalized treatment and recall strategies to preserve dentition.

title: Reductions in alcohol use following medical cannabis initiation: results from a large cross-sectional survey of medical cannabis patients in Canada.
text_ai: Evidence details how cannabis can influence the use of other psychoactive substances, including prescription medications, alcohol, tobacco and illicit drugs, but very little research has examined the factors associated with these changes in substance use patterns. This paper explores the self-reported use of cannabis as a substitute for alcohol among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population. Utilizing a large cross-sectional survey, data were collected from 2,130 Canadian authorized medical cannabis patients. Participants completed an online questionnaire detailing medical conditions, cannabis use patterns, and perceived changes in alcohol consumption post-initiation. Our analysis revealed that a significant proportion (68.5%) reported reducing or ceasing alcohol consumption after initiating medical cannabis, with 45.2% explicitly indicating cannabis as a direct substitute. Logistic regression identified factors significantly associated with alcohol reduction, including younger age, higher frequency of cannabis use, and using cannabis to manage pain, anxiety, or sleep disturbances. Patients frequently cited cannabis's perceived efficacy for symptom management and fewer undesirable side effects compared to alcohol as primary motivations, suggesting a deliberate harm reduction strategy. These findings underscore medical cannabis's potential role as a harm reduction tool for individuals seeking to reduce alcohol intake within a regulated medical context. The observed substitution patterns highlight patients' strategic leveraging of cannabis to achieve therapeutic goals while mitigating alcohol-related risks. Longitudinal research is warranted to confirm causal pathways and explore long-term health outcomes. Clinicians and policymakers should consider these patient-reported trends when developing harm reduction strategies and counseling patients about the potential interplay between cannabis and alcohol use.

title: On the stability of the spherically symmetric solution to an inflow problem for an isentropic model of compressible viscous fluid
text_ai: We investigate an inflow problem for the multi-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations. The fluid under consideration occupies the exterior domain of unit ball, $\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\,\vert\, |x|\ge 1\}$, and a constant stream of mass is flowing into the domain from the boundary $\partial\Omega=\{|x|=1\}$. We first establish the existence and uniqueness of a smooth, spherically symmetric stationary solution to this problem, which exhibits a specific decay profile at spatial infinity. The primary focus of this work is to analyze the nonlinear stability of this stationary solution under general multi-dimensional perturbations. Utilizing a combination of weighted energy estimates and spectral analysis, we demonstrate that this base state is nonlinearly asymptotically stable provided the inflow mass flux is sufficiently small and the adiabatic index satisfies certain conditions relevant for physical gases. Specifically, we prove that any sufficiently small perturbation, originating from appropriate weighted Sobolev spaces, converges exponentially fast to the stationary solution as time tends to infinity. Our analysis highlights the crucial role of the inflow boundary condition and the interplay between viscosity and compressibility in determining the long-term behavior of the fluid system. The results are obtained for $n \ge 2$.

title: The effect of structural and magnetic disorder on the 3$d$-5$d$ exchange interactions of La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_{6}$
text_ai: The delicate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystalline electric field interactions observed in Ir-based oxides is usually manifested as exotic magnetic behavior. Here we investigate the evolution of the exchange coupling between Co and Ir for partial La substitution by Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. This substitution, creating La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_{6}$, introduces both structural and magnetic disorder. We employ a combination of X-ray diffraction, bulk magnetometry, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy to elucidate the intricate interplay between charge, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom. Structural analysis reveals a progressive distortion of the IrO$_6$ and CoO$_6$ octahedra with increasing Ca content, accompanied by a reduction in the long-range structural order. This structural perturbation directly impacts the superexchange pathways critical for the 3$d$-5$d$ interactions. Concurrently, charge compensation mechanisms drive mixed valency, primarily evidenced by the coexistence of Co$^{2+/3+}$ and Ir$^{4+/5+}$ states. X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Co and Ir L-edges confirms these valence state changes, revealing a significant modification of the local electronic structure and the effective magnetic moments of both Co and Ir. Specifically, the Ir electronic configuration shifts from a dominant $J_{eff}$=1/2 state towards a more complex orbital configuration, thereby weakening the strong spin-orbit coupling effects characteristic of Ir$^{4+}$ and altering its magnetic anisotropy. Bulk magnetization measurements reveal a systematic suppression of the long-range magnetic order observed in the parent compound, giving way to complex magnetic states characterized by enhanced frustration and spin-glass-like behavior at higher Ca concentrations. Our findings demonstrate that the induced structural irregularities and charge disorder profoundly disrupt the delicate balance governing the Co-Ir exchange interactions, leading to a competition between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic superexchange pathways. This study underscores the critical role of disorder engineering in tuning the fundamental magnetic interactions in 3$d$-5$d$ double perovskites, offering valuable insights into designing materials with tailored magnetic properties and understanding the emergence of novel quantum phenomena in systems where strong correlations and spin-orbit coupling coexist.
prefix: The delicate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystalline electric field interactions observed in Ir-based oxides is usually manifested as exotic magnetic behavior. title: VIVID: A Novel Approach to Remediation Prioritization in Static Application Security Testing (SAST)
text_ai: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) enables organizations to detect vulnerabilities in code early; however, major SAST platforms do not include visual aids and present little insight on correlations between tainted data chains. VIVID (Visual Interactive Vulnerability Insight Dashboard) addresses these critical limitations by introducing a novel visual analytics framework for enhanced remediation prioritization. Our approach leverages a sophisticated graph-based representation to map intricate data flows and taint propagation paths, offering an intuitive, interactive visualization of security-relevant data dependencies. Crucially, VIVID employs a proprietary algorithm that analyzes the interconnectedness of multiple tainted data chains, identifying critical nodes and pathways that contribute to a broader set of vulnerabilities. This allows for a data-driven, intelligent prioritization mechanism that moves beyond static severity rankings, focusing instead on the systemic impact and exploitability of underlying taint issues. By quantifying the 'risk propagation' and 'shared dependency' of tainted sources and sinks, VIVID significantly enhances the developer's ability to understand root causes, streamline remediation efforts, and reduce false positives. Our evaluation demonstrates that VIVID can substantially improve the efficiency and effectiveness of vulnerability management, leading to faster mean time to remediation and a more focused allocation of security resources.
prefix: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) enables organizations to detect vulnerabilities in code early; however, major SAST platforms do not include visual aids and present little insight on correlations between tainted data chains.

title: Partial-Information Multiple Access Protocol for Orthogonal Transmissions
text_ai: With the stringent requirements introduced by the new sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) use cases, traditional approaches to multiple access control have started to show their limitations. A new wave of grant-free (GF) approaches have been therefore proposed as a viable alternative. However, a definitive solution is still to be accomplished. This paper introduces a novel Partial-Information Multiple Access Protocol for Orthogonal Transmissions (PIMAP-OT) specifically engineered to overcome these limitations. PIMAP-OT operates under a grant-free paradigm, enabling IoT devices to transmit data without explicit scheduling requests, thereby significantly reducing access latency and signaling overhead. Its core innovation lies in the intelligent utilization of partial information regarding user activity and coarse channel state. Instead of relying on full channel state information or complex control signaling, PIMAP-OT leverages minimal, coarse-grained feedback or implicit signaling to facilitate efficient and collision-aware resource allocation across orthogonal transmission channels, such as OFDMA subcarriers or time slots. This allows the base station to perform robust activity detection and resolve potential resource contention with unprecedented efficiency. The protocol mechanism is meticulously designed to balance the inherent trade-offs between spectral efficiency, collision probability, and overall system complexity. Devices autonomously select orthogonal resources, and the base station, aided by the partial information, effectively identifies active users and their chosen resources, even amidst simultaneous transmissions. This partial-information-driven strategy significantly mitigates the high collision rates and throughput degradation common in pure ALOHA-like GF schemes under heavy load. Through extensive analytical modeling and comprehensive system-level simulations, we rigorously evaluate the performance of PIMAP-OT. The results consistently demonstrate that our proposed protocol achieves substantial gains in terms of network throughput, average access delay, and energy efficiency, particularly for massive IoT deployments. PIMAP-OT exhibits superior scalability and robustness against varying traffic loads and user densities, positioning it as a highly promising candidate for fulfilling the demanding connectivity requirements of future 6G IoT ecosystems.
prefix: With the stringent requirements introduced by the new sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) use cases, traditional approaches to multiple access control have started to show their limitations. A new wave of grant-free (GF) approaches have been therefore proposed as a viable alternative. However, a definitive solution is still to be accomplished.

title: Diversifying Knowledge Enhancement of Biomedical Language Models using Adapter Modules and Knowledge Graphs
text_ai: Recent advances in natural language processing (NLP) owe their success to pre-training language models on large amounts of unstructured data. Still, there is an increasing effort to combine the unstructured nature of LMs with structured knowledge and reasoning. In the biomedical domain, where precision and accuracy are paramount, leveraging rich, structured knowledge from Knowledge Graphs (KGs) is crucial to mitigate LM limitations (e.g., hallucination, poor interpretability). However, direct KG integration into LMs is often computationally intensive and rigid. This paper introduces a novel framework for diversifying knowledge enhancement of biomedical LMs using adapter modules and KGs. We utilize lightweight, parameter-efficient adapter modules, each specializing in distinct biomedical knowledge types (e.g., gene-disease associations, drug-target interactions) from KGs. This modular design enables flexible, incremental knowledge injection, allowing LMs to acquire and reason with diverse domain-specific facts without extensive retraining. Our experiments demonstrate that these knowledge-infused adapters, selectively activated or composed, yield significant performance gains across biomedical NLP tasks such as NER, relation extraction, and QA. This highlights adapter-based knowledge diversification's efficacy in enhancing biomedical LM accuracy, robustness, and interpretability, offering a scalable paradigm for integrating complex domain expertise.
prefix: Recent advances in natural language processing (NLP) owe their success to pre-training language models on large amounts of unstructured data. Still, there is an increasing effort to combine the unstructured nature of LMs with structured knowledge and reasoning.

title: Generative Text-Guided 3D Vision-Language Pretraining for Unified Medical Image Segmentation
text_ai: Vision-Language Pretraining (VLP) has demonstrated remarkable capabilities in learning visual representations from textual descriptions of images without annotations. Yet, effective VLP demands large-scale image-text pairs, a resource that suffers scarcity in the medical domain. Moreover, conventional VLP is limited to 2D images while medical images encompass diverse modalities, often in 3D, making the learning process more challenging. To address these limitations, we propose a novel Generative Text-Guided 3D Vision-Language Pretraining (GTVLP) framework. GTVLP leverages a generative model to synthesize diverse 3D visual features conditioned on descriptive medical texts, effectively expanding the training data and alleviating scarcity. This approach enables the model to learn rich, text-aligned 3D representations without explicit pixel-level annotations. Furthermore, GTVLP incorporates a 3D vision transformer backbone to inherently process volumetric data, allowing for direct learning from multi-modal 3D medical scans. By unifying visual and textual information in a shared embedding space, our method facilitates zero-shot and few-shot segmentation across various anatomical structures and imaging modalities, guided solely by natural language prompts. Extensive experiments on multiple public medical image datasets demonstrate that GTVLP significantly outperforms state-of-the-art VLP and specialized segmentation models, achieving superior performance in challenging 3D medical image segmentation tasks. Our findings highlight the potential of generative text-guided pretraining to unlock truly unified and annotation-efficient medical AI.

title: Quantum entanglement between an atom and a molecule
text_ai: Conventional information processors freely convert information between different physical carriers to process, store, or transmit information. It seems plausible that quantum information will also be held by different physical carriers in applications such as tests of fundamental physics, quantum-enhanced sensors, and quantum information processing. Such heterogeneous quantum systems, leveraging the distinct advantages of various physical carriers, offer unique opportunities for expanding the capabilities of quantum technologies. Here, we theoretically propose a novel scheme to generate and verify quantum entanglement between a single trapped atomic ion and a co-trapped polar molecule. The atom, with its well-defined electronic transitions and long coherence times, serves as a robust qubit, while the molecule offers a rich internal structure of rotational and vibrational states that can be precisely manipulated and engineered. Our approach leverages a resonant dipole-dipole interaction mediated by a shared optical cavity field, enabling coherent state transfer and entangling operations. This hybrid architecture promises to bridge the gap between highly coherent atomic systems and the complex, engineerable degrees of freedom of molecular systems. This advancement opens new avenues for exploring fundamental atom-molecule interactions, developing precision quantum sensors utilizing molecular internal states, and constructing modular quantum networks where information can be flexibly processed across disparate quantum registers, thereby enhancing the versatility and functionality of future quantum platforms.

It seems plausible that quantum information will also be held by different physical carriers in applications such as tests of fundamental physics, quantum-enhanced sensors, and quantum information processing.

title: Bone remodeling of the proximal tibia after uncemented total knee arthroplasty: secondary endpoints analyzed from a randomized trial comparing monoblock and modular tibia traysâ??2 year follow-up of 53 cases
text_ai: Background and purpose â?? Bone remodeling as a response to bone trauma, postoperative immobilization, and device-related bone reactions can lead to loss of bone stock and increase the risk of periprosthetic fracture and aseptic loosening. This study investigates the adaptive bone remodeling of the proximal tibia after uncemented total knee arthroplasty (TKA). This study analyzed secondary endpoint data from a randomized controlled trial of 53 patients (53 knees) undergoing uncemented TKA, randomized to receive either a monoblock or a modular uncemented tibial component. Periprosthetic bone mineral density (BMD) was quantitatively assessed using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) at pre-defined regions of interest around the tibial component at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Longitudinal change in BMD from baseline, comparing the two designs, was the primary outcome over 2 years. At 2-year follow-up, significant changes in periprosthetic BMD were observed across several zones, predominantly bone loss in proximal medial/lateral regions and distal bone gain. The most pronounced BMD decrease, up to 15% reduction, occurred in proximal medial and lateral zones. Both monoblock and modular trays showed similar overall remodeling patterns, but the modular design exhibited statistically greater initial BMD loss in central load-bearing zones at 3 and 6 months (p < 0.05). This difference, however, attenuated by 12 and 24 months, with no significant BMD differences between groups at 2 years. No aseptic loosening or periprosthetic fracture occurred. This study demonstrates significant adaptive bone remodeling, characterized by proximal bone loss and distal bone gain, around uncemented tibial components within two years post-TKA. Although initial BMD differences were noted between monoblock and modular designs, these largely equalized by 24 months. These findings suggest both monoblock and modular tibial trays elicit similar long-term bone remodeling patterns, crucial for implant longevity and preventing complications.

title: Efficient Computation in Adaptive Artificial Spiking Neural Networks
text_ai: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are bio-inspired models of neural computation that have proven highly effective. Still, ANNs lack a natural notion of time, and neural units in ANNs exchange analog values in a frame-based manner, a computationally and energetically inefficient form of communication. Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), conversely, process information via discrete temporal events (spikes), mirroring biological brains more closely. This event-driven paradigm offers inherent advantages in sparsity, asynchronous operation, and energy efficiency, particularly for neuromorphic hardware. However, training SNNs to achieve competitive performance with ANNs, especially for complex tasks or continuous adaptation, remains a significant challenge. Direct application of backpropagation is often infeasible, and spike-based learning rules struggle with gradient propagation or convergence. This paper addresses these limitations by proposing novel methodologies for achieving efficient computation and robust adaptivity in artificial spiking neural networks. We introduce a biologically plausible, event-driven learning rule capable of rapid online adaptation without backpropagation through time. Our approach integrates a refined spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) mechanism with homeostatic regularization to maintain network stability and optimize synaptic efficacy based on local activity. Furthermore, we explore a specialized neuron model facilitating sparse activity and minimizing computational overhead during inference. Experimental results across diverse benchmarks, including dynamic pattern recognition and real-time control, demonstrate our adaptive SNN framework achieves state-of-the-art performance while significantly reducing computational cost and energy consumption compared to conventional ANNs and other SNN training methods. This work paves the way for highly efficient, autonomous, and biologically inspired AI systems.

title: Gravitational waves constraints on post-inflationary phases stiffer than radiation
text_ai: We point out that the existence of post-inflationary phases stiffer than radiation leads to the production of stochastic gravitational waves (GW) backgrounds whose logarithmic energy spectra (in critical units) are typically "blue" at high frequencies. Such phases, characterized by an equation of state parameter $w > 1/3$ (e.g., kination), are motivated by various early universe scenarios, including specific reheating mechanisms or dark matter production. The distinct blue tilt of their GW spectrum, scaling roughly as $\Omega_{GW} \propto f^n$ with $n>0$, makes them compelling targets for high-frequency gravitational wave observatories. We perform a comprehensive calculation of the full spectral shape of these backgrounds, accounting for the transition from the stiff phase to the subsequent radiation-dominated era, and parameterizing their duration and equation of state. Our analysis demonstrates that existing upper limits from pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and ground-based interferometers (LIGO/Virgo) already provide stringent constraints on the parameter space of such post-inflationary stiff phases. We show that these observations effectively constrain the energy scale and duration of these non-standard cosmological eras, extending beyond typical Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) bounds. Furthermore, we project the sensitivity of future detectors, including LISA and proposed higher-frequency experiments, illustrating their potential to either detect these unique GW signatures or further restrict the viability of these scenarios. This work establishes gravitational waves as a powerful probe of the fundamental physics governing the universe's earliest moments.

title: H-atom bombardment of CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO containing ices
text_ai: Context: Hydrogenation reactions are expected to be among the most important surface reactions on interstellar ices. However, solid state astrochemical laboratory data on reactions of H-atoms with common interstellar ice constituents are largely lacking. This study addresses this deficiency by investigating the hydrogenation of CO2, HCOOH, and CH3CHO ices under astrophysically relevant conditions (10-20 K, ultra-high vacuum). Using a dedicated experimental setup combining in-situ Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy and Quadrupole Mass Spectrometry (QMS), we monitored the chemical evolution of these ice analogues upon exposure to a beam of thermalized H-atoms. For CO2 ices, we observe the efficient formation of formic acid (HCOOH) and formaldehyde (H2CO), with subsequent hydrogenation of HCOOH leading to further H2CO production. Exposure of HCOOH ices directly resulted in the formation of H2CO and methanol (CH3OH), demonstrating a sequential hydrogenation pathway. Furthermore, the bombardment of acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) ice yielded ethanol (CH3CH2OH) as the primary product, confirming the reduction of the carbonyl group. Kinetic analysis of these reactions reveals significant production rates even at cryogenic temperatures, suggesting that these processes are viable routes for the synthesis of more complex organic molecules (COMs) within interstellar ice mantles. The observed product branching ratios and reaction efficiencies provide crucial input for astrochemical models, enabling a more accurate prediction of molecular abundances in various interstellar environments. These laboratory findings underscore the critical role of H-atom bombardment in driving the chemical complexity on dust grain surfaces, contributing to the inventory of molecules subsequently released into the gas phase, and ultimately influencing the chemical evolution of star-forming regions and protoplanetary disks.

title: Spot evolution on LQ Hya during 2006--2017: temperature maps based on SOFIN and FIES data
text_ai: Context. LQ Hya is one of the most frequently studied young solar analogue stars. Recently, it has been observed to show intriguing behaviour by analysing long-term photometry: during 2003--2009, a coherent spot structure migrating in the rotational frame has been reported by various authors, but since that time the star has entered a chaotic state where coherent structures seem to have disappeared and rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima occur irregularly over time. Aims. We investigate the surface spot evolution and temperature characteristics of LQ Hya during 2006–2017, covering its transition from a coherent migration phase to a chaotic regime. Methods. We employed Doppler imaging on 13 years of high-resolution spectroscopic observations from SOFIN and FIES spectrographs. These data, primarily photospheric absorption lines, enabled reconstruction of detailed temperature maps, allowing analysis of spot latitudes, longitudes, sizes, and temperature contrasts. Results. Our temperature maps reveal a dominant high-latitude spot feature persisting during 2006–2009, showing slow prograde migration, consistent with earlier photometry. Around 2010, surface activity patterns transformed significantly. The coherent high-latitude structure fragmented, replaced by multiple, smaller, rapidly evolving spot groups across wider latitudes. These features displayed erratic longitudinal movements and shorter lifetimes, directly correlating with observed photometric phase jumps and the chaotic state. Average spot temperature contrast remained stable, but spatial distribution and temporal dynamics changed drastically. Conclusions. This study provides direct spectroscopic evidence for the breakdown of a stable dynamo regime on LQ Hya, transitioning to a more complex, irregular magnetic activity pattern. Disappearance of coherent high-latitude spots and emergence of fragmented, rapidly evolving features explain the photometric irregularities, offering unique insight into stellar dynamo variability.

Recently, it has been observed to show intriguing behaviour by analysing long-term photometry: during 2003--2009, a coherent spot structure migrating in the rotational frame has been reported by various authors, but since that time the star has entered a chaotic state where coherent structures seem to have disappeared and rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima occur irregularly over time.

title: Funnel control -- a survey
text_ai: The methodology of funnel control was introduced in the early 2000s, and it has developed since then in many respects achieving a level of mathematical maturity balanced by practical applications. Its fundamental tenet is the attainment of prescribed transient and asymptotic behaviour for continuous-time controlled dynamical processes encompassing linear and nonlinear systems described by functional differential equations, differential-algebraic systems, and partial differential equations. A defining characteristic of funnel control is its ability to guarantee that the system output remains within a pre-defined, time-varying performance funnel, thereby ensuring desired transient performance and robustness against uncertainties and disturbances without requiring precise knowledge of system parameters or explicit disturbance models. This makes it particularly attractive for complex systems operating in uncertain environments. The underlying methodology typically involves a high-gain feedback mechanism, often adaptive, that dynamically adjusts the control input to keep the output error within the shrinking or expanding funnel boundaries. Over the past two decades, the initial framework has been significantly extended to address a multitude of challenging control problems. These extensions include output feedback funnel control, adaptive funnel control for systems with unknown parameters, distributed funnel control for multi-agent systems, and implementations for systems with time delays, input constraints, or event-triggered communication. Practical applications span a wide range of engineering domains, from robotics and aerospace to chemical processes and biomedical systems, demonstrating its versatility and effectiveness in real-world scenarios. This survey provides a comprehensive review of the theoretical advancements, algorithmic developments, and diverse practical applications of funnel control, consolidating key results and identifying promising avenues for future research.

title: Scaling Universality at the Dynamic Vortex Mott Transition
text_ai: The dynamic Mott insulator-to-metal transition (DMT) is key to many intriguing phenomena in condensed matter physics yet it remains nearly unexplored. The cleanest way to observe DMT, without the interference from disorder and other effects inherent to electronic and atomic systems, is to employ the vortex Mott states formed by superconducting vortices in a regular array of pinning sites. Here, we present a comprehensive study of the dynamic vortex Mott transition (DVMT) in such an ideal system. By systematically varying an external driving force, we induce a critical transition from an insulating-like state, where vortices are localized by pinning, to a metallic-like state characterized by collective vortex flow. Through extensive numerical simulations and theoretical modeling, we precisely characterize the critical behavior of this transition. Our results reveal robust scaling universality in the current-voltage characteristics and dynamic correlations near the DVMT. We identify a unique set of critical exponents that govern the transition, demonstrating their independence from microscopic details of the pinning landscape and vortex interactions. These findings establish the DVMT as a distinct universality class for non-equilibrium phase transitions in periodically driven systems, providing profound insights into the fundamental mechanisms underlying dynamic Mott phenomena and offering a general framework for their analysis across diverse physical platforms.

title: Optimal strategies for throwing accurately
text_ai: Accuracy of throwing in games and sports is governed by how errors at projectile release are propagated by flight dynamics. To address the question of what governs the choice of throwing strategy, we use a simple model of throwing with an arm modelled as a hinged bar of fixed length that can release a projectile at any angle and angular velocity. We define throwing accuracy as the inverse of the variance of the projectile's landing position at a specified target. Through a sensitivity analysis, we systematically investigate how small perturbations in release parameters (angle, speed, and arm angular velocity) propagate to the final landing error. Our optimization framework identifies strategies that minimize this variance for various throwing distances and target configurations, subject to biomechanical constraints such as maximum arm angular velocity. The results reveal that optimal accuracy is not achieved by simply maximizing release velocity or range. Instead, it critically depends on minimizing the propagation of intrinsic neuromuscular noise. We demonstrate distinct optimal release strategies for different throwing tasks: shorter, precise throws often favor release points where the trajectory is less sensitive to angular errors, while longer throws necessitate higher speeds, making them more vulnerable to velocity-related inaccuracies. This model provides a theoretical foundation for understanding the complex interplay between biomechanical constraints, error propagation, and the selection of effective throwing strategies in human motor control, offering insights applicable to sports training and rehabilitation.

title: Is the faint young Sun problem for Earth solved?
text_ai: Stellar evolution models predict that the solar luminosity was lower in the past, typically 20-25 % lower during the Archean (3.8-2.5 Ga). Despite the fainter Sun, there is strong evidence for the presence of liquid water on Earth's surface at that time. This discrepancy constitutes the "faint young Sun problem," a long-standing paradox in Earth and planetary science. Numerous hypotheses have been proposed to reconcile this apparent contradiction, primarily invoking an enhanced greenhouse effect. Higher atmospheric concentrations of CO2 and CH4 are widely cited mechanisms to maintain surface temperatures above freezing. Other proposed solutions include a lower planetary albedo from reduced cloud cover or less extensive continental ice sheets, and potentially different atmospheric pressure or composition. Recent studies also explore the roles of other potent greenhouse gases like N2O or OCS, and alternative atmospheric circulation regimes. However, geological and geochemical proxies for Archean atmospheric CO2 and CH4 levels present challenges, with some estimates suggesting insufficient concentrations to fully compensate for reduced solar forcing. Furthermore, the stability of such a climate system and the evolution of greenhouse gas sources and sinks throughout the Archean remain subjects of active debate. This paper critically reviews the leading hypotheses for resolving the faint young Sun problem, evaluating their consistency with geological, astrophysical, and climate modeling constraints. We assess whether current solutions comprehensively account for Archean warmth and discuss remaining uncertainties required to definitively conclude if this fundamental paradox is truly resolved.

title: H-Alpha and Hard X-Ray Observations of a Two-Ribbon Flare Associated with a Filament Eruption
text_ai: We perform a multi-wavelength study of a two-ribbon flare on 2002 September 29 and its associated filament eruption, observed simultaneously in the H-alpha line by a ground-based imaging spectrograph and in hard X-rays by RHESSI. The flare ribbons contain several H-alpha bright kernels that show different evolutional behaviors. We find that these kernels exhibit both impulsive, short-lived brightenings and more gradual, sustained emission, often appearing at the footpoints of newly reconnected magnetic field lines. Hard X-ray sources observed by RHESSI are predominantly located near these H-alpha kernels, particularly those displaying rapid temporal variations. A strong correlation is established between the hard X-ray flux and the H-alpha intensity of specific kernels, providing direct evidence for non-thermal electron precipitation as a significant driver of chromospheric heating and optical emission in these regions. The filament eruption precedes the main impulsive phase, suggesting its destabilization triggers the large-scale magnetic reconnection responsible for the flare. Our analysis reveals the intricate relationship between the erupting filament, the evolving flare ribbons, and the sites of energetic particle acceleration, offering insights into the energy release and transport mechanisms in two-ribbon flares.

title: Strategic Defense against Stealthy Link Flooding Attacks: A Signaling Game Approach
text_ai: With the increasing diversity of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, it is becoming extremely challenging to design a fully protected network. For instance, Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA) is a variant of DDoS attacks that strives to block access to a target area by flooding a small set of links, and it is shown that it can bypass traditional DDoS defense mechanisms. To counter this critical vulnerability, we propose a novel strategic defense framework leveraging a signaling game. Stealthy Link Flooding Attacks inherently involve significant information asymmetry, where the attacker possesses private information regarding its capabilities and chosen target links, while the defender operates under uncertainty about the attack's nature, intensity, and optimal resource allocation. Our model features a rational attacker and a network defender. The attacker's type encompasses its resource budget and stealth capabilities, influencing its selection of links to flood and the intensity of the attack. Conversely, the defender's type reflects its monitoring capabilities and available defense resources. The attacker's actions involve choosing a subset of links to target and the rate of flooding, aiming to maximize disruption while minimizing the probability of detection. The defender's actions include strategically allocating surveillance and mitigation resources across potential target links and deciding on the level of response upon detecting suspicious activity. Payoffs are defined to reflect the attacker's objective of maximizing network disruption and minimizing attack costs, and the defender's goal of minimizing network damage and resource expenditure. We characterize the Perfect Bayesian Equilibria of this signaling game, revealing optimal strategies for both the attacker and the defender under various conditions. Our analysis demonstrates how the attacker's choice of stealth level and attack intensity can signal its underlying type, thereby influencing the defender's resource allocation decisions. Crucially, we identify conditions under which a separating equilibrium emerges, enabling the defender to infer the attacker's type and mount a more tailored and efficient defense. We also explore pooling equilibria, where different attacker types employ similar strategies, presenting greater challenges for detection and mitigation. The findings provide significant insights into designing adaptive and proactive defense mechanisms that explicitly account for attacker rationality and information asymmetry. This work contributes a robust game-theoretic framework for understanding and mitigating sophisticated, stealthy network attacks, offering practical guidance for network security architects to strategically allocate defense resources and develop more resilient network architectures against evolving threats.

For instance, Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA) is a variant of DDoS attacks that strives to block access to a target area by flooding a small set of links, and it is shown that it can bypass traditional DDoS defense mechanisms.

title: A Latent Variable Approach for Non-Hierarchical Multi-Fidelity Adaptive Sampling
text_ai: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods are gaining popularity for enhancing surrogate modeling and design optimization by incorporating data from various low-fidelity (LF) models. While most existing MF methods assume a fixed dataset, adaptive sampling methods that dynamically allocate resources among fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in the exploring and exploiting the design space. However, current adaptive MF strategies often presuppose a hierarchical structure among fidelity levels, limiting their applicability to scenarios with diverse, non-hierarchical fidelity sources. To address this, we propose a novel **latent variable approach** for **non-hierarchical multi-fidelity adaptive sampling**. Our method models the complex, non-linear relationships between various fidelity levels by projecting them into a lower-dimensional latent space. This latent representation captures the underlying commonalities and discrepancies among different fidelity sources without imposing rigid hierarchical assumptions. By learning these latent variables, our framework can effectively leverage information from disparate, potentially conflicting, low-fidelity models, which might not be ordered in a clear hierarchy of accuracy or cost. The latent variable model is then integrated into an adaptive sampling strategy. It quantifies the uncertainty associated with the high-fidelity (HF) response surface and guides the sequential selection of new samples. The strategy dynamically determines not only the optimal location in the design space to query but also the most informative fidelity level at which to perform the evaluation. This resource allocation is optimized by considering both the acquisition cost and the expected reduction in uncertainty or improvement in the objective function, as inferred from the latent space. This allows for efficient exploration of the design space and exploitation of promising regions, even when the relationships between fidelities are intricate and non-hierarchical. We demonstrate the superior performance and robustness of our approach across several benchmark problems, showcasing its ability to significantly reduce the number of expensive high-fidelity evaluations required to achieve a desired level of accuracy compared to state-of-the-art hierarchical and non-hierarchical MF methods.

title: Clinical Significance of Cytotoxic Lesions of the Corpus Callosum in Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Patients: A Retrospective Analysis.
text_ai: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum are secondary lesions induced by significant increases in cytokine levels in the brain and are associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). However, their clinical significance in SAH patients remains unclear. This retrospective study aimed to delineate the prevalence, radiological characteristics, and clinical implications of CLCC in a cohort of SAH patients. We retrospectively analyzed medical records and neuroimaging data (CT/MRI) from 215 SAH patients admitted between 2018-2022. Patients were categorized by CLCC presence, identified via diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) restriction and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) changes. Clinical variables collected included Hunt-Hess and modified Fisher grades, incidence of delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI), vasospasm, and 3-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) outcomes. Statistical analyses compared groups and identified independent predictors of CLCC and their prognostic value. CLCC were identified in 38 (17.7%) patients. Those with CLCC exhibited significantly higher Hunt-Hess and Fisher grades (p<0.001), greater incidence of vasospasm (68.4% vs. 32.7%, p<0.001), and more frequent DCI (47.4% vs. 18.9%, p<0.001). Importantly, CLCC independently predicted poorer 3-month neurological outcomes (mRS > 3; Adjusted OR 3.21, 95% CI 1.68-6.14, p<0.001), prolonged intensive care unit stays (median 18 vs. 10 days, p<0.001), and increased hospital mortality (26.3% vs. 9.4%, p<0.01). Our findings indicate CLCC are not uncommon in SAH patients and signify more severe disease, increased DCI risk, and independently predict poorer long-term neurological outcomes and higher mortality. Early CLCC identification on neuroimaging aids risk stratification and may guide more aggressive management, highlighting their critical prognostic value.

title: ALMA-IMF XVI: Mass-averaged temperature of cores and protostellar luminosities in the ALMA-IMF protoclusters
text_ai: ALMA-IMF imaged 15 massive protoclusters down to a resolution of of 2 kau scales, identifying about 1000 star-forming cores. The mass and luminosity of these cores, which are fundamental physical characteristics, are difficult to determine, a problem greatly exacerbated at the distances >2 kpc of ALMA-IMF protoclusters. To overcome this, we present a novel method to derive the mass-averaged core temperature from their continuum emission at 1.3 mm and 3 mm. By combining these observations with a dust opacity model, we simultaneously constrain core masses and temperatures, mitigating the degeneracy often encountered in single-band measurements. Ancillary multi-wavelength data are used to estimate bolometric luminosities of embedded protostars. Our analysis reveals a median mass-averaged core temperature of 20 K, with a significant spread from 15 K to 40 K. We find a clear trend of increasing core temperature with increasing core mass, suggesting efficient heating in the most massive cores. Cores hosting embedded protostars also exhibit systematically higher temperatures compared to quiescent cores. The derived protostellar luminosities span several orders of magnitude, from <1 L$_\odot$ to >10$^4$ L$_\odot$, reflecting diverse evolutionary stages and stellar masses. We observe a strong correlation between core mass and protostellar luminosity, consistent with accretion-driven growth. The luminosity function of embedded protostars in these protoclusters is presented and compared with theoretical predictions. These findings provide crucial insights into the thermal properties of massive star-forming cores and early massive protostellar evolution. The observed temperature gradients and luminosity distributions offer strong constraints for models of radiative feedback and accretion processes in high-mass star formation, highlighting the complex interplay between core structure and protostellar activity.

The mass and luminosity of these cores, which are fundamental physical characteristics, are difficult to determine, a problem greatly exacerbated at the distances >2 kpc of ALMA-IMF protoclusters.

title: Genetic engineering and characterisation of chlorotoxin-fused gelonin for enhanced glioblastoma therapy.
text_ai: Despite substantial advances in its treatment, brain cancer remains a life-threatening disease with a poor survival rate. The main challenges for the conventional chemotherapy include an insufficient efficacy of drugs and toxicity caused by their nonselective mode of action. To address these limitations, we genetically engineered a novel immunotoxin, chlorotoxin-fused gelonin (CTX-GEL). Chlorotoxin (CTX) was selected for its selective glioblastoma cell binding and blood-brain barrier permeability; gelonin (GEL) provides potent ribosome-inactivating cytotoxicity. This fusion aims for targeted delivery of a powerful payload, enhancing efficacy and reducing systemic toxicity. The CTX-GEL construct was expressed and purified from *E. coli*. *In vitro* characterisation confirmed its specific binding to glioblastoma cell lines (e.g., U87-MG), demonstrating enhanced cellular uptake and potent cytotoxicity compared to free gelonin. Minimal toxicity towards non-cancerous cells was observed, underscoring chlorotoxin-mediated targeting's effectiveness in inducing robust glioblastoma cell death. This genetically engineered fusion protein represents a promising, selective therapeutic agent with strong potential to improve glioblastoma treatment outcomes.

title: Sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of xylazine with and without acepromazine in Nordestino donkeys.
text_ai: Information on appropriate protocols for sedation of Nordestino donkeys is scarce. To evaluate the sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of intravenous (i.v.) xylazine with and without acepromazine in 'Nordestino' donkeys. Seven healthy female Nordestino donkeys (150 ± 18 kg) were included in this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment. Each donkey received two treatments with a 7-day washout period: XYL (0.3 mg/kg i.v. xylazine) and XYL-ACE (0.3 mg/kg i.v. xylazine + 0.03 mg/kg i.v. acepromazine). Sedation depth was assessed via a 5-point subjective scale; cardiorespiratory parameters (heart rate, respiratory rate, non-invasive mean arterial pressure, peripheral oxygen saturation, rectal temperature) were recorded at baseline and intervals for 120 minutes. Data were analysed using repeated measures ANOVA (P < 0.05). Both treatments induced mild to moderate sedation, but XYL-ACE produced significantly deeper and longer-lasting effects (P < 0.01). Onset was rapid for both protocols. Cardiorespiratory parameters remained within physiological limits, though a transient, clinically acceptable decrease in heart rate and mean arterial pressure was observed, more pronounced with XYL-ACE. Respiratory rate and SpO2 remained stable and comparable between groups. In conclusion, the combination of low-dose xylazine and acepromazine provides superior and more prolonged sedation in Nordestino donkeys compared to xylazine alone, with minimal and clinically acceptable cardiorespiratory depression. This protocol offers a safe and effective option for short diagnostic or minor therapeutic procedures in this species.
