title: The H - Omega_o Diagram From Recent CMB Observations: Yes, We Can Already Say Something
text_ai: The CMB is already one of the pillars of the Big Bang model. However it may also become our most powerful tool to distinguish contending models and to determine their cosmological parameters. To realize this goal, more than 20 observational groups and two new satellites are gearing up to make precise measurements of the CMB at small angular scales. Current measurements of the CMB angular power spectrum, particularly the precise locations and amplitudes of its acoustic peaks at small angular scales, are already yielding significant cosmological insights. These features are exquisitely sensitive to fundamental cosmological parameters, including the total matter density ($\Omega_o$) and the Hubble constant ($H_0$). The interplay between these parameters dictates the sound horizon at recombination, which in turn sets the characteristic angular scale of the CMB anisotropies, allowing for powerful degeneracy breaking when combined with other cosmological probes. This paper leverages recent high-resolution CMB anisotropy data, primarily from the WMAP satellite and ground-based experiments like ACBAR and CBI, to explore the degeneracy between $H_0$ and $\Omega_o$. We construct the $H_0 - \Omega_o$ diagram, mapping the likelihood contours derived solely from current CMB observations. By analyzing the shifts in the angular scale of the first acoustic peak and the damping tail, we delineate the regions of this parameter space consistent with existing data. Our analysis demonstrates that even with current data, robust constraints can be placed on the $H_0 - \Omega_o$ plane. Specifically, we show that models with a low Hubble constant and high matter density are already strongly disfavored. The results strongly favor a spatially flat universe and are highly consistent with the $\Lambda$CDM concordance model, providing independent support for its parameters without relying on external datasets like supernovae or galaxy clustering.

title: Funding pharmacists in general practice: A feasibility study to inform the design of future economic evaluations.
text_ai: Funding is a significant barrier to employing general practice pharmacists. To explore the feasibility of determining the cost-benefit of pharmacists in Australian general practice. Two part-time pharmacists were employed by general practices in Canberra, Australia. Diaries of the pharmacists were analysed to determine time worked and participation in income-generating activities, including Government-funded programs: Asthma Cycle of Care, Home Medicine Reviews, and Health Care Assessments. General practitioner (GP) and practice nurse (PN) time saved by pharmacist interventions was estimated via weekly surveys. Patient consultations and practice revenue from these activities were also recorded. Over six months, pharmacists averaged 15 hours/week. They conducted 18 Home Medicine Reviews and 25 Asthma Cycle of Care services, generating AUD $3,200 for practices. GPs reported saving an average of 2 hours/week on medication-related tasks. However, income-generating activity was limited by billing restrictions and administrative burden. Key challenges included workflow integration and sustainable funding identification. This study confirms the feasibility of data collection for future economic evaluations, yet highlights current income generation limitations. Future evaluations must quantify indirect benefits (GP time savings, patient outcomes) and explore alternative funding models for sustainable integration.

title: CorrectNav: Self-Correction Flywheel Empowers Vision-Language-Action Navigation Model
text_ai: Existing vision-and-language navigation models often deviate from the correct trajectory when executing instructions. However, these models lack effective error correction capability, hindering their recovery from errors. To address this challenge, we propose Self-correction Flywheel, a novel post-training paradigm. This paradigm enables models to continuously identify and rectify navigational errors via an iterative feedback loop. Upon detecting deviations, the flywheel mechanism triggers a self-correction process, generating refined actions to guide the agent back onto the optimal path. Our proposed CorrectNav model integrates this Self-correction Flywheel, leveraging multi-modal perception to detect discrepancies and dynamic re-planning to synthesize corrective actions. This significantly enhances robustness against environmental variations and planning inaccuracies, fostering superior error recovery. Evaluated on challenging vision-and-language navigation benchmarks (R2R, RxR), CorrectNav consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods by a substantial margin in success rate and navigation efficiency. Our results highlight its transformative potential for building reliable, adaptable autonomous navigation agents.

title: Quantile LSTM: A Robust LSTM for Anomaly Detection In Time Series Data
text_ai: Anomalies refer to the departure of systems and devices from their normal behaviour in standard operating conditions. An anomaly in an industrial device can indicate an upcoming failure, often in the temporal direction. In this paper, we make two contributions: 1) we estimate conditional quantiles and consider three different ways to define anomalies based on the estimated quantiles. These definitions leverage point predictions and uncertainty bounds, yielding flexible, adaptive anomaly thresholds that surpass fixed limits. 2) we propose Quantile Long Short-Term Memory (QLSTM), a novel deep learning architecture specifically designed for robust conditional quantile estimation in time series. Unlike traditional LSTMs predicting mean values, QLSTM directly learns multiple quantiles via a pinball loss function. This inherently captures the conditional distribution, ensuring robustness to noise, outliers, and non-Gaussian data typical in industrial time series. The full predictive distribution enables dynamic anomaly threshold adjustment. Evaluated on challenging industrial time series datasets, QLSTM demonstrates superior effectiveness in detecting point and contextual anomalies compared to state-of-the-art methods, highlighting enhanced robustness and accuracy for proactive maintenance.

title: Reverberation and photoionization estimates of the Broad Line Region Radius in Low-z Quasars
text_ai: Black Hole Mass (M_BH) estimation in quasars, especially at high redshift, involves use of single epoch spectra with s/n and resolution that permit accurate measurement of the width of a broad line assumed to be a reliable virial estimator. Coupled with an estimate of the radius of the broad line region this yields M_BH. This critical Broad Line Region (BLR) radius, R_BLR, is traditionally determined through the time-intensive technique of reverberation mapping (RM), which measures the light travel time delay between continuum variations and broad emission line responses. While RM provides the most direct measurement of R_BLR, its observational demands limit its application primarily to low-redshift (z < 0.3) quasars. For the vast majority of high-redshift quasars, R_BLR is instead inferred from a luminosity-radius relation (R_BLR-L), calibrated using RM data from local objects. However, uncertainties in this scaling relation propagate directly into M_BH errors. This paper addresses these challenges by employing an alternative method: detailed photoionization modeling of broad emission lines. We apply this technique to a sample of low-redshift quasars, for many of which independent RM R_BLR estimates are also available. By comparing the R_BLR derived from photoionization models with those from reverberation mapping, we critically assess the consistency and accuracy of the photoionization method. Our findings provide insights into the physical structure of the BLR and offer a robust validation of photoionization modeling as a tool for R_BLR estimation. This work aims to refine the R_BLR-L relation and improve the reliability of M_BH estimations for high-redshift quasars, where direct RM is currently unfeasible, ultimately enhancing our understanding of black hole growth across cosmic time.

title: ImmuNeCS: Neural Committee Search by an Artificial Immune System
text_ai: Current Neural Architecture Search techniques can suffer from a few shortcomings, including high computational cost, excessive bias from the search space, conceptual complexity or uncertain empirical benefits over random search. To address these limitations, we introduce ImmuNeCS, a novel Neural Committee Search method inspired by Artificial Immune Systems (AIS). It leverages AIS's diversity-seeking and adaptive capabilities to efficiently explore the neural architecture search space. Unlike conventional NAS, which seeks a single optimal architecture, ImmuNeCS discovers a robust *committee* of diverse, complementary neural networks. Candidate architectures, as 'antibodies,' evolve via 'antigen recognition' based on task performance. Clonal selection and affinity maturation foster diverse, high-performing architectures. This bio-inspired approach balances exploration and exploitation, promoting diversity and mitigating premature convergence. Evolving a committee, not a monolithic model, inherently builds robustness and improves generalization. We extensively evaluate ImmuNeCS on challenging image classification tasks, demonstrating its ability to discover high-performing and diverse neural committees. Our results show ImmuNeCS achieves competitive or superior performance against state-of-the-art NAS, with substantial computational overhead reductions. Furthermore, ImmuNeCS ensembles exhibit enhanced predictive accuracy and reliability across various benchmarks. This work proposes an elegant and effective NAS paradigm, shifting focus from single-model optimization to harnessing the collective intelligence and robustness of diverse neural committees.

title: An Effective Crop-Paste Pipeline for Few-shot Object Detection
text_ai: Few-shot object detection (FSOD) aims to expand an object detector for novel categories given only a few instances for training. However, detecting novel categories with only a few samples usually leads to the problem of misclassification. In FSOD, we notice the false positive (FP) of novel categories is prominent, in which the base categories are often recognized as novel ones. This prominence of false positives stems from severe novel class data scarcity, leading to ambiguous feature learning and poor discrimination against visually similar base categories. To address this, we propose an effective Crop-Paste Pipeline synthesizing diverse, realistic training instances for novel categories. Our pipeline meticulously extracts novel objects, intelligently selects backgrounds, and employs advanced blending for seamless integration. Crucially, it generates 'hard' synthetic samples by varying object scales, orientations, and contextual placements. These samples improve the detector's ability to distinguish novel objects from base categories or clutter. By expanding the novel feature space with robust, discriminative examples, our pipeline effectively reduces misclassification and significantly mitigates the false positive problem. Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC and MS COCO demonstrate our Crop-Paste Pipeline consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance, boosting novel category detection accuracy and ensuring robust false positive suppression, leading to more reliable FSOD models.

title: QCD against BlackHoles of Stellar Mass
text_ai: In course of the consolidation of nucleon (neutron) spacing inside a compact star, two key factors are expected to come into play side by side: the lack of self-stabilization against shutting into black hole (BH) and forthcoming phase transition - color deconfinement and QCD-vacuum reconstruction - within the nuclear matter the star is composed of. As the central density surpasses typical nuclear saturation, the strong interaction, governed by Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), predicts a fundamental phase transition where nucleons lose their individual identities. Quarks and gluons become deconfined, forming a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) or other forms of exotic quark matter. This transition is hypothesized to be accompanied by a profound modification of the equation of state (EoS) of matter, as well as a reconstruction of the QCD vacuum within the star's core. Crucially, the emergence of a stiff EoS at ultra-high densities, characteristic of deconfined quark matter, can generate an immense outward pressure. This QCD-driven pressure acts as a potent counterforce against the relentless gravitational pull, potentially halting the gravitational collapse that would otherwise lead to the formation of a stellar-mass black hole (BH). Instead, this mechanism may stabilize the compact object at densities beyond those of conventional neutron stars, giving rise to exotic remnants such as quark stars or hybrid stars. Such objects would possess distinct mass-radius relations and gravitational wave signatures compared to both neutron stars and black holes. This work employs theoretical models, incorporating insights from effective field theories and lattice QCD, to investigate the critical conditions for this phase transition and its impact on the stability of ultra-dense matter. We explore how the emergent QCD pressure modifies the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equations, establishing potential new maximum mass limits for compact stars and thereby challenging the conventional understanding of BH formation. The astrophysical implications for gravitational wave events and electromagnetic observations are discussed, proposing discriminative signatures to test the 'QCD against BH' hypothesis.

title: Do people's user types change over time? An exploratory study
text_ai: In recent years, different studies have proposed and validated user models (e.g., Bartle, BrainHex, and Hexad) to represent the different user profiles in games and gamified settings. However, the results of applying these user models in practice (e.g., to personalize gamified systems) are still contradictory. A critical gap in this research is the unexamined assumption that user types remain stable over extended periods, despite the known fluidity of human preferences and behaviors. This exploratory study investigates the temporal dynamics of user types through a longitudinal analysis. We recruited 120 participants from an online learning environment and administered the Hexad user type questionnaire at three separate points over a six-month duration. Our analysis, employing both individual and group-level comparisons, revealed significant shifts in primary and secondary user types for a notable proportion of participants (approximately 60%). These changes suggest that user types are not static labels but dynamic profiles evolving with prolonged engagement. The findings challenge the conventional static application of user models, highlighting the need for adaptive personalization strategies and dynamic user modeling approaches to ensure sustained engagement and effectiveness in gamified systems. This research provides a foundational understanding for future studies on user experience evolution.

title: Depinning and flow of a vortex line in an uniaxial random medium
text_ai: We study numerically and analytically the dynamics of a single directed elastic string driven through a 3-dimensional disordered medium. In the quasistatic limit the string is super-rough in the driving direction, with roughness exponent $\zeta_{\parallel} = 1.25\pm 0.01$, dynamic exponent $z_{\parallel}= 1.43 \pm 0.01$, correlation-length exponent $\nu= 1.33 \pm 0.02$, depinning exponent $\beta = 0.24\pm 0.01$, and avalanche-size exponent $\tau_{\parallel} = 1.09 \pm 0.03$. The depinning transition is found to be continuous, characterized by scale-free avalanches whose size distribution follows a power law with exponent $\tau_{\parallel}$. Beyond the critical force $F_c$, the string enters a steady-state flow regime where its average velocity $v$ scales as $(F-F_c)^\beta$. A key aspect of our study is the uniaxial nature of the three-dimensional random medium, which introduces an anisotropic quenched disorder potential. This anisotropy profoundly influences the string's transverse fluctuations, leading to distinct scaling properties in directions parallel and perpendicular to the uniaxial axis. Specifically, we observe that while the string remains super-rough in the driving direction, its transverse roughness exhibits anisotropic scaling, departing significantly from the isotropic Edwards-Wilkinson class or other known universality classes for isotropic disorder. This anisotropic scaling manifests in different roughness exponents for transverse directions aligned with and perpendicular to the uniaxial axis, highlighting the directional dependence of pinning forces. Our analytical framework, employing a functional renormalization group (FRG) approach, provides theoretical predictions for these exponents and their associated scaling relations, which are in excellent agreement with our extensive numerical simulations. These findings establish a novel universality class for the depinning and creep dynamics of elastic lines in anisotropic quenched disorder, offering critical insights into phenomena such as vortex motion in layered superconductors or the dynamics of domain walls in materials with directional pinning sites.

title: Palette-colouring: a belief-propagation approach
text_ai: We consider a variation of the prototype combinatorial-optimisation problem known as graph-colouring. Our optimisation goal is to colour the vertices of a graph with a fixed number of colours, in a way to maximise the number of different colours present in the set of nearest neighbours of each given vertex. This objective, distinct from traditional graph-colouring's aim of preventing same-coloured adjacent vertices, prioritises local colour diversity. Recognising the NP-hard nature of palette-colouring and intractability of exact solutions for large graphs, we propose a novel approximate approach leveraging Belief Propagation (BP). Our contribution is a tailored BP message-passing scheme effectively propagating local colour diversity requirements. The framework iteratively updates beliefs for optimal colour assignments, considering neighbourhood palette richness. We evaluate our BP algorithm against exact methods on small instances and heuristics on larger graphs. Results demonstrate its efficiency and solution quality, establishing the BP framework as a scalable, effective method for high local colour diversity in networks.
prefix: We consider a variation of the prototype combinatorial-optimisation problem known as graph-colouring. Our optimisation goal is to colour the vertices of a graph with a fixed number of colours, in a way to maximise the number of different colours present in the set of nearest neighbours of each given vertex.

title: Does the Presence of Risk Factors for Fetal Growth Restriction Increase the Probability of Antenatal Detection? A French National Study.
text_ai: Screening for fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a major component of prenatal care. We investigated whether the presence of maternal and pregnancy risk factors for FGR improves the antenatal suspicion of FGR for infants born small-for-gestational age (SGA) as well as their impact on screening specificity. We conducted a secondary analysis of the 2016 French National Perinatal Survey data, including 12,187 singleton live births at ≥22 weeks’ gestation. FGR risk factors were identified from maternal history and pregnancy characteristics. Antenatal FGR suspicion was defined by documented diagnosis in medical charts. SGA was defined as birth weight <10th percentile for gestational age and sex, using French national growth curves. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between risk factors and antenatal FGR suspicion among SGA infants, adjusting for potential confounders. We also calculated screening sensitivity and specificity, stratified by the number of identified risk factors. Overall, 9.2% of SGA infants had documented antenatal FGR suspicion. The presence of at least one FGR risk factor significantly increased the odds of antenatal FGR suspicion among SGA infants (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.87; 95% CI 1.62–2.15). Specifically, maternal chronic hypertension (aOR 2.51; 95% CI 1.78–3.55) and previous FGR (aOR 3.12; 95% CI 2.20–4.43) were strong predictors. While sensitivity for detecting SGA infants with FGR suspicion modestly improved with increasing numbers of risk factors (from 28.5% with no risk factors to 38.1% with ≥2 risk factors), the overall specificity of antenatal FGR screening remained high (91.5%), with only a slight decrease in specificity observed in the presence of multiple risk factors. Our findings indicate that while specific FGR risk factors moderately improve the antenatal detection of FGR among SGA infants, this improvement is limited. The overall specificity of current screening practices remains suboptimal. These results underscore the ongoing challenge in accurately identifying FGR antenatally and highlight the need for more effective screening strategies.

title: TeraHertz Band Communication: An Old Problem Revisited and Research Directions for the Next Decade
text_ai: Terahertz (THz) band communications are envisioned as a key technology for 6G and Beyond. As a fundamental wireless infrastructure, THz communication can boost abundant promising applications. In 2014, our team published two comprehensive roadmaps for the development and progress of THz communication networks [1], [2], which helped the research community to start research on this subject afterwards. Since then, despite significant advancements in device technology and channel modeling, fundamental challenges persist, including severe path loss, power inefficiency, and complex channels, hindering deployment. This paper critically revisits these 'old problems,' assessing solutions proposed over the past decade and highlighting persistent bottlenecks in THz communication. We provide a comprehensive overview of the current state-of-the-art, covering breakthroughs in transceiver design, signal processing, and networking paradigms. Finally, we delineate key research directions for the next decade, encompassing reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, ultra-massive MIMO, AI-driven resource management, and integrated sensing and communication, to unlock THz's full potential for 6G and beyond.

title: Reproductive Coercion Among African American Female Adolescents: Associations with Contraception and Sexually Transmitted Diseases.
text_ai: Background: Among adolescents, racial disparities in reproductive health outcomes persist. The question of whether reproductive coercion (RC) influences these outcomes has received increased attention. Little is known about whether RC is independently associated with contraceptive use and having a sexually transmitted disease (STD) among African American female adolescents. This study aimed to examine the prevalence of RC and its independent associations with both current contraceptive use and lifetime STD diagnosis among African American female adolescents. Utilizing data from the National Survey of Family Growth (2015-2019 cycle), this study analyzed a nationally representative sample of 850 sexually experienced African American female adolescents aged 15-19. RC was assessed via a validated scale; current contraceptive use and self-reported lifetime STD diagnosis were primary outcomes. Logistic regression models determined independent associations, adjusting for key sociodemographic confounders including age, education, and poverty level. Findings indicated that 18.5% of African American female adolescents reported experiencing some form of RC. After controlling for confounders, RC was significantly associated with lower odds of current contraceptive use (AOR = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.48-0.89, p < .01) and significantly higher odds of a lifetime STD diagnosis (AOR = 1.87, 95% CI: 1.32-2.65, p < .001). These associations highlight RC's detrimental impact on reproductive health. These findings underscore the urgent need for targeted interventions to screen for and address reproductive coercion among African American female adolescents. Integrating RC screening into routine adolescent health visits could mitigate adverse reproductive health outcomes and promote autonomy.

title: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to Parameter Selection for Distributed Optimal Power Flow
text_ai: With the increasing penetration of distributed energy resources, distributed optimization algorithms have attracted significant attention for power systems applications due to their potential for superior scalability, privacy, and robustness to a single point-of-failure. The Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is a popular distributed optimization algorithm; however, its convergence performance is highly dependent on the selection of penalty parameters, which are usually chosen heuristically. This heuristic approach often leads to suboptimal convergence rates or even divergence, requiring significant manual tuning. To address this, this paper proposes a novel reinforcement learning (RL) framework for adaptive and autonomous selection of ADMM penalty parameters. An RL agent observes the optimization state, defined by primal and dual residuals, and selects optimal parameters as actions. The reward function minimizes convergence iterations while ensuring solution accuracy, enabling a dynamic adjustment policy adaptable to varying network conditions. Applied to the Distributed Optimal Power Flow (D-OPF) problem, simulation results demonstrate that the RL approach significantly accelerates ADMM convergence, reduces computational burden, and improves the robustness of D-OPF solutions compared to fixed or manually tuned parameters, showcasing its practical potential.

title: Non-union of the ulnar styloid process in children is common but long-term morbidity is rare: a population-based study with mean 11 years (9-15) follow-up.
text_ai: Background and purpose - Fracture of the ulnar styloid process (USP) is common in children in connection with distal radius fracture. The long-term morbidity of USP non-union following a childhood distal radius fracture is unclear. We evaluated long-term clinical and radiographic findings of USP non-union. A population-based cohort of 267 children (age <16 years) with a distal radius fracture including a USP fracture, treated between 2002 and 2006, was identified from a regional fracture registry. Patients were invited for clinical and radiographic follow-up at a mean of 11 years (range 9-15) post-injury. Clinical assessment included questionnaires on pain, functional limitations, and patient-reported outcomes (e.g., Patient-Rated Wrist Evaluation, PRWE). Radiographic evaluation involved standardized anteroposterior and lateral wrist radiographs to assess USP non-union and secondary degenerative changes. Of the 267 patients, 212 (79%) participated in the follow-up. USP non-union was radiographically confirmed in 68 patients (32%). Among these, only 5 patients (7%) reported persistent mild wrist pain or discomfort directly attributable to the non-union, and none experienced significant functional impairment or required surgical intervention related to the USP. This prevalence of symptoms was not significantly different from the group without USP non-union. Radiographic signs of osteoarthritis in the radiocarpal or distal radioulnar joint were rare and not associated with USP non-union. USP non-union is a common radiographic finding following childhood distal radius fracture, occurring in nearly one-third of cases. However, at a mean follow-up of 11 years, long-term clinical morbidity, including pain or functional limitations, is rare and generally mild. These findings suggest that USP non-union in children is largely asymptomatic and typically does not necessitate specific intervention, providing important prognostic information for clinicians and patients.

title: Distributed generalized Nash equilibria computation of monotone games via a preconditioned proximal point algorithm
text_ai: In this paper, we investigate distributed generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) computation of monotone games with affine coupling constraints. Each player can only utilize its local objective function, local feasible set and a local block of the coupling constraint, and can only communicate with its neighbours. To address this challenging distributed setting, we propose a novel algorithm leveraging a preconditioned proximal point framework. The core idea involves introducing an auxiliary variable to decouple the affine constraints, allowing each player to solve a local, simpler subproblem. The preconditioning matrix is carefully designed to accelerate convergence and improve robustness, especially when dealing with ill-conditioned problem instances. Communication is restricted to neighboring players for updating the auxiliary variable and coordinating decisions. We prove the global convergence of the proposed distributed algorithm to a GNE under standard assumptions of monotonicity and compactness. Numerical simulations illustrate the algorithm's effectiveness, scalability, and superior convergence performance compared to state-of-the-art distributed GNE computation methods, thereby demonstrating its practical applicability in large-scale multi-agent systems.

title: Illustrating the Applicability of IRT to Implementation Science: Examining an Instrument of Therapist Attitudes.
text_ai: Pragmatic instruments with psychometric support are important to advance dissemination and implementation (D&I) research, but few well-researched D&I instruments exist. Item response theory (IRT), an approach that is underutilized in D&I, can help with the development of actionable and brief instruments. This study applies IRT to a widely-used instrument measuring therapist attitudes toward evidence-based practices, illustrating its utility for D&I research. Employing a graded response model, we evaluated item characteristics, model fit, and potential for scale refinement. Analysis revealed specific items with suboptimal psychometric properties, indicating opportunities for revision or removal. Crucially, IRT facilitated identification of a parsimonious item subset maintaining strong measurement precision, offering a brief, robust alternative for D&I researchers. These findings underscore IRT's capacity to optimize measures for efficiency and accuracy, critical in resource-constrained implementation settings. We advocate for greater integration of IRT in implementation science to develop more actionable, brief, and psychometrically sound instruments, thereby enhancing D&I research and practice.

title: Visibility of current and shot noise in electrical Mach-Zehnder and Hanbury Brown Twiss interferometers
text_ai: We investigate the visibility of the current and shot-noise correlations of electrical analogs of the optical Mach-Zehnder interferometer and the Hanbury Brown Twiss interferometer. The electrical analogs are discussed in conductors subject to high magnetic fields where electron motion is along edge states. The transport quantities are modulated with the help of an Aharonov-Bohm flux. The average current and its shot noise exhibit Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in the Mach-Zehnder geometry, with visibility dependent on electron coherence. For the Hanbury Brown Twiss interferometer, two-particle shot noise correlations are investigated. Our findings reveal that current visibility in the Mach-Zehnder setup is strongly limited by dephasing, yet shot noise visibility in both interferometer types displays enhanced robustness, persisting even when average current oscillations are damped. Parameter variations (electron temperature, path imbalance, coupling strengths) further reveal this distinct sensitivity to decoherence. These results underscore fundamental differences, positioning shot noise as a more resilient probe for quantum coherence and entanglement in the quantum Hall regime, for electron interferometry and quantum information.

title: Artificial intelligence in government: Concepts, standards, and a unified framework
text_ai: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), especially in generative language modelling, hold the promise of transforming government. Given the advanced capabilities of new AI systems, it is critical that these are embedded using standard operational procedures, clear epistemic criteria, and behave in alignment with the normative expectations of society. However, the rapid adoption of AI across public sectors often outpaces the development of robust governance mechanisms, leading to significant challenges in areas such as data privacy, algorithmic bias, accountability, and public trust. Addressing this imperative, this paper first clarifies fundamental concepts underpinning AI's application in public administration, distinguishing relevant AI paradigms from predictive analytics to autonomous agents. It then critically examines existing and emerging international standards pertinent to AI development and deployment, focusing on ethics, transparency, interpretability, and cybersecurity. Building upon this conceptual and normative foundation, we propose a novel, unified framework for the responsible deployment and governance of AI systems within governmental contexts. This framework integrates technical, ethical, and governance dimensions, offering a methodology for assessing AI readiness, ensuring regulatory compliance, and fostering public engagement. It aims to provide policymakers and practitioners with actionable guidelines to develop AI strategies that are both innovative and trustworthy, promoting efficiency, fairness, and accountability. Ultimately, this work provides a foundational understanding and roadmap for governments worldwide to adopt AI responsibly, ensuring its deployment serves the public good and reinforces democratic values.

title: Status of the Medium-Sized Telescopes for the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory
text_ai: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) is a next-generation ground-based gamma-ray observatory that will study the universe at very high energy using atmospheric Cherenkov light. CTAO will comprise over 67 telescopes of three different sizes, located in the northern and southern hemispheres. The array incorporates Large, Medium (MSTs), and Small-Sized Telescopes. The MSTs, forming the backbone of CTAO's scientific program with 15 in the South and 23 in the North, are designed to cover the core energy range of 100 GeV to 10 TeV. Each MST features a 12-meter diameter dish, equipped with 90 hexagonal mirror facets, and advanced FlashCam and NectarCam camera systems utilizing silicon photomultipliers. Following successful prototyping and rigorous testing, the MST project has transitioned into production and construction. This paper provides a comprehensive update on the current status of MSTs, detailing progress in the industrialization of major subsystems: telescope structure, mirror facets, and camera assembly. We discuss challenges and solutions during pre-production and series production, focusing on quality control and performance validation. We also present the deployment schedule and initial commissioning results from the first MSTs installed at the array sites. The robust performance and ongoing progress of MSTs are crucial for realizing CTAO's unprecedented sensitivity and angular resolution, enabling groundbreaking discoveries across a wide range of astrophysical sources, and are paramount for the observatory's timely completion and scientific operations.

title: Proportional Dynamics in Linear Fisher Markets with Auto-bidding: Convergence, Incentives and Fairness
text_ai: Proportional dynamics, originated from peer-to-peer file sharing systems, models a decentralized price-learning process in Fisher markets. Previously, items in the dynamics operate independently of one another, and each is assumed to belong to a different seller. This paper extends this framework by incorporating auto-bidding strategies, where buyers algorithmically adjust bids, and considering scenarios with a single seller offering multiple items. We analyze convergence properties, demonstrating that, under mild conditions on auto-bidding algorithms, the market efficiently converges to a competitive equilibrium despite coupled buyer strategies. We investigate the incentive landscape, showing how auto-bidding affects buyer utilities and market efficiency, proposing mechanisms aligning individual incentives with system-wide optimality. Finally, we explore fairness considerations in multi-item, single-seller scenarios, characterizing fair allocations and discussing their implications for equitable resource distribution. This work provides foundational insights into decentralized algorithmic markets, bridging theoretical models with practical auto-bidding applications.

title: SL-YOLO: A Stronger and Lighter Drone Target Detection Model
text_ai: Detecting small objects in complex scenes, such as those captured by drones, is a daunting challenge due to the difficulty in capturing the complex features of small targets. While the YOLO family has achieved great success in large target detection, its performance is less than satisfactory when faced with small targets. To address these limitations, we propose SL-YOLO, a novel architecture specifically designed for robust and accurate small target detection in drone imagery. SL-YOLO incorporates an enhanced feature extraction backbone that prioritizes fine-grained information at multiple scales, coupled with an optimized feature fusion network that effectively aggregates contextual cues critical for small object recognition. Furthermore, we introduce a lightweight detection head and employ strategic model optimization techniques to significantly reduce computational complexity and parameter count, making SL-YOLO highly efficient for deployment on resource-constrained drone platforms. Extensive experiments conducted on challenging drone datasets, such as VisDrone2019-DET, demonstrate that SL-YOLO achieves state-of-the-art performance. It significantly outperforms existing YOLO variants and other leading small object detectors in terms of mean Average Precision (mAP) for small targets, while simultaneously achieving superior inference speeds. These advancements establish SL-YOLO as a highly effective and practical solution for real-time small target detection in diverse and dynamic drone surveillance and inspection scenarios.

title: Articulatory Representation Learning Via Joint Factor Analysis and Neural Matrix Factorization
text_ai: Articulatory representation learning is the fundamental research in modeling neural speech production system. Our previous work has established a deep paradigm to decompose the articulatory kinematics data into gestures, which explicitly model the phonological and linguistic structure encoded with human speech production mechanism, and corresponding gestural scores. However, achieving robust, disentangled articulatory representations that effectively separate linguistic information from speaker-specific variations remains a significant challenge for purely data-driven approaches. To overcome this, we propose a novel hybrid model that integrates Joint Factor Analysis (JFA) with Neural Matrix Factorization (NMF). JFA is employed to robustly factorize articulatory kinematics into speaker-independent phonetic content and speaker-dependent characteristics, thereby accounting for inter-speaker variability. Subsequently, NMF is applied to the speaker-independent factors to extract sparse, non-negative gestural activations and corresponding gestural prototypes, enhancing the linguistic interpretability of the learned features. Experiments conducted on the MOCHA-TIMIT articulatory dataset demonstrate that our proposed joint factor analysis and neural matrix factorization (JFA-NMF) framework yields significantly more disentangled and phonologically motivated articulatory gestures. The model achieves superior performance in reconstructing articulatory trajectories and exhibits enhanced generalization across speakers, outperforming established baselines in both objective metrics and perceptual evaluations. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of the hierarchical organization of speech motor control and offers a powerful tool for robust articulatory synthesis and analysis.

title: Prevalence of mecA on oral mucosa in patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
text_ai: Objectives: Severe oral mucositis occurring after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HCT) is associated with a risk of systemic infection related to bacteremia. We reported antibiotic-resistant bacteria detected on the oral mucosa frequently during the period of HCT and indicated an association between oral mucositis and antibiotic-resistant bacterial infection (2011 MASCC/ISOO Annual Meeting). Methicillin-resistant *Staphylococcus aureus* (MRSA), harboring the *mecA* gene, poses a serious threat in immunocompromised patients, with the oral cavity a potential reservoir during mucositis. This study aimed to determine *mecA* prevalence on HCT patients' oral mucosa, assessing longitudinal colonization and its correlation with mucositis severity and systemic infections. Oral mucosal swabs were collected weekly from 50 adult HCT recipients from pre-conditioning until neutrophil engraftment. *Staphylococcus aureus* isolates were tested for *mecA* by PCR. Direct quantitative PCR on oral rinse samples also detected *mecA*, and oral mucositis was graded daily (WHO scale). *mecA* was detected in 35% (17/50) of patients, with 10% (5/50) colonized pre-transplant. Positivity significantly increased during severe oral mucositis (WHO grade ≥ 2) versus mild/no mucositis (p<0.01). Oral *mecA* detection significantly associated with subsequent MRSA bacteremia (p<0.05), particularly in patients with severe mucositis. The oral mucosa is a significant reservoir for *mecA*-positive bacteria in HCT patients, with colonization increasing during mucositis. Monitoring *mecA* prevalence offers a valuable tool for identifying those at high risk for systemic MRSA infections.

title: $R^2$-Mesh: Reinforcement Learning Powered Mesh Reconstruction via Geometry and Appearance Refinement
text_ai: Mesh reconstruction based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) is popular in a variety of applications such as computer graphics, virtual reality, and medical imaging due to its efficiency in handling complex geometric structures and facilitating real-time rendering. However, existing works often fail to capture fine geometric details accurately and struggle with optimizing rendering quality. To address these limitations, we introduce $R^2$-Mesh, a novel reinforcement learning (RL) powered framework for high-fidelity mesh reconstruction. It employs a multi-agent RL paradigm to collaboratively refine mesh geometry and appearance. An RL agent adaptively adjusts mesh vertices and faces based on local geometric discrepancies from the NeRF representation, enhancing intricate detail capture. Simultaneously, another RL agent optimizes material properties and texture maps, guided by a perceptual rendering loss, achieving superior visual fidelity. This iterative, RL-driven refinement overcomes static optimization issues, yielding meshes with unprecedented geometric accuracy and photorealistic rendering quality. Extensive experiments demonstrate $R^2$-Mesh consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in quantitative metrics (e.g., Chamfer distance, LPIPS) and qualitative visual evaluation, producing highly detailed and visually appealing 3D models. Our work marks a significant advancement towards automated, accurate 3D reconstruction from implicit representations.

title: Multi-Tracer Correlated Stacking: A Novel Way to Discover Anisotropy in nano-Hz Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background
text_ai: The isotropic stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) generated by a population of supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs) provides a unique window into their cosmic evolution. In addition to the isotropic power spectrum, the anisotropic component of the signal carries additional information about the supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and host galaxy connection. Detecting these subtle anisotropies in the nano-Hz regime, probed by pulsar timing arrays (PTAs), is challenging. Low signal-to-noise ratios and difficulty disentangling faint GW signals from noise limit traditional angular power spectrum analyses, which often lack requisite sensitivity and resolution. This paper introduces Multi-Tracer Correlated Stacking (MTCS), a novel methodology to enhance SGWB anisotropy detectability. MTCS leverages electromagnetic (EM) sky maps of astrophysical tracers (e.g., galaxies, quasars, dark matter halos) known to host SMBHBs and correlate with the anisotropic SGWB. By cross-correlating PTA data with these EM tracers' spatial distribution, our approach coherently stacks anisotropic gravitational wave signatures, dramatically improving the signal-to-noise ratio and enabling detection of weak anisotropic components obscured in direct map-based analyses. MTCS offers a framework for probing SMBHB merger spatial distribution and connection to large-scale cosmic structure, providing insights into the SGWB's astrophysical origins. We outline its theoretical framework and discuss applications to current and future PTA datasets, promising to unlock details about SMBHB demographics, merger rates, and galaxy-black hole co-evolution.

title: Paxos Made EPR: Decidable Reasoning about Distributed Protocols
text_ai: Distributed protocols such as Paxos play an important role in many computer systems. Therefore, a bug in a distributed protocol may have tremendous effects. Accordingly, a lot of effort has been invested in verifying such protocols. However, checking invariants of such protocols is undecidable and hard in practice, as it requires reasoning about an unbounded number of nodes and messages. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing a novel approach that leverages the effectively propositional (EPR) fragment of first-order logic. While full first-order logic is undecidable, EPR remains decidable, offering a powerful sweet spot for expressing properties of systems with potentially unbounded domains. We show that a significant class of safety and liveness properties of distributed protocols, including critical invariants of Paxos, can be precisely encoded within EPR. Our methodology involves a systematic translation of protocol specifications, including node roles, message passing, and state transitions, into a set of EPR formulas. This encoding allows for automated verification using off-the-shelf EPR solvers. Specifically, we demonstrate how to transform the complex, unbounded reasoning required for Paxos into a decidable problem by carefully structuring the logical representation. This enables the automatic checking of core Paxos properties, such as agreement and validity, for any number of participants. The approach thereby provides a sound and complete framework for verifying a broad range of distributed protocols, significantly improving the practicality and automation of their formal analysis.

title: Short-ranged interaction effects on $Z_2$ topological phase transitions: The perturbative mean-field method
text_ai: Time-reversal symmetric topological insulator is a novel state of matter that a bulk-insulating state carries dissipationless spin transport along the surfaces, embedded by the $Z_2$ topological invariant. In the noninteracting limit, this exotic state has been intensively studied and explored with realistic systems, such as HgTe/(Hg,Cd)Te quantum wells. However, the influence of electron-electron interactions, particularly short-ranged ones, on these topological properties and phase transitions remains less explored. This work employs a perturbative mean-field method to systematically investigate how such interactions modify $Z_2$ topological phase transitions. Considering a generic lattice model, we introduce various short-ranged interactions, including on-site Hubbard repulsion, analyzing their renormalization effects on the band structure and the $Z_2$ invariant. Weak interactions are shown to shift critical points, induce new transition pathways, or alter the phase diagram. Repulsive interactions can both suppress the topological phase, narrowing its stability, and, under specific conditions, enhance it. We also discuss interaction-driven symmetry breaking, leading to novel correlated topological states. This study provides a theoretical framework for understanding the interplay between electron correlations and topological order in time-reversal symmetric systems, guiding the search for and design of next-generation topological materials.

title: Computational insights and the observation of SiC nanograin assembly: towards 2D silicon carbide
text_ai: While an increasing number of two-dimensional (2D) materials, including graphene and silicene, have already been realized, others have only been predicted. An interesting example is the two-dimensional form of silicon carbide (2D-SiC). Here, we present an observation of atomically thin and hexagonally bonded nanosized grains of SiC assembling temporarily in graphene oxide pores during an atomic resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy experiment. These nanoscale building blocks, identified as SiC through electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) and exhibiting hexagonal lattice fringes, coalesce transiently, suggesting a pathway for bottom-up assembly into larger 2D-SiC sheets. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations corroborate the energetic favorability and structural stability of these hexagonal SiC clusters, and their preferred growth orientations within confining environments. The observed assembly is driven by specific interactions with the graphene oxide scaffold, facilitating nanograin alignment and bonding. This unique *in situ* observation, supported by theoretical modeling, offers compelling experimental evidence for stable 2D-SiC nanostructures and critical understanding of their early formation stages. This work lays a foundational experimental and computational framework for directed synthesis of macroscopic 2D silicon carbide, a material with promising applications in high-power electronics and quantum technologies.

title: Continual Evolution in Nonreciprocal Ecological Models
text_ai: Feedbacks between evolution and ecology are ubiquitous, with ecological interactions determining which mutants are successful, and these mutants in turn modifying community structure. We study the evolutionary dynamics of several ecological models with overlapping niches, including consumer resource and Lotka-Volterra models. We model nonreciprocal interaction strengths, combining competitive resource exploitation with predator-prey or host-parasite-like dynamics. Using adaptive dynamics, we reveal a breakdown of evolutionary stability. Unlike reciprocal models converging to an Evolutionary Stable Strategy (ESS) or stable polymorphism, our systems exhibit perpetual, non-equilibrium evolution. This dynamism often manifests as Red Queen-like cycles or complex, chaotic trait trajectories, driven by a constantly shifting fitness landscape. The absence of a global fitness maximum means successful mutations inevitably create conditions for subsequent, distinct mutations, fueling an unending arms race. Overlapping niches, coupled with nonreciprocity, amplify this effect via intricate, indirect feedbacks preventing settling, fostering persistent trait variation and turnover. Our findings suggest nonreciprocity fundamentally drives eco-evolutionary dynamism, explaining persistent evolutionary change, phenotypic diversity, and unpredictable long-term trajectories in natural communities. This provides a theoretical basis for how inherent asymmetries prevent evolutionary stasis and promote continuous adaptation.
prefix: Feedbacks between evolution and ecology are ubiquitous, with ecological interactions determining which mutants are successful, and these mutants in turn modifying community structure. We study the evolutionary dynamics of several ecological models with overlapping niches, including consumer resource and Lotka-Volterra models.

title: Cycle-SUM: Cycle-consistent Adversarial LSTM Networks for Unsupervised Video Summarization
text_ai: In this paper, we present a novel unsupervised video summarization model that requires no manual annotation. The proposed model termed Cycle-SUM adopts a new cycle-consistent adversarial LSTM architecture that can effectively maximize the information preserving and compactness of the summary video. It consists of a frame selector and a cycle-consistent learning based evaluator. The frame selector, an LSTM, assigns importance scores to video frames. The evaluator, an adversarial discriminator, differentiates original segments from those reconstructed via the summary. Cycle-SUM's core innovation is its cycle-consistent learning, enforcing bidirectional reconstruction: the original video must be reconstructible from its summary, and vice-versa. This self-supervised objective ensures maximally informative and representative summary frames. The adversarial framework further refines summaries, pushing the selector to generate ideal, indistinguishable outputs. Extensive experiments on SumMe and TVSum benchmark datasets demonstrate Cycle-SUM's superior performance, achieving state-of-the-art results against existing unsupervised and several supervised methods.

The proposed model termed Cycle-SUM adopts a new cycle-consistent adversarial LSTM architecture that can effectively maximize the information preserving and compactness of the summary video. It consists of a frame selector and a cycle-consistent learning based evaluator.

title: An Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph first view on Solar Spicules
text_ai: Solar spicules have eluded modelers and observers for decades. Since the discovery of the more energetic type II, spicules have become a heated topic but their contribution to the energy balance of the low solar atmosphere remains unknown. The Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), with its unprecedented high-resolution UV spectra and images of the solar chromosphere and transition region, offers a unique opportunity to scrutinize these enigmatic structures. This paper presents the first comprehensive analysis of Type II spicules observed with IRIS, leveraging its capabilities to resolve fine-scale motions and thermal signatures. Our study utilizes observations in multiple spectral lines, including Mg II k (chromosphere), C II 1334 Å, C IV 1402 Å, and Si IV 1394 Å (transition region), to trace the evolution of spicules from their chromospheric roots into the hotter transition region. We employ advanced tracking algorithms and Doppler shift analysis to derive their kinematic properties, such as upward velocities and accelerations, and investigate their thermal evolution through line broadening and intensity profiles. These first-of-their-kind observations reveal compelling evidence for rapid heating associated with spicule upflows, characterized by significant non-thermal broadening and blueshifts extending into the Si IV formation temperatures. We observe highly dynamic events, often exhibiting rapid deceleration and subsequent heating, suggesting a potential role for magnetic reconnection or shock dissipation at their tips. The data provide crucial constraints on the mass and energy fluxes carried by Type II spicules, indicating a substantial, previously unquantified, contribution to heating the solar corona. This IRIS perspective offers a transformative understanding of spicule physics, suggesting that these transient phenomena are not merely mass conduits but active sites of energy deposition critical for the overall energy balance of the solar atmosphere.

title: Broad-band spectral study of LMXB black hole candidate 4U 1957+11 with NuSTAR
text_ai: We present here the results of broadband spectral analysis of low-mass X-ray binary and a black hole candidate 4U 1957+11. The source was observed nine times with the Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array (NuSTAR) between 2018 September and 2019 November. During these observations, the spectral state of 4U 1957+11 evolved marginally. Spectral fitting employed a phenomenological model comprising a multicolor disk blackbody and a Comptonization component. Our analysis consistently revealed a soft thermal-dominant state, with the inner disk temperature remaining relatively stable around ~1.0-1.2 keV across all observations. The power-law component, representing the corona, contributed minimally to the overall flux, exhibiting a steep photon index (Γ ~ 2.5-3.0) consistent with a soft state. We found no significant evidence for strong relativistic reflection features, preventing precise constraints on the black hole spin. The source luminosity varied only slightly within the observed period, reinforcing the interpretation of a stable, high-accretion rate soft state. These findings are consistent with 4U 1957+11 being a persistent LMXB accreting at high Eddington fractions, with its spectral characteristics primarily driven by a dominant thermal disk.

title: Negotiating access to the Nigerian healthcare system: the experiences of HIV-positive men who have sex with men.
text_ai: Men who have sex with men in sub-Saharan Africa continue to have a disproportionately higher burden of HIV than their counterparts in the general population. In this qualitative study, barriers to participants accessing healthcare services in Nigeria, a country where same-sex relationships are criminalised and considered societally abhorrent, were explored. Semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted with 25 HIV-positive MSM, recruited through snowball sampling from community-based organisations in two major Nigerian cities. Participants consistently reported pervasive stigma and discrimination from healthcare providers, manifesting as judgmental attitudes, confidentiality breaches, and outright service refusal. This prejudice, exacerbated by criminalisation, fostered profound fear of disclosure, leading to delayed care-seeking, treatment non-adherence, and reliance on informal networks. These systemic barriers critically compromised access to quality and timely care. The study underscores an urgent need for targeted interventions to sensitise healthcare professionals, advocate for policy reforms, and establish safe, non-discriminatory healthcare environments. Addressing these challenges is vital for improving health outcomes and upholding human rights for HIV-positive MSM in Nigeria.

title: Nothing to see here: Failed supernovae are faint or rare
text_ai: The absence of Type IIP core-collapse supernovae arising from progenitors above 17 solar masses suggests the existence of another evolutionary path by which massive stars end their lives. The direct collapse of a stellar core to a black hole without the production of a bright, explosive transient is expected to produce a long-lived, dim, red transient known as a failed supernova. Such events are characterized by a rapid luminosity drop after an initial, brief brightening, as the stellar envelope fails ejection and falls back onto the newly formed black hole. Despite theoretical predictions for their prevalence, direct observational evidence for these "dark" collapses remains elusive. Extensive searches in nearby galaxies have yielded only ambiguous candidates, none definitively confirmed. This scarcity poses a critical astrophysical puzzle, challenging theoretical rates or expected observational properties. This paper synthesizes current theoretical models with comprehensive observational limits from wide-field transient surveys. Our analysis robustly demonstrates that if failed supernovae account for the missing massive star deaths, their peak luminosities must be significantly fainter than conservative theoretical estimates, or their intrinsic event rate is considerably lower than the observed Type IIP supernova rate. These findings have profound implications for understanding massive star evolution, stellar-mass black hole formation, and the design of future transient searches.

title: Imitation Learning for Active Neck Motion Enabling Robot Manipulation beyond the Field of View
text_ai: Most prior research in deep imitation learning has predominantly utilized fixed cameras for image input, which constrains task performance to the predefined field of view. However, enabling a robot to actively maneuver its neck can significantly expand the scope of imitation learning to encompass a wider variety of tasks and expressive actions such as neck gestures. This paper introduces a novel imitation learning framework that enables a robot to learn a joint policy for both end-effector manipulation and active neck articulation. By integrating proprioceptive and egocentric visual inputs, our method allows the robot to dynamically adjust its camera viewpoint to track objects, explore occluded regions, and maintain task-relevant visual information, thereby addressing the limitations of static camera perspectives. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a physical robot performing various manipulation tasks, including picking objects initially outside the camera's fixed field of view and requiring active neck reorientation for successful interaction. Experimental results show that our framework significantly improves task success rates and robustness in scenarios demanding dynamic visual exploration and re-acquisition, outperforming traditional fixed-camera imitation learning baselines. This work represents a crucial step towards enabling more versatile and adaptive robot manipulation in complex, real-world environments through active perception.

title: Truth is Universal: Robust Detection of Lies in LLMs
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionised natural language processing, exhibiting impressive human-like capabilities. In particular, LLMs are capable of "lying", knowingly outputting false statements. Hence, it is of interest and importance to develop methods to detect when LLMs lie. Indeed, several authors trained classifiers to detect LLM lies based on their internal model activations. However, these activation-based methods often lack generalizability across diverse LLM architectures and tasks. We hypothesize that the fundamental distinction between truthful and false statements manifests in a more universal, model-agnostic signature within LLM outputs. Our paper introduces a novel framework exploiting this property by systematically analyzing the semantic coherence and logical consistency of LLM generations. Instead of relying on internal states, our method identifies subtle output inconsistencies characteristic of deception. Extensive experiments demonstrate superior robustness and cross-model generalizability (e.g., GPT-3.5, Llama 2) in detecting lies across various contexts, significantly outperforming activation-based predecessors. This represents a crucial advancement towards reliable and transferable lie detection, vital for responsible LLM deployment.

title: Neural response to modulating the probability that actions of self or other result in auditory tones: A parametric fMRI study into causal ambiguity.
text_ai: In normal circumstances we can easily distinguish between changes to the external world brought about by our own actions from those with external causes. However, in certain contexts our sense of ownership and agency over acts is not so clear. This ambiguity, often termed "causal ambiguity," poses a significant challenge for the brain's causal inference mechanisms. We parametrically investigated the neural underpinnings of processing such ambiguous causal links between actions and their sensory consequences. Using a parametric fMRI design, participants performed a task where their own actions or an "other's" could probabilistically trigger an auditory tone. We systematically modulated the probability (0-100%) of this action-outcome link for both self and other, creating varying degrees of causal ambiguity. Our fMRI results revealed distinct neural signatures. Activity in the anterior insula and superior temporal sulcus (STS) parametrically increased with greater causal ambiguity (probabilities near 50%), irrespective of agent. However, the temporoparietal junction (TPJ) and precuneus showed a significant interaction, responding more strongly to ambiguous self-generated outcomes, while medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) activity differentiated between self and other agency, particularly under high certainty. These findings suggest a distributed neural network for resolving causal ambiguity, with distinct regions supporting general ambiguity processing, agent-specific causal inference, and agency attribution. This study offers novel insights into the computational mechanisms underlying our sense of agency and causal understanding, with implications for conditions involving distorted agency.

title: Microfracture provides better clinical results than debridement in the treatment of acute talar osteochondral lesions using arthroscopic assisted fixation of acute ankle fractures
text_ai: PURPOSE: Ankle arthroscopy is a useful tool for detection and treatment of accompanying intraarticular pathologies in acute ankle fractures. The purpose of this study was to compare the treatment results of talus osteochondral lesions (OLT) with debridement and microfracture in arthroscopy assisted surgery of acute ankle fractures. METHODS: This retrospective comparative study enrolled 68 patients (34 in each group) with acute ankle fractures and concomitant talar OLTs treated with arthroscopy-assisted open reduction and internal fixation between 2015 and 2020. Exclusions included chronic OLTs or prior ankle surgery. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) score and a Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain at a mean follow-up of 36.5 ± 8.2 months. RESULTS: The microfracture group demonstrated significantly superior clinical outcomes at final follow-up. Mean AOFAS scores were substantially higher (90.3 ± 5.1 vs. 78.9 ± 6.7, p < 0.001), and VAS pain scores significantly lower (1.5 ± 0.8 vs. 3.9 ± 1.2, p < 0.001) in the microfracture group. Demographic and fracture characteristics were comparable. No major procedure-related complications were observed in either group. CONCLUSION: Microfracture treatment for acute talar osteochondral lesions identified during arthroscopy-assisted fixation of acute ankle fractures yields significantly better clinical results than simple debridement. These findings advocate for microfracture as the preferred treatment modality to enhance functional outcomes and reduce pain.

title: Binary black holes and tori in AGN I. Ejection of stars and merging of the binary
text_ai: Most galaxies have central massive black holes (BH), and merge with others during their evolution, as strongly suggested by recent observations. Consequently a black hole binary (BHB) emerges. Considering the evolution of the binary when it has become hard, at a separation of the BHs of about 1 pc, we propose to solve two basic questions in our understanding of the central activity of galaxies: (1) Do the BHs actually merge? (2) How does the binary interact with its dense stellar environment, impacting its inspiral and the surrounding stellar cluster? We address these questions through N-body simulations of a hard BHB embedded within a dense stellar cluster. Our simulations demonstrate that strong three-body encounters between the BHB and passing stars efficiently eject stars from the galactic center via gravitational slingshot. This process effectively extracts orbital energy and angular momentum from the BHB, causing it to shrink significantly. This stellar scattering mechanism provides a viable solution to the 'final parsec problem', allowing the BHB to harden from ~1 pc to separations where gravitational wave emission dominates, ultimately leading to merger. The continuous depletion of the central stellar cusp creates a region largely devoid of stars, influencing the BHB's subsequent evolution and its interaction with any surrounding circumbinary gas or torus. This process has profound implications for the dynamical evolution and observational signatures of galactic nuclei, shaping their stellar density profiles and potentially influencing the gas accretion relevant for AGN fueling, a topic further explored in subsequent work.

title: QCD correction to gluino decay to $t\bar{t}\tilde{\chi}^0_1$ in the MSSM
text_ai: We calculate the complete next-to-leading order QCD corrections to the three-body decay of gluino into top-pair associated with a lightest neutralino in the minimal supersymmetric standard model. We obtain that the LO and NLO QCD corrected decay widths of $\tilde{g} \to t \bar{t} \tilde{\chi}_1^0$ at the ${\rm SPS 6}$ benchmark point are $0.1490 GeV$ and 0.1069 GeV respectively, and the relative correction is -28.2%. We employed dimensional regularization to handle ultraviolet and infrared divergences, performing renormalization in the on-shell scheme for relevant masses and mixing angles, and the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme for the strong coupling constant. Our detailed analysis reveals a substantial dependence of these corrections on supersymmetric parameters, particularly the gluino and neutralino masses, as well as $\tan\beta$. We observe that the NLO corrections consistently lead to a reduction in the decay width across a wide range of parameter space. This significant negative correction underscores the necessity of including higher-order QCD effects for precise theoretical predictions of gluino phenomenology. Such improved precision is vital for interpreting experimental searches for supersymmetry at the Large Hadron Collider and for accurately constraining the MSSM parameter space, thereby enhancing the sensitivity of current and future collider experiments to new physics signals.

title: H-EYE: Holistic Resource Modeling and Management for Diversely Scaled Edge-Cloud Systems
text_ai: Computing systems have been evolving to be more pervasive, heterogeneous, and dynamic. An increasing number of emerging domains now rely on diverse edge to cloud continuum where the execution of applications often spans various tiers of systems with significantly heterogeneous computational capabilities. Resources in each tier are often handled in isolation due to scalability and privacy concerns. This fragmented view prevents global optimization, leading to inefficient resource utilization, increased latency, and compromised reliability for applications requiring seamless execution across the continuum. Existing solutions often focus on specific tiers or lack the comprehensive awareness needed for true end-to-end management. To address these critical challenges, we propose H-EYE, a novel framework for Holistic Resource Modeling and Management designed to provide a unified and adaptive approach to resource orchestration across the entire edge-cloud spectrum. H-EYE introduces a multi-faceted resource modeling approach that captures the diverse characteristics and interdependencies of computational, network, and storage resources across all tiers. It employs intelligent, context-aware algorithms for dynamic resource allocation, task placement, and workload migration, optimizing for key performance indicators like latency, energy consumption, and throughput. Crucially, our framework leverages hierarchical and federated learning mechanisms to build a real-time, global awareness of available resources without centralizing sensitive data, thereby ensuring both scalability and data privacy. Through extensive simulations and prototype implementations on diverse edge-cloud testbeds, we demonstrate that H-EYE significantly outperforms traditional isolated management strategies, achieving up to 35% reduction in end-to-end application latency, 20% improvement in resource utilization, and enhanced system resilience, thus paving the way for truly adaptive and efficient continuum computing.

title: Mid-term results of the modular ANCA-Fit femoral component in total hip replacement
text_ai: We report the minimum five-year follow-up of 352 primary total hip replacements using the uncemented hydroxyapatite-coated ANCA-Fit femoral component with a modular neck and head. The series comprised 319 patients (212 men, 107 women) with a mean age at operation of 64.4 years (28 to 97). The principal diagnosis was osteoarthritis. Clinical and radiographic outcomes were assessed at a mean follow-up of 6.2 years (5.0 to 9.8). The mean Harris Hip Score (HHS) improved significantly from 45 preoperatively to 92 postoperatively, and the mean visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score decreased from 7.5 to 1.2. The overall survival rate of the femoral component, with revision for any reason as the endpoint, was 96.3% (95% CI 94.1–98.5%). Reasons for revision included aseptic loosening (2.0%), periprosthetic fracture (0.9%), and deep infection (0.6%). Radiographic analysis demonstrated stable osseointegration in 97.2% of stems, with no evidence of femoral osteolysis or stem fracture. These mid-term results indicate excellent clinical and radiographic performance of the ANCA-Fit femoral component, demonstrating robust osseointegration and a low rate of aseptic loosening. The modular design appears durable, with no junctional complications. Long-term studies are necessary to confirm these promising findings.

title: The Use of Telemedicine for Penicillin Allergy Skin Testing.
text_ai: Penicillin skin testing (PST) is increasingly used as a tool to evaluate penicillin allergy in patients with a reported history. The limited availability of allergists, however, may be an impeding factor. We sought to assess the clinical utility of telemedicine to facilitate PST. Penicillin-allergic inpatients receiving systemic antibiotics were prospectively identified between April and August 2017. Eligible patients then underwent PST, performed by a trained bedside nurse or pharmacist, who was remotely supervised by a board-certified allergist via secure video conferencing. The allergist reviewed the patient's allergy history, observed the live skin testing procedure, interpreted the results in real-time, and provided a definitive recommendation regarding penicillin allergy status and subsequent antibiotic management. Primary outcomes included the proportion of patients successfully delabeled from penicillin allergy and the incidence of adverse drug reactions during PST. Secondary outcomes assessed changes in antibiotic prescribing patterns post-testing and the mean time from initial consultation to PST completion. Of the 105 inpatients identified as eligible, 87 underwent telemedicine-facilitated PST. A high proportion, 83%, were successfully delabeled, allowing for a switch to appropriate, narrower-spectrum penicillin-based antibiotics in 75% of these cases. No severe adverse events were reported. The mean time from initial consultation to PST completion was 1.8 days. Our findings demonstrate that telemedicine provides a safe, efficient, and clinically effective method for conducting PST in hospitalized patients. This approach significantly enhances access to specialized allergy care, optimizes antibiotic prescribing, and addresses current limitations in allergist availability, thereby improving patient care and promoting antimicrobial stewardship.

title: Implantable LVAD infections: implications for permanent use of the device
text_ai: BACKGROUND: Infection in implantable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) patients is common and has serious implications regarding permanent use of the LVAD. METHODS: Thirty-three patients had HeartMate LVAD insertion as a bridge to heart transplantation. The mean length of hospital stay was 8 days before LVAD insertion. Patients were prospectively followed for a mean of 18 ± 12 months. Infection surveillance included weekly blood cultures, exit site examinations, and clinical assessment. Data on infection type, causative organisms, treatment, and patient outcomes were collected. RESULTS: A total of 21 infections occurred in 15 (45%) patients, with driveline infections (n=12, 57%) and Gram-positive organisms, primarily *Staphylococcus aureus*, predominating. Five (33%) infected patients required LVAD exchange or explantation due to refractory infection. Infection significantly prolonged hospital stay (mean 45 vs. 15 days, p<0.01) and delayed transplantation. Critically, infection contributed to device failure or prevented successful bridge to transplant in 8 patients, highlighting its profound impact on long-term device viability and patient outcomes. CONCLUSION: LVAD infections cause significant morbidity and device failure, often necessitating explantation. This critically challenges permanent LVAD support, underscoring the need for advanced prophylactic and management strategies.

title: Modified Lagrangian Formulation of Gear Tooth Crack Analysis using Combined Approach of Variable Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Time Synchronous Averaging (TSA)
text_ai: This paper discusses the possible observation of an integrated gear tooth crack analysis procedure that employs the combined approach of variable mode decomposition (VMD) and time synchronous averaging (TSA) based on the coupled electromechanical gearbox (CEMG) system. This paper also incorporates the modified Lagrangian formulation to model the CEMG system by considering Rayleigh's dissipative potential. This formulation comprehensively represents the coupled electromechanical dynamics, integrating non-linearities like backlash and time-varying mesh stiffness. Rayleigh's dissipative potential is included to accurately account for energy losses, enabling realistic simulation of system responses influenced by evolving gear tooth cracks. The model dynamically incorporates crack propagation by altering the gear mesh stiffness profile. Subsequently, the proposed signal processing strategy utilizes VMD to decompose the complex vibration signals from the CEMG model into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), separating distinct frequency components. This is synergistically combined with TSA, a robust technique for enhancing gear-related periodic components and suppressing noise. The VMD-TSA approach is designed to isolate and amplify subtle, non-linear features characteristic of early-stage gear tooth cracks, often obscured by operational noise and other system vibrations. Numerical simulations, based on the developed modified Lagrangian CEMG model, rigorously validate the methodology's superior performance. Results demonstrate significantly enhanced sensitivity and robustness in detecting and characterizing gear tooth cracks under varying load and noise conditions, outperforming conventional signal processing techniques. This integrated procedure offers a highly accurate and reliable framework for proactive fault detection and predictive maintenance in industrial gearboxes.
