title: Snow Globe: An Advancing-Front 3D Delaunay Mesh Refinement Algorithm
text_ai: <incorrect proofs; does not consider an important case because of which the proofs are wrong. The paper was withdrawn from submission> One of the objectives of a Delaunay mesh refinement algorithm is to produce meshes with tetrahedral elements having a bounded aspect ratio, which is the ratio between the radius of the circumscribing and inscribing spheres. The algorithm presented in this paper, Snow Globe, is an advancing-front 3D Delaunay mesh refinement method designed to achieve this crucial objective. Snow Globe systematically generates high-quality tetrahedral meshes for complex three-dimensional domains by incrementally building the mesh from the boundary inward. It employs a sophisticated point insertion strategy to eliminate poorly shaped tetrahedra, specifically those with large aspect ratios or small dihedral angles, which are known to degrade the accuracy and stability of numerical simulations. A key innovation of Snow Globe lies in its robust management of the advancing front and its novel criteria for point placement, which carefully balance local feature sizes and curvature. This ensures that newly inserted points preserve the Delaunay property and contribute to overall mesh quality without introducing new degeneracies. The algorithm provides theoretical guarantees for producing meshes where all generated tetrahedra satisfy a user-defined minimum aspect ratio. This makes Snow Globe highly effective for demanding applications in computational science and engineering, where element quality directly impacts the fidelity of the simulation. Extensive computational experiments demonstrate the algorithm's efficiency, scalability, and robustness across a wide range of intricate geometries, consistently generating high-quality meshes free from inverted or degenerate elements, thus providing a significant advancement in 3D mesh generation.

title: Cleavage of the SUN-domain protein Mps3 at its N-terminus regulates centrosome disjunction in budding yeast meiosis.
text_ai: Centrosomes organize microtubules and are essential for spindle formation and chromosome segregation during cell division. Duplicated centrosomes are physically linked, but how this linkage is dissolved remains unclear. Yeast centrosomes are tethered by a nuclear-envelope-attached structure called the half-bridge, whose components have mammalian homologues. We reveal that Mps3, a conserved SUN-domain protein of the nuclear envelope and half-bridge, undergoes specific N-terminal proteolytic cleavage during budding yeast meiotic prophase, crucial for timely centrosome disjunction. Preventing Mps3 cleavage causes persistent centrosome association, leading to meiotic spindle assembly defects and chromosome segregation errors during meiosis I. Conversely, a constitutively cleaved Mps3 variant promotes premature centrosome separation. Our findings establish Mps3 N-terminal cleavage as a novel regulatory mechanism precisely controlling centrosome disjunction, vital for proper spindle formation and accurate meiotic chromosome segregation and gamete viability. Given the evolutionary conservation of SUN-domain proteins and centrosome components, this mechanism likely represents a fundamental strategy for regulating centrosome dynamics in diverse eukaryotes.

title: Aberrated optical cavities
text_ai: Optical cavities are an enabling technology of modern quantum science: from their essential role in the operation of lasers, to applications as fly-wheels in atomic clocks and interaction-enhancing components in quantum optics experiments, developing a quantitative understanding of the mode-shapes and energies of optical cavities has been crucial for the growth of the field. However, practical systems inevitably feature mirror aberrations from manufacturing or environmental factors. These imperfections fundamentally alter ideal mode-shapes and resonant frequencies, degrading performance in sensitive quantum applications requiring high fidelity. While numerical simulations offer insights, a general analytical framework quantifying these effects remains elusive. This paper develops a comprehensive theoretical model using a paraxial wave equation perturbation approach. Characterizing mirror deformations with Zernike polynomials, we derive analytical expressions for perturbed mode-shapes and eigenfrequency shifts. Our findings elucidate the intricate interplay between aberration types and cavity geometry, offering crucial design principles for robust optical systems and a powerful diagnostic tool for optimizing advanced quantum technologies.

title: Simplified Muscle-Suspension Lower Blepharoplasty by Orbicularis Hitch.
text_ai: The suspension of orbicularis oculi during lower blepharoplasty presents a logical surgical addition for further support of the lid, as well as further improvement to its contour profile. It has traditionally been performed as an extension of the skin-muscle flap procedure, but more recently, and aggressively, as a muscle strap-flap separated from the orbicularis sheet by myotomy. Such aggressive techniques increase dissection and risk tissue trauma. This paper introduces the 'orbicularis hitch,' a simplified technique providing robust lid support with reduced invasiveness. It involves securing the intact orbicularis oculi directly to the deep temporal fascia or periosteum of the lateral orbital rim using a permanent suture, bypassing myotomy and extensive flap creation. This minimizes dissection, preserves muscle integrity, and potentially reduces complications like lid malposition. We retrospectively reviewed 115 consecutive patients undergoing lower blepharoplasty with the orbicularis hitch (2018-2022). Outcomes, assessed at 18-month average follow-up, included aesthetic results, patient satisfaction, and complication incidence. Results indicate consistent improvement in lower lid contour and support, high patient satisfaction, and a low complication rate, particularly regarding lid retraction or scleral show. The simplified orbicularis hitch offers an efficient, safe, and effective method for lasting lower lid support in blepharoplasty, presenting a valuable alternative to more complex muscle suspension techniques.

It has traditionally been performed as an extension of the skin-muscle flap procedure, but more recently, and aggressively, as a muscle strap-flap separated from the orbicularis sheet by myotomy.

title: The quaternionic KP hierarchy and conformally immersed 2-tori in the 4-sphere
text_ai: The quaternionic KP hierarchy is the integrable hierarchy of p.d.e obtained by replacing the complex numbers with the quaternions, mutatis mutandis, in the standard construction of the KP hierarchy equations and solutions; it is equivalent to what is often called the Davey-Stewartson II hierarchy. This paper establishes a profound connection between this integrable system and conformally immersed 2-tori in the 4-sphere (S^4). We demonstrate that all such geometric objects can be explicitly characterized and constructed from specific solutions of the quaternionic KP hierarchy. This construction leverages a quaternionic analogue of the loop group factorization method, where solutions are associated with elements of a suitable infinite-dimensional loop group, whose factorization provides the complete immersion data for the 2-tori. We further show how the dressing method, a key technique in integrable systems theory, can be effectively adapted to generate a broad spectrum of such geometric configurations. This framework offers a systematic and powerful approach to understanding and classifying conformally immersed 2-tori in S^4, extending classical results relating the complex KP hierarchy to minimal surfaces in R^3 and S^3, and offering a novel perspective on their rich geometric properties.

title: Modelling of initially stressed solids: structure of the energy density in the incompressible limit
text_ai: This study addresses the modelling of elastic bodies, particularly when the relaxed configuration is unknown or non-existent. We adopt the theory of initially stressed materials, incorporating the deformation gradient and stress state of the reference configuration (initial stress tensor) into the response function. Our primary objective is to systematically characterize the structure of the stored energy density function, accounting for both initial stress and material symmetry requirements. We demonstrate how the initial stress tensor, as an additional tensorial argument, modifies the conventional integrity basis for isotropic and anisotropic materials, leading to an expanded set of invariants. A significant focus is placed on deriving the explicit form of this energy density in the incompressible limit, where the constraint is rigorously integrated into the initially stressed framework. This reveals distinct structural implications and a more intricate dependence on both deformation and initial stress compared to initially unstressed counterparts. The analysis yields a comprehensive framework for developing constitutive models for initially stressed incompressible solids, offering crucial insights into their mechanical response and stability under complex loading conditions.

We adopt the theory of initially stressed materials, incorporating the deformation gradient and stress state of the reference configuration (initial stress tensor) into the response function.

title: UCPhrase: Unsupervised Context-aware Quality Phrase Tagging
text_ai: Identifying and understanding quality phrases from context is a fundamental task in text mining. The most challenging part of this task arguably lies in uncommon, emerging, and domain-specific phrases. The infrequent nature of these phrases significantly hurts the performance of phrase mining methods that rely on sufficient phrase occurrences in the input corpus. To address this critical limitation, we propose **UCPhrase**, an Unsupervised Context-aware Quality Phrase Tagging framework. UCPhrase identifies high-quality phrases irrespective of their frequency, overcoming the data sparsity challenge. Unlike prior work relying on statistical co-occurrences or supervised models, UCPhrase leverages a novel context-aware neural network architecture. This architecture learns rich contextual representations for phrase candidates, discerning quality via semantic coherence and contextual fit, rather than raw frequency. UCPhrase operates in two stages: candidate generation and self-supervised quality scoring. The scorer utilizes surrounding linguistic context to evaluate 'phraseness' and informativeness, even for infrequent candidates. This focus on contextual consistency and semantic relevance significantly mitigates the data sparsity problem. Extensive experiments on diverse real-world datasets demonstrate UCPhrase's superior performance. It consistently outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised and weakly supervised baselines in identifying both frequent and rare quality phrases. Qualitative analysis confirms its ability to discover meaningful domain-specific and emerging terminology, highlighting its robustness and utility for text mining applications.

title: A new introduction rule for disjunction
text_ai: We extend Natural Deduction with a third introduction rule for the disjunction, $\vee$-i3, with a conclusion $\Gamma\vdash A\vee B$, but both premises $\Gamma\vdash A$ and $\Gamma\vdash B$. This rule is admissible in Natural Deduction. This extension is interesting in several respects. Firstly, while $\vee$-i3 is admissible and does not expand the set of derivable theorems, its inclusion significantly alters proof structure. We demonstrate that it enables substantially shorter and more elegant derivations for specific classes of disjunctive formulae, thereby offering novel insights into proof search strategies and proof compression within Natural Deduction. Secondly, we provide a detailed analysis of its impact on the system's metatheory, particularly concerning proof normalization and cut-elimination. We show that $\vee$-i3 integrates seamlessly, preserving these crucial properties while introducing distinct normalization paths. This challenges conventional understandings of introduction rules, which typically require minimal information. By requiring both disjuncts as premises, $\vee$-i3 highlights a subtle distinction in the constructive interpretation of disjunction, prompting a re-evaluation of what constitutes an 'introduction' for this connective across classical and intuitionistic frameworks. Our findings suggest a richer, more nuanced structural understanding of disjunction in formal proofs.

title: Image-Specific Information Suppression and Implicit Local Alignment for Text-based Person Search
text_ai: Text-based person search (TBPS) is a challenging task that aims to search pedestrian images with the same identity from an image gallery given a query text. In recent years, TBPS has made remarkable progress and state-of-the-art methods achieve superior performance by learning local fine-grained correspondence between images and texts. However, existing methods often struggle with suppressing irrelevant image-specific information, like background clutter, diluting visual features. Moreover, explicit local alignment is brittle to pose/viewpoint variations. To address this, we propose a framework with Image-Specific Information Suppression and Implicit Local Alignment. Our suppression module dynamically attenuates noisy image regions, enabling focus on salient human attributes, refining representations, and enhancing robustness. Concurrently, our implicit alignment learns flexible, context-aware correspondences between textual phrases and visual regions. Moving beyond rigid mappings, this robustly captures semantic relationships resilient to pose and appearance variations. Integrating these synergistically, our framework generates more discriminative and alignment-aware representations. Extensive experiments on CUHK-PEDES and RSTPReid benchmarks demonstrate superior performance, achieving new state-of-the-art results. This significantly outperforms existing methods, validating the importance of image noise suppression and flexible local alignment for robust person search.

In recent years, TBPS has made remarkable progress and state-of-the-art methods achieve superior performance by learning local fine-grained correspondence between images and texts.

title: An ab-initio study on engineering quantum anomalous Hall effect in compensated antiferromagnet MnBi$_{2}$Te$_{4}$
text_ai: Recently, the quantum anomalous Hall effect (QAHE) has been theoretically proposed in compensated antiferromagnetic systems by using the magnetic topological insulator model [see arXiv:2404.13305 (2024)]. However, the related and systematic study based on a realistic material system is still limited. As the only experimentally realized antiferromagnetic topological insulator, MnBi$_{2}$Te$_{4}$ becomes a vital platform for exploring various topological states. Here, we perform a comprehensive ab-initio study to systematically investigate the realization and engineering of QAHE in MnBi$_{2}$Te$_{4}$. Our first-principles calculations explore the intricate interplay between magnetic order and electronic structure under external perturbations. We demonstrate that by judiciously tuning the magnetic configuration, specifically achieving a compensated antiferromagnetic state through interlayer magnetic coupling manipulation or charge doping, a robust QAHE can be established. We identify conditions under which MnBi$_{2}$Te$_{4}$ transitions from its intrinsic antiferromagnetic phase to a QAHE phase, characterized by a sizable topological band gap and quantized Hall conductivity. This engineering mechanism involves breaking the effective time-reversal symmetry at the surface while preserving bulk antiferromagnetism. Our findings offer a detailed theoretical blueprint for experimental realization of QAHE in MnBi$_{2}$Te$_{4}$ and highlight a general strategy for designing novel topological quantum states in other compensated antiferromagnetic systems, paving the way for future spintronic applications.

title: Dynamical Majorana Neutrino Masses and Axions II: Inclusion of Axial Background and Anomaly Terms
text_ai: We extend the study of a previous publication \cite{amsot} on Schwinger-Dyson dynamical mass generation for fermions and pseudoscalar fields (axion-like particles (ALP)), in field theories containing Yukawa type interactions between the fermions and ALPs, by incorporating anomaly terms and/or (constant) axial background fields. This extension is motivated by the ubiquitous presence of chiral anomalies in gauge theories and the potential role of axial backgrounds in various physical scenarios, ranging from strong electromagnetic fields to dense matter environments. We rigorously derive the coupled Schwinger-Dyson equations for the fermion self-energy and the ALP inverse propagator, incorporating the modifications arising from these additional terms. Our analysis reveals that the axial background field introduces novel momentum-dependent structures into the gap equations, which can significantly alter the conditions for dynamical symmetry breaking and the magnitude of the generated masses. Specifically, we demonstrate how the axial background can induce an anisotropic mass generation for Majorana neutrinos, potentially leading to a richer mass spectrum than previously considered. Furthermore, the anomaly terms play a crucial role in shaping the effective potential of the ALPs, influencing their dynamically generated mass and interaction properties. We explore the intricate interplay between the Yukawa coupling, the strength of the axial background, and the anomaly coefficients, identifying critical parameters that govern the existence and characteristics of the non-trivial solutions for both fermion and ALP masses. These findings provide a deeper understanding of non-perturbative mass generation mechanisms beyond the Standard Model, offering new pathways for explaining neutrino masses and enriching the phenomenology of axion-like particles in cosmology and particle physics.

title: Sketch and Validate for Big Data Clustering
text_ai: In response to the need for learning tools tuned to big data analytics, the present paper introduces a framework for efficient clustering of huge sets of (possibly high-dimensional) data. Building on random sampling and consensus (RANSAC) ideas pursued earlier in a different (computer vision) context for robust regression, a suite of novel dimensionality and set-reduction algorithms is developed. Specifically, our proposed methodology leverages the RANSAC paradigm to iteratively identify and refine a compact, representative 'sketch' of the dataset. This sketch robustly captures intrinsic cluster structures, even amidst noise and outliers, significantly mitigating the computational complexity for subsequent clustering algorithms, thereby enabling their application to datasets of unprecedented scale and dimensionality. A novel validation module is integrated to rigorously assess the quality, stability, and statistical significance of discovered clusters. Employing robust metrics for coherence and separation, this module provides objective criteria for parameter selection and ensures outcome reliability. Extensive experimental validation on diverse synthetic and real-world big datasets demonstrates our framework's consistent superiority over state-of-the-art methods in terms of efficiency, scalability, and clustering accuracy, positioning it as a powerful tool for big data analytics.

title: Black Silicon with high density and high aspect ratio nanowhiskers
text_ai: Physical properties of black Silicon (b-Si) formed on Si wafers by reactive ion etching in chlorine plasma are reported in an attempt to clarify the formation mechanism and the origin of the observed optical and electrical phenomena which are promising for a variety of applications. Morphological analysis confirms the spontaneous formation of dense, vertically oriented silicon nanowhiskers (aspect ratios >10:1), attributed to a self-masking mechanism during chlorine plasma etching that yields highly anisotropic material removal. Optical characterization demonstrates dramatic surface reflectance reduction (below 1% across 300-1100 nm), indicative of superior light trapping. Concurrently, electrical measurements reveal enhanced minority carrier lifetime and improved surface passivation, attributed to the nanowhiskers' high surface area and modified electronic band structure. These attributes position high-density, high-aspect-ratio b-Si as a compelling platform for next-generation photovoltaics, photodetectors, and sensors, leveraging its exceptional light absorption and tunable surface properties.

title: Quantum Hamiltonians with weak random abstract perturbation. II. Localization in the expanded spectrum
text_ai: We consider multi-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with a weak random perturbation distributed in the cells of some periodic lattice. In every cell the perturbation is described by the translate of a fixed abstract operator depending on a random variable. The random variables, indexed by the lattice, are assumed to be independent and identically distributed according to an absolutely continuous probability density. We demonstrate that, under suitable conditions on the unperturbed operator and the abstract perturbation, the spectrum of the full Hamiltonian exhibits a pure point component in certain regions. Specifically, we establish the existence of an expanded pure point spectrum associated with exponentially localized eigenfunctions. This localization emerges within a spectral band formed from the unperturbed continuous spectrum due to the weak random perturbation. Our analysis employs a multi-scale analysis argument adapted to the abstract nature of the perturbation, combined with a resolvent expansion technique. We prove that for sufficiently small perturbation strength, the Hamiltonian possesses an infinite number of eigenvalues, each corresponding to an exponentially decaying eigenfunction, providing a detailed understanding of spectral properties in this weakly disordered regime.

In every cell the perturbation is described by the translate of a fixed abstract operator depending on a random variable. The random variables, indexed by the lattice, are assumed to be independent and identically distributed according to an absolutely continuous probability density.

title: Randomized Classifiers vs Human Decision-Makers: Trustworthy AI May Have to Act Randomly and Society Seems to Accept This
text_ai: As \emph{artificial intelligence} (AI) systems are increasingly involved in decisions affecting our lives, ensuring that automated decision-making is fair and ethical has become a top priority. Intuitively, we feel that akin to human decisions, judgments of artificial agents should necessarily be grounded in some moral principles. However, this intuition overlooks limitations of purely deterministic systems. Even well-intentioned, such systems can inadvertently perpetuate societal biases, create arbitrary distinctions, or be exploitable. In critical domains like resource allocation, risk assessment, and legal arbitration, strict deterministic logic can paradoxically undermine fairness and public trust. Drawing parallels with human decisions, where lotteries and tie-breakers are often deemed acceptable mechanisms for impartiality or preventing manipulation, this paper explores the controversial but crucial role of randomized classifiers. We argue that by introducing a controlled degree of stochasticity, AI systems can mitigate systemic biases, ensure more equitable distribution of limited resources, and enhance robustness against strategic gaming. Our analysis suggests that, while counter-intuitive, judicious randomness can, in certain circumstances, render AI decisions more trustworthy, legitimate, and fairer. This challenges the notion that moral AI must always be perfectly predictable, suggesting instead that controlled randomness may be a necessary component for truly trustworthy AI, a concept society, we contend, implicitly accepts in high-stakes human judgments.

Intuitively, we feel that akin to human decisions, judgments of artificial agents should necessarily be grounded in some moral principles.

title: Enhancing the Properties of Plasma Activated Water using an Air Bubble Diffuser
text_ai: In this study, the impact of an air bubbler on the properties of plasma-activated water (PAW) was investigated in different configurations. A pencil plasma jet (PPJ) using a dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) was used to prepare PAW. 50 mL deionized water samples were treated in three configurations: plasma-only, simultaneous plasma and air bubbling, and post-plasma bubbling using a fine-pore diffuser at a controlled flow rate. PAW properties, including pH, oxidation-reduction potential (ORP), electrical conductivity, and key reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS: H2O2, NO2-, NO3-), were characterized immediately post-treatment and during storage. Results demonstrated that an air bubbler significantly influenced PAW properties. Simultaneous bubbling during plasma treatment consistently maximized H2O2, NO2-, and NO3- concentrations, alongside a more pronounced decrease in pH and increase in ORP, compared to plasma-only treatment. This enhancement is attributed to improved gas-liquid mass transfer and continuous replenishment of atmospheric gases, supporting RONS formation. While post-plasma bubbling aided RONS stability, concurrent plasma activation and bubbling was optimal for initial RONS generation. These findings highlight a simple, effective strategy to intensify PAW's active species production and stability, expanding its applications in agriculture, sterilization, and biomedicine.

title: The effects of water temperature on gastric motility and energy intake in healthy young men.
text_ai: Although immediate pre-meal water ingestion has been shown to reduce energy intake in healthy young men, no studies are available regarding potential mechanisms underlying the effect of energy intake in response to different temperatures of pre-meal water ingestion. This study examined the effects of consuming different temperatures of water on gastric motility and energy intake in healthy young men. Twenty healthy young men participated in a randomized, crossover study. Participants consumed 500 mL of water at three different temperatures (4°C, 22°C, or 50°C) 30 minutes prior to an *ad libitum* standardized test meal. Gastric emptying rate was assessed via real-time ultrasonography, and subjective ratings of hunger, fullness, and satiety were collected using visual analogue scales (VAS). Energy intake was quantified by weighing the consumed meal. Results showed that gastric emptying was significantly accelerated following 4°C water ingestion compared to 22°C and 50°C water (p < 0.01). Despite these differences in gastric motility, there was no significant effect of water temperature on subsequent *ad libitum* energy intake (p = 0.45), with participants consuming similar amounts across all conditions. Subjective satiety ratings were transiently higher after 50°C water ingestion compared to 4°C, but this did not translate to reduced energy intake. This study demonstrates that while water temperature acutely influences gastric emptying, this physiological modulation does not appear to directly alter energy intake in healthy young men. The findings suggest that the previously observed effect of pre-meal water on energy intake may be mediated by mechanisms independent of acute temperature-induced gastric motility changes. Further research is warranted to explore other potential temperature-dependent gastrointestinal or neural mechanisms.

title: Energy-Based Flow Matching for Generating 3D Molecular Structure
text_ai: Molecular structure generation is a fundamental problem that involves determining the 3D positions of molecules' constituents. It has crucial biological applications, such as molecular docking, protein folding, and molecular design. Recent advances in generative modeling, such as diffusion models and flow matching, have made great progress on these tasks by modeling molecular conformations as a distribution. However, these models often lack explicit mechanisms to ensure the physical stability and chemical validity of generated structures, which are dictated by their underlying energy landscapes. To address this, we introduce **Energy-Based Flow Matching (EBFM)**, a novel generative framework that explicitly incorporates molecular potential energy functions into the continuous flow matching process. EBFM leverages the gradient of a learned or predefined energy function to guide the transformation from a simple prior distribution to the intricate manifold of stable molecular conformations. This energy-guided approach inherently promotes the generation of physically plausible and chemically stable 3D molecular structures. We demonstrate that EBFM significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on various molecular generation benchmarks, producing structures with superior energy stability and better adherence to chemical validity metrics, while maintaining competitive generation efficiency. Our work represents a significant advance towards developing more robust and physically informed generative models for molecular design and discovery.

It has crucial biological applications, such as molecular docking, protein folding, and molecular design. title: Adaptive sports for promoting physical activity in community-dwelling adults with stroke: A feasibility study.
text_ai: Despite proven health benefits of regular participation in physical activities (PA), adults with stroke fail to achieve recommended levels of PA. Sports being an enjoyable activity is more likely to encourage participation. This study aimed to assess the feasibility and acceptability of a 12-week adaptive sports program to increase PA in community-dwelling adults with chronic stroke. A single-arm, prospective feasibility study recruited ten community-dwelling adults (>6 months post-stroke). Participants engaged in thrice-weekly sessions of adaptive cycling, seated volleyball, and boccia. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, attendance, safety, and participant satisfaction. PA was objectively measured via accelerometry and self-reported (PASIPD) at baseline and post-intervention. Recruitment was challenging (30% enrollment rate). However, retention was high (90%), with participants completing 85% of sessions. No serious adverse events occurred; minor musculoskeletal discomfort was reported by two. Participants reported high enjoyment, social engagement, and perceived functional improvements. Preliminary PA data showed a non-significant trend toward increased moderate-to-vigorous PA (+45 minutes/week) and a significant increase in PASIPD scores (p < 0.05). Despite recruitment hurdles, the adaptive sports program demonstrated promising feasibility and high acceptability. It appears safe and enjoyable, with preliminary evidence suggesting increased PA. These findings support a larger randomized controlled trial to evaluate adaptive sports' effectiveness in promoting long-term PA adherence in adults with stroke.
prefix: Despite proven health benefits of regular participation in physical activities (PA), adults with stroke fail to achieve recommended levels of PA. Sports being an enjoyable activity is more likely to encourage participation.

title: Properties of the $\eta_q$ leading-twist distribution amplitude and its effects to the $B/D^+ \to\eta^{(\prime)}\ell^+ \nu_\ell$ decays
text_ai: The $\eta^{(\prime)}$-mesons in the quark-flavor basis are mixtures of two mesonic states $|\eta_{q}\rangle=|\bar u u+\bar d d\rangle/\sqrt 2$ and $|\eta_{s}\rangle=|\bar s s\rangle$. In the previous work, we have made a detailed study on the $\eta_{s}$ leading-twist distribution amplitude. Building upon that, this work provides a comprehensive analysis of the $\eta_q$ leading-twist distribution amplitude (DA). Employing the light-cone QCD sum rule approach, we systematically determine its first few Gegenbauer moments, crucial for characterizing its shape and providing essential input for phenomenological calculations. Subsequently, we investigate the impact of these newly constrained $\eta_q$ DA properties on the semileptonic decays $B/D^+ \to\eta^{(\prime)}\ell^+ \nu_\ell$. We calculate the relevant form factors within light-cone QCD sum rules, incorporating both $\eta_q$ and $\eta_s$ DAs and meticulously accounting for $\eta-\eta'$ mixing effects. Our predictions for branching ratios and differential decay distributions are presented, compared with experimental data and other theoretical estimates. This study offers improved insights into the internal structure of $\eta^{(\prime)}$ mesons and provides precise tests of the Standard Model, emphasizing the necessity of accurate $\eta_q$ DA knowledge for precision flavor physics.

title: Minimization based formulations of inverse problems and their regularization
text_ai: The conventional way of formulating inverse problems such as identification of a (possibly infinite dimensional) parameter, is via some forward operator, which is the concatenation of the observation operator with the parameter-to-state-map for the underlying model. This setup invariably leads to an ill-posed problem, characterized by non-uniqueness of solutions, extreme sensitivity to measurement noise, and often, non-existence in a classical sense. Consequently, inverse problems are commonly reformulated as minimization problems, where the objective is to find a parameter that optimally fits the observed data, typically by minimizing a data misfit functional (e.g., L2-norm discrepancy). However, such unregularized minimization problems inherit the inherent ill-posedness, rendering their solutions unstable and non-unique. Regularization is therefore crucial, transforming the ill-posed problem into a well-posed one by introducing additional constraints or penalties that incorporate prior knowledge about the desired parameter. This paper explores a range of minimization-based formulations, from standard Tikhonov-type regularization to more advanced sparsity-promoting methods such as L1-norm or total variation (TV) regularization. We analyze their mathematical foundations, discuss their effectiveness in promoting stability and incorporating specific solution characteristics (e.g., smoothness, piecewise constancy, sparsity), and examine their performance across various applications. Special attention is given to the selection of regularization parameters and the computational algorithms required to solve the resulting optimization problems. The overarching goal is to provide a systematic exposition of these methods, highlighting their theoretical properties and practical implications for robust and accurate parameter identification across diverse scientific and engineering fields.
prefix: The conventional way of formulating inverse problems such as identification of a (possibly infinite dimensional) parameter, is via some forward operator, which is the concatenation of the observation operator with the parameter-to-state-map for the underlying model.

title: Challenges in the thermal modeling of highly porous carbon foams
text_ai: The heat pulse experiment is a well-known method for determining thermal diffusivity. However, neither the measurement nor the evaluation methodologies are straightforward for heterogeneous, highly porous materials. In the present paper, we focus on two open-cell carbon foam types, differing in their porosity but having the same size. We investigate the limitations of traditional analytical models, which often assume homogeneous and purely conductive heat transfer, when applied to these complex structures. Our study employs a combination of advanced experimental techniques and detailed numerical simulations that incorporate coupled heat transfer mechanisms including conduction, convection, and radiation within the porous matrix. We demonstrate that the standard one-dimensional heat diffusion analysis yields significantly inaccurate thermal diffusivity values, especially for the higher porosity samples, due to the pronounced effects of internal radiation and interstitial fluid convection. The non-uniform temperature evolution observed experimentally underscores the breakdown of conventional assumptions. This work highlights the critical need for sophisticated modeling approaches and refined experimental protocols to accurately characterize the thermal transport properties of highly porous carbon foams, providing crucial insights for their design and application in high-performance thermal management systems.

However, neither the measurement nor the evaluation methodologies are straightforward for heterogeneous, highly porous materials. In the present paper, we focus on two open-cell carbon foam types, differing in their porosity but having the same size.

title: Immunofluorescence Capillary Imaging Segmentation: Cases Study
text_ai: Nonunion is one of the challenges faced by orthopedics clinics for the technical difficulties and high costs in photographing interosseous capillaries. Segmenting vessels and filling capillaries are critical in understanding the obstacles encountered in capillary growth. This study introduces an innovative immunofluorescence imaging segmentation technique for precise identification and quantification of interosseous capillaries. Utilizing advanced image processing algorithms, our method automates capillary delineation even in dense tissues, reducing manual effort and subjectivity. Our robust segmentation framework integrates morphological operations with intensity-based thresholding, optimized for immunofluorescence micrographs. This enhances segmentation accuracy and provides quantitative measures of capillary density and morphology, vital for assessing vascularization in compromised healing environments. A comprehensive case study of persistent nonunion demonstrates our model's practical applicability and superior performance in visualizing and analyzing capillary networks. The findings highlight its potential to deepen understanding of angiogenesis dynamics in bone repair, offering an objective, cost-effective tool for diagnosing, monitoring, and guiding targeted nonunion interventions.

title: Clinical and functional outcome of open primary repair of triangular fibrocartilage complex tears associated with distal radius fractures
text_ai: PURPOSE: We evaluate the clinical and functional outcome of open primary repair of acute TFCC tears in distal radius fracture, when there is gross intraoperative distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) instability after fixation of the distal radius, in the absence of an ulnar styloid fracture or when the ulnar fracture fragment is too small to be fixed. METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 28 patients (mean age 42.5 years) undergoing open primary TFCC repair for acute DRUJ instability following distal radius fixation, as per the specified criteria, was analyzed. Clinical and functional outcomes were assessed at a mean follow-up of 36 months using the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (DASH) score, Mayo Wrist Score (MWS), Patient-Rated Wrist Evaluation (PRWE) score, grip strength, and range of motion. RESULTS: At final follow-up, all functional scores significantly improved (p < 0.001). Mean DASH score decreased from 58.2 ± 12.5 preoperatively to 15.1 ± 8.7. Mayo Wrist Score improved from 42.8 ± 10.1 to 87.5 ± 7.2, and PRWE decreased from 68.5 ± 15.3 to 18.3 ± 9.1. Grip strength recovered to an average of 85% of the contralateral side. All patients achieved stable and pain-free DRUJ motion with excellent range of motion. One minor complication (superficial wound infection) was observed and resolved uneventfully. CONCLUSION: Open primary repair of acute TFCC tears associated with distal radius fractures, with gross DRUJ instability after stable radius fixation and without a fixable ulnar styloid fracture, yields excellent clinical and functional outcomes, effectively restoring DRUJ stability and promoting pain-free wrist function.
prefix: PURPOSE: We evaluate the clinical and functional outcome of open primary repair of acute TFCC tears in distal radius fracture, when there is gross intraoperative distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) instability after fixation of the distal radius, in the absence of an ulnar styloid fracture or when the ulnar fracture fragment is too small to be fixed.

title: The Implications of Local Fluctuations in the Galactic Midplane for Dynamical Analysis in the Gaia Era
text_ai: Orbital properties of stars, computed from their six-dimensional phase space measurements and an assumed Galactic potential, are used to understand the structure and evolution of the Galaxy. Stellar actions, computed from orbits, have the attractive quality of being invariant under certain assumptions and are therefore used as quantitative labels of a star's orbit. However, the idealized assumptions of a smooth, static, and often axisymmetric Galactic potential, upon which the strict invariance of actions relies, are increasingly challenged by observational evidence. The Galactic midplane is characterized by significant non-axisymmetric and time-dependent features like spiral arms, the bar, and various substructures. These localized fluctuations perturb the gravitational field, causing stellar orbits to deviate from idealized paths and potentially altering their actions. The unprecedented astrometric precision of the Gaia mission means these subtle orbital alterations, previously considered negligible, are now detectable and critically important for accurate dynamical analysis. This paper investigates the sensitivity of stellar actions to these realistic, localized fluctuations. We demonstrate how neglecting such transient and non-axisymmetric features can systematically bias derived orbital properties, impacting age-velocity dispersion relations, chemodynamical tagging, and the inference of Galactic structure and evolution. We explore the limitations of standard action-angle formalisms in dynamic environments and propose strategies for quantifying and mitigating these effects, aiming for more robust analyses in the high-precision Gaia era.
prefix: Orbital properties of stars, computed from their six-dimensional phase space measurements and an assumed Galactic potential, are used to understand the structure and evolution of the Galaxy. title: How Black Holes Stop Their Host Galaxy from Growing Without AGN Feedback
text_ai: Super-massive black holes (SMBHs) with $M_{\bullet} \sim 10^9 $ M$_{\odot}$ at $z>6$ likely originate from massive seed black holes (BHs). We investigate the consequences of seeding SMBHs with direct collapse BHs (DCBHs) ($M_{\bullet}=10^{4-6}\, \mathrm{M}_\odot$) on proto-galactic disc growth. Using high-resolution hydrodynamical simulations, we demonstrate that a massive DCBH impacts its host proto-galaxy's gas dynamics and star formation. Its deep gravitational potential drives rapid, efficient gas infall directly onto the BH, leading to its growth and early central gas depletion. This intense accretion starves the host region, suppressing massive stellar disc formation and inhibiting subsequent star formation. This quenching mechanism operates through the massive seed's gravitational influence and direct gas consumption, maintaining a hotter, diffuse atmosphere unlike energetic outflows or radiative pressure of typical AGN feedback. This novel pathway suggests that a massive seed BH's existence and initial growth self-regulate host galaxy development, forming compact, quiescent galaxies at high redshifts without strong AGN-driven feedback. Our results offer an alternative explanation for observed massive, quiescent galaxies in the early Universe, providing insights into SMBH-host galaxy co-evolution from the earliest cosmic epochs.

title: Position-Constrained Stochastic Inference for Cooperative Indoor Localization
text_ai: We address the problem of distributed cooperative localization in wireless networks, i.e. nodes without prior position knowledge (agents) wish to determine their own positions. In non-cooperative approaches, positioning is only based on information from reference nodes with known positions (anchors). However, in cooperative positioning, information from other agents is considered as well. This is crucial indoors where anchor line-of-sight is frequently obstructed, degrading non-cooperative performance. However, conventional cooperative methods often struggle with ambiguity and slow convergence, especially with sparse anchors. To address this, we propose a novel **position-constrained stochastic inference** framework. It explicitly integrates prior spatial knowledge, such as building floor plans, as geometric constraints into the probabilistic localization process. This integration effectively prunes geometrically inconsistent hypotheses, guiding state estimation towards physically plausible locations. Formulated within a Bayesian inference framework, our distributed algorithm leverages inter-agent range measurements and anchor observations. The proposed method significantly enhances cooperative indoor localization accuracy and robustness, particularly in challenging non-line-of-sight conditions. Extensive evaluations demonstrate our position-constrained approach consistently outperforms existing techniques, achieving superior performance in complex indoor scenarios with limited anchor visibility and high uncertainty.

title: SCOUT: Teaching Pre-trained Language Models to Enhance Reasoning via Flow Chain-of-Thought
text_ai: Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting improves the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs) by encouraging step by step thinking. However, CoT-based methods depend on intermediate reasoning steps, which limits scalability and generalization. Recent work explores recursive reasoning, where LLMs reuse internal layers across iterations to refine latent representations without explicit CoT supervision. Building on this, we introduce SCOUT (Scalable Chain-of-Thought Understanding), a novel framework designed to teach pre-trained language models to enhance reasoning through a "Flow Chain-of-Thought" (FCoT). SCOUT moves beyond discrete, explicit reasoning steps by enabling models to learn a continuous, latent reasoning trajectory. This is achieved by iteratively refining an internal reasoning state via a series of specialized, lightweight transformation modules, akin to a learned inner monologue. During training, SCOUT utilizes a self-supervision mechanism that encourages the model to generate coherent and progressively refined reasoning states, even without explicit human-annotated CoT demonstrations. This 'flow' allows for more flexible and robust progression towards a solution, mitigating common pitfalls like error propagation and lack of generalization inherent in fixed-step CoT methods. Our approach effectively guides the model to autonomously identify and traverse optimal reasoning paths within its latent space. We evaluate SCOUT across a diverse suite of complex reasoning benchmarks, including arithmetic, symbolic logic, and commonsense question answering. Empirical results demonstrate that SCOUT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art CoT-based methods and other recursive reasoning techniques, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, SCOUT exhibits superior computational efficiency and requires fewer explicit prompts, highlighting its potential for developing more autonomous and scalable reasoning capabilities in large language models.

title: New interventions to treat chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
text_ai: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) can be defined as a type of precapillary pulmonary hypertension (PH) resulting from incomplete resolution of pulmonary embolism. Symptoms are exertional breathlessness and most patients come to a cardiologist's attention with a dilated right heart on echocardiography. While pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) remains the potentially curative treatment for patients with surgically accessible disease, a substantial proportion of CTEPH patients are deemed inoperable due to the distal location of their disease or significant comorbidities, while others experience persistent or recurrent PH following PEA. This unmet clinical need has driven the development and refinement of alternative therapeutic strategies. Balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) has emerged as a transformative catheter-based intervention for patients with technically inoperable CTEPH or residual disease post-PEA. This procedure involves sequential dilatation of stenotic pulmonary arteries, aiming to improve pulmonary blood flow and reduce pulmonary vascular resistance, with growing evidence demonstrating significant hemodynamic and symptomatic benefits. Concurrently, pulmonary hypertension-specific pharmacotherapies, including endothelin receptor antagonists, phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors, and soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators, initially developed for idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension, are increasingly being utilized in CTEPH. These agents serve to improve hemodynamics, enhance functional capacity, and potentially act as a bridge to surgery or as long-term management for inoperable or residual cases. This review critically evaluates the mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety profiles, and evolving role of BPA and targeted medical therapies within the multidisciplinary management algorithm for CTEPH, highlighting their potential to optimize outcomes for this complex patient population.

title: Optimal liquidation for a risk averse investor in a one-sided limit order book driven by a Levy process
text_ai: In a one-sided limit order book, satisfying some realistic assumptions, where the unaffected price process follows a Levy process, we consider a market agent that wants to liquidate a large position of shares. We assume that the agent has constant absolute risk aversion and aims at maximising the expected utility of the cash position at the end of time. We formulate this problem as a stochastic optimal control problem, where the agent dynamically determines the rate of market order submission to liquidate their position. The underlying Levy process introduces both continuous price movements and sudden jumps, profoundly influencing the optimal trading strategy. We derive the optimal liquidation policy and the corresponding value function by solving the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. Our analysis reveals that higher risk aversion systematically leads to more aggressive liquidation, prioritising certainty over potential price gains. The Levy process characteristics, particularly the frequency and magnitude of jumps, introduce a trade-off between immediate execution and waiting for advantageous price movements. We provide a detailed characterisation of the optimal policy, illustrating how it adapts to market conditions and investor preferences, and discuss its implications for practical implementation.

title: Anticancer and cancer preventive compounds from edible marine organisms.
text_ai: A direct impact of food on health, which demonstrates that dietary habit is one of the most important determinants of chronic diseases such as cancers, has led to an increased interest of the consumers toward natural bioactive compounds as functional ingredients or nutraceuticals. Among various natural sources, marine organisms represent an underexplored reservoir of structurally diverse and biologically potent molecules. Their unique evolutionary adaptations to extreme marine environments have resulted in the biosynthesis of secondary metabolites with distinct chemical structures and promising pharmacological activities. This paper reviews the current knowledge on anticancer and cancer preventive compounds isolated from edible marine species, including algae, invertebrates (e.g., crustaceans, mollusks, echinoderms), and fish. These marine-derived compounds, encompassing polysaccharides, peptides, carotenoids, polyunsaturated fatty acids, and polyphenols, exhibit diverse mechanisms of action, such as inhibition of cell proliferation, induction of apoptosis, anti-angiogenesis, and modulation of immune responses. We critically discuss the potential of these bioactive ingredients as functional foods or as leads for novel pharmaceutical development against various cancer types.

title: Voltage Estimation in Low-Voltage Distribution Grids with Distributed Energy Resources
text_ai: The present distribution grids generally have limited sensing capabilities and are therefore characterized by low observability. Improved observability is a prerequisite for increasing the hosting capacity of distributed energy resources such as solar photovoltaics (PV) in distribution grids. In this context, this paper presents learning-aided low-voltage estimation using untapped but readily available and widely distributed sensors from cable television (CATV) networks. It details a novel data-driven framework leveraging widespread CATV infrastructure co-located with LV grids. The methodology utilizes readily available CATV operational metrics (e.g., signal levels) as indirect indicators, training a machine learning model to correlate them with nodal voltages. This transforms the CATV network into a pervasive, cost-effective virtual sensing layer, circumventing dedicated grid measurement units. Rigorous validation on realistic LV grid models with varying PV penetration demonstrates high accuracy; the estimator consistently achieves a mean absolute error below 0.5% in nodal voltage prediction across diverse conditions. This significantly enhances grid observability, facilitating advanced control and enabling increased DER hosting capacity.

title: Nuclear dimension and Z-stability of pure C*-algebras
text_ai: In this article I study a number of topological and algebraic dimension type properties of simple C*-algebras and their interplay. In particular, a simple C*-algebra is defined to be (tracially) (m,\bar{m})-pure, if it has (strong tracial) m-comparison and is (tracially) \bar{m}-almost divisible. These notions are related to each other, and to nuclear dimension. We demonstrate that (tracial) (m,$\bar{m}$)-purity provides a unified framework for understanding the interplay between comparison properties and approximate divisibility in simple C*-algebras. Our main result establishes that a simple, separable, nuclear C*-algebra with finite nuclear dimension is Z-stable if and only if it is (tracially) (m,$\bar{m}$)-pure for some m and $\bar{m}$. This generalizes previous characterizations of Z-stability, offering a refined understanding of the structural properties that imply absorption of the Jiang-Su algebra $\mathcal{Z}$. We further investigate the relationship between these purity notions and nuclear dimension. We prove that C*-algebras with finite nuclear dimension and strong tracial m-comparison are necessarily (tracially) $\bar{m}$-almost divisible for suitable $\bar{m}$, establishing a deep connection between these dimensional invariants. Conversely, we show that (tracially) (m,$\bar{m}$)-pure C*-algebras often possess finite nuclear dimension under certain regularity assumptions, clarifying purity's role in determining the amenability properties of the algebra. These findings contribute significantly to the classification program of simple, separable, nuclear C*-algebras, offering new tools and insights into the structural properties characterizing Z-stability.

title: Towards An Efficient LLM Training Paradigm for CTR Prediction
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated tremendous potential as the next-generation ranking-based recommendation system. Many recent works have shown that LLMs can significantly outperform conventional click-through-rate (CTR) prediction approaches. Despite such promising results, the computational inefficiency inherent in the current training paradigm makes it particularly challenging to train LLMs for ranking-based recommendation tasks on large datasets. This inefficiency primarily arises from the substantial parameter counts inherent in LLMs and the vast, dynamic nature of user-item interaction data characteristic of real-world CTR prediction tasks. Traditional full fine-tuning approaches demand extensive computational resources and prolonged training times, rendering them impractical for frequent model updates or deployment in resource-constrained environments. To address these critical challenges, this paper introduces a novel, efficient training paradigm specifically tailored for LLMs in CTR prediction. Our approach integrates several key innovations: first, a lightweight, domain-adaptive pre-training strategy distills relevant recommendation knowledge into a more compact model representation. Second, we incorporate a sophisticated parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) mechanism, judiciously updating only a small fraction of model parameters while freezing the majority, significantly reducing computational overhead during adaptation. Finally, a hierarchical knowledge distillation framework compresses learned representations from a powerful teacher LLM into a smaller student model, optimizing both training speed and inference latency. Extensive experiments on multiple large-scale datasets demonstrate that our proposed paradigm substantially reduces training time and GPU memory consumption compared to conventional full fine-tuning, while achieving comparable or superior CTR prediction performance. This work paves the way for the practical and scalable deployment of LLMs as formidable ranking models in real-world recommendation systems.

title: MAP Estimation, Message Passing, and Perfect Graphs
text_ai: Efficiently finding the maximum a posteriori (MAP) configuration of a graphical model is an important problem which is often implemented using message passing algorithms. The optimality of such algorithms is only well established for singly-connected graphs and other limited settings. For general loopy graphs, however, these algorithms lack theoretical guarantees for convergence or optimality. This paper investigates perfect graphs, a structurally rich class, for exact MAP estimation. We show that for graphical models on perfect graphs, the MAP problem can be solved exactly in polynomial time. We propose a novel message passing scheme leveraging inherent decomposition properties of perfect graphs, extending exact inference beyond tree structures. Our approach rigorously establishes MAP optimality for this broader class of models. The algorithm is proven to converge to the true MAP configuration, offering a tractable and guaranteed method for exact MAP inference on perfect graphs. This opens new avenues for exact inference in complex scenarios.

title: The Mystery of Two Straight Lines in Bacterial Genome Statistics. Release 2007
text_ai: In special coordinates (codon position--specific nucleotide frequencies) bacterial genomes form two straight lines in 9-dimensional space: one line for eubacterial genomes, another for archaeal genomes. All the 348 distinct bacterial genomes available in Genbank in April 2007, belong to these lines with high accuracy. The main challenge now is to explain the observed high accuracy. This paper investigates potential biological and evolutionary factors that constrain genome composition to these precise linear manifolds. We hypothesize that these lines reflect deeply conserved, yet distinct, genomic architectures between Eubacteria and Archaea, potentially linked to fundamental differences in their replication, transcription, or translation machinery, or to distinct adaptive strategies. Through rigorous statistical analysis and comparative genomics of the 348 genomes, we demonstrate that this linearity is a robust feature of bacterial genome organization, not a statistical artifact. We identify key genomic parameters defining the slopes and intercepts of these lines, suggesting they represent universal constraints on nucleotide composition across broad phylogenetic groups. Understanding the origins of these relationships offers novel insights into the forces shaping bacterial genome evolution and provides a powerful statistical framework for microbial genome classification and analysis. This study thus opens new avenues for exploring foundational principles governing prokaryotic life.

title: Repeated end range spinal movement while seated abolishes the proprioceptive deficit induced by prolonged flexed sitting posture. A study assessing the statistical and clinical significance of spinal position sense.
text_ai: Sustained spinal flexion has been proposed to affect the properties of spinal tissues, increase postural muscle's activation latency and act detrimentally on proprioception. This study evaluated the effect of flexed posture (FP) on spinal proprioception and assessed the immediate effect of spinal movement on the presumable flexion-induced proprioceptive deficit. Thirty healthy individuals were recruited for this randomized crossover study. Spinal position sense (SPS) was quantified as the absolute error (AE) in degrees during repositioning to a target neutral lumbar posture, using a 3D motion capture system. Participants completed three conditions on separate days: 30 minutes of sustained flexed sitting (FP), 30 minutes of neutral sitting (Control), and 30 minutes of FP immediately followed by 10 repetitions of seated end-range lumbar extension and flexion movements (FP+ERSM). Results revealed a statistically significant increase in AE following the FP condition compared to Control (p < 0.001), indicating a proprioceptive deficit. Critically, the FP+ERSM condition abolished this deficit, with AE returning to baseline levels and significantly differing from FP (p < 0.001). The observed improvement surpassed established minimal detectable change values, confirming clinical significance. These findings demonstrate that prolonged flexed sitting impairs spinal proprioception, and that simple, repeated end-range spinal movements can immediately restore spinal position sense. Incorporating such movements into daily routines may offer a practical strategy to mitigate the detrimental effects of sedentary postures on proprioceptive function and musculoskeletal health.

title: Evaluation of nerve capture using classical landmarks for genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation: 3D cadaveric study.
text_ai: Radiofrequency (RF) denervation of the superolateral genicular nerve (SLGN), superomedial genicular nerve (SMGN) and inferomedial genicular nerve (IMGN) is commonly used to manage chronic knee joint pain. However, knowledge of articular branches captured, using classical landmarking techniques, remains unclear. This 3D cadaveric study aimed to precisely quantify the capture rate and proximity of the SLGN, SMGN, and IMGN using established surface anatomical landmarks for RF ablation, and to identify any collateral nerve involvement. Ten fresh-frozen cadaveric knees (n=20 limbs) underwent percutaneous RF needle insertion at classical landmark positions. High-resolution micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) generated detailed 3D reconstructions of the knee, tissues, and needles. Subsequent anatomical dissection allowed precise measurement of needle-to-target nerve distances and proximity to adjacent neural structures. Our findings revealed significant variability in target nerve capture. The SLGN was consistently captured within 2mm of the needle tip in most cases, but SMGN and IMGN capture proved inconsistent, often requiring repositioning. Notably, needles were frequently in close proximity to or directly captured non-target articular branches or major neurovascular structures (e.g., saphenous and common peroneal nerve branches), raising concerns for off-target effects. These results underscore the anatomical variability of genicular nerves and highlight the potential for inconsistent nerve capture and collateral damage when relying solely on classical surface landmarks. The study emphasizes the need for image guidance (e.g., fluoroscopy or ultrasound) to enhance precision and improve patient safety during genicular nerve RF ablation.

title: Loewner Theory in annulus I: evolution families and differential equations
text_ai: Loewner Theory, based on dynamical viewpoint, is a powerful tool in Complex Analysis, which plays a crucial role in such important achievements as the proof of famous Bieberbach's conjecture and well-celebrated Schramm's Stochastic Loewner Evolution (SLE). Recently Bracci et al [Bracci et al, to appear in J. Reine Angew. Math. ] introduced a novel framework for Loewner theory applicable to certain multiply connected domains. Building upon these advancements, this paper is the first in a series dedicated to establishing a comprehensive Loewner theory for the annulus. We define and rigorously analyze evolution families of univalent functions that map the annulus conformally into subdomains of itself, characterized by specific growth or shrinking processes. These families are shown to be governed by a system of Loewner-type differential equations, driven by functions on both the inner and outer boundaries of the annulus. We prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions to these equations and explore the fundamental properties of the generated maps, including their semigroup property and connection to slit mappings. This work provides the essential analytical tools for understanding complex dynamics and geometric properties of functions in annular regions.

title: Entanglement distillation based on polarization and frequency hyperentanglement
text_ai: Entanglement distillation has many applications in quantum information processing and is an important tool for improving the quality and efficiency of quantum communication, cryptography, computing, and simulation. We propose an entanglement distillation scheme using only one pair of polarization-frequency hyperentangled photons, which can be equivalently viewed as containing two pairs of entangled logical qubits: a pair of polarization-entangled qubits and a pair of frequency-entangled qubits. This approach leverages the inherent correlation between these two entangled degrees of freedom to enable efficient purification. By performing appropriate local operations on one degree of freedom, such as frequency-domain manipulation, the entanglement quality of the other degree of freedom, polarization, can be significantly enhanced. Our scheme details a specific protocol involving only linear optical elements and single-photon measurements, making it experimentally feasible with current technology. We demonstrate that this method can effectively increase the fidelity of both polarization and frequency entanglement simultaneously, or selectively purify one degree of freedom while sacrificing the other, depending on the desired application. The proposed scheme offers a higher success probability and improved resource efficiency compared to traditional distillation protocols requiring multiple entangled pairs, paving the way for more robust and scalable quantum networks.

title: Advice Complexity of Adaptive Priority Algorithms
text_ai: The priority model was introduced to capture "greedy-like" algorithms. Motivated by the success of advice complexity in the area of online algorithms, the fixed priority model was extended to include advice, and a reduction-based framework was developed for proving lower bounds on the amount of advice required to achieve certain approximation ratios in this rather powerful model. This paper extends this line of inquiry by introducing advice complexity to *adaptive* priority algorithms, a more powerful variant where item priorities can change dynamically during algorithm execution. We develop a comprehensive framework to analyze the advice complexity of such adaptive algorithms, addressing their increased flexibility and potential for improved performance. Our investigation focuses on several classic combinatorial optimization problems, including scheduling on parallel machines and maximum weight independent set. For these problems, we establish novel lower bounds on the amount of advice required by adaptive priority algorithms to achieve specific approximation guarantees. Furthermore, we provide corresponding upper bounds by designing new adaptive priority algorithms that utilize advice to match these theoretical limits. A key finding is that adaptivity, when combined with advice, can significantly reduce the advice complexity compared to fixed priority algorithms for certain problem classes, often leading to optimal solutions with only a logarithmic or constant amount of advice. Conversely, we identify inherent limitations, showing that for other problems, even adaptive priority algorithms require substantial advice to achieve high-quality approximations. This work provides a refined understanding of the computational power of adaptive priority algorithms in the presence of external information, shedding light on the trade-offs between algorithm flexibility, information access, and solution quality.

title: On the ubiquity of duopolies in constant sum congestion games
text_ai: We analyse a coalition formation game between strategic service providers of a congestible service. The key novelty of our formulation is that it is a constant sum game, i.e., the total payoff across all service providers (or coalitions of providers) is fixed, and dictated by the size of the market. Within this constant sum framework, providers strategically form coalitions to maximize their collective market share. Utilizing cooperative game theory, we analyze coalition stability and the resulting market structures. Our central finding is the robust emergence of duopolies. We demonstrate that, across diverse market conditions, stable coalition formation invariably leads to a market dominated by precisely two major service providers. This ubiquity stems from a delicate balance: larger coalitions face internal instability, while fragmented markets incentivize profitable mergers. The duopoly, therefore, represents a unique and robust equilibrium. These results offer a compelling theoretical explanation for duopoly prevalence in various industries, underscoring the constant sum payoff structure's critical role in shaping market concentration.

title: Quantum secret sharing for a multipartite system under energy dissipation
text_ai: We propose a protocol for multipartite secret sharing of quantum information through an \textit{amplitude damping} quantum channel. This network is, for example, of two organizations communicating with their own employees connected via classical channels locally. We consider a GHZ state distributed among four members in an asymmetric fashion where the members of a sub-party collaborate to decode the received information at their end. Our scheme employs a set of local unitary operations and classical communication (LOCC) by the dealer to encode the quantum secret onto the distributed GHZ state. The members of a designated sub-party then cooperatively perform specific measurements and classical information exchange to reconstruct the secret, establishing a threshold sharing mechanism. We rigorously analyze the fidelity of the recovered quantum secret as a function of the amplitude damping parameter, demonstrating the protocol's performance under increasing channel noise. Our findings reveal the critical impact of decoherence on the security and reliability of the shared information. Crucially, we identify specific conditions and strategies that enable a high-fidelity reconstruction even in the presence of significant energy dissipation. This protocol thus presents a robust and practical framework for secure quantum information transfer in realistic, noisy quantum communication networks.

title: Effect of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation on Pain Management: A Systematic Narrative Review
text_ai: Recently, clinicians have been using repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for treating various pain conditions. This systematic narrative review aimed to examine the use and efficacy of rTMS for controlling various pain conditions. A PubMed search was conducted for articles that were published until June 7, 2019 and used rTMS for pain alleviation. The search yielded 287 articles; 45 studies meeting predefined inclusion criteria (original research, human studies, rTMS intervention, pain outcome assessment) were included for detailed narrative review. Studies covered diverse chronic pain conditions (e.g., neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, chronic low back pain). Despite heterogeneous rTMS protocols, a consistent theme emerged: significant short-term pain reduction. High-frequency rTMS over the primary motor cortex (M1) contralateral to the pain site was generally effective. Beyond pain relief, some studies reported improvements in mood and quality of life. However, long-term efficacy remained less robust and inconsistent across studies. Common limitations included methodological variability, small sample sizes, and lack of standardized sham controls. This review concludes rTMS holds promising potential as a non-invasive neuromodulatory intervention for chronic pain management. Future large-scale, rigorously designed, sham-controlled, and long-term studies are essential to establish optimal parameters, identify predictors of response, and confirm sustained therapeutic benefits.

title: Self-Refine Instruction-Tuning for Aligning Reasoning in Language Models
text_ai: The alignments of reasoning abilities between smaller and larger Language Models are largely conducted via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) using demonstrations generated from robust Large Language Models (LLMs). Although these approaches deliver more performant models, they do not show sufficiently strong generalization ability as the training only relies on the provided demonstrations. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Refine Instruction-Tuning, a novel framework designed to enhance reasoning alignment and generalization. Unlike traditional SFT, our method empowers the student model to iteratively refine and augment its own training data by generating diverse problem-solving paths and critically evaluating their correctness and coherence. This iterative self-correction mechanism leverages the model's evolving capabilities to produce higher-quality, more varied reasoning demonstrations, moving beyond fixed initial examples. By actively participating in data generation and refinement, the model develops a deeper understanding of underlying reasoning principles, leading to significantly improved generalization across unseen tasks and domains. Our experiments demonstrate that models trained with Self-Refine Instruction-Tuning achieve superior performance on complex reasoning benchmarks compared to SFT-only approaches. Furthermore, this self-supervised augmentation fosters a more robust and transferable alignment of reasoning abilities, effectively closing the performance gap between smaller models and their larger counterparts.

title: MVGrasp: Real-Time Multi-View 3D Object Grasping in Highly Cluttered Environments
text_ai: Nowadays robots play an increasingly important role in our daily life. In human-centered environments, robots often encounter piles of objects, packed items, or isolated objects. Therefore, a robot must be able to grasp and manipulate different objects in various situations to help humans with daily tasks. However, grasping in highly cluttered environments presents significant challenges due to severe object occlusion, varied geometries, and the imperative for robust 3D perception. Traditional single-view 2D methods often struggle with accurate pose estimation under such conditions. To overcome these limitations, we introduce MVGrasp, a novel real-time multi-view 3D object grasping system designed for highly cluttered scenes. MVGrasp fuses information from multiple depth and RGB cameras to generate a comprehensive 3D environmental understanding. Our approach employs a deep learning framework that directly predicts robust 6-Degree-of-Freedom grasp poses for unknown and occluded objects, leveraging this rich multi-view 3D data. Optimized for real-time operation, MVGrasp ensures practical applicability. Extensive evaluations demonstrate its superior grasp success rates and robustness compared to existing state-of-the-art methods, particularly in dense clutter, marking a significant advancement in robotic manipulation for unstructured human-centered settings.

title: Development and clinical study of submicronic-atropine sulphate respiratory fluid as a novel organophosphorous poisoning antidote.
text_ai: Increased use of organophosphate insecticides (OPI) and possibility of terror groups using stocks of nerve agents underscore the need to develop effective and safe antidotes. While intramuscular administration of antidotes like atropine sulphate (AS) has certain lacunae, intravenous route may not be always feasible in emergency field conditions. This study developed and clinically evaluated a novel submicronic-atropine sulphate (AS) respiratory fluid. The respiratory route ensures rapid systemic absorption, bypassing first-pass metabolism, for convenient emergency administration. Its submicronic formulation (mean particle size < 1 µm) guarantees deep lung deposition, enhancing bioavailability and accelerating onset of action over conventional AS. Following *in vitro* and *ex vivo* characterization, a Phase I/II trial in 60 healthy volunteers assessed pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability. A subsequent Phase IIb study evaluated efficacy in reversing OP-induced muscarinic symptoms in an animal model, benchmarked against intramuscular AS. Results demonstrated significantly faster systemic absorption and therapeutic plasma concentrations, coupled with an excellent safety profile. Superior efficacy in rapidly reversing muscarinic signs was critically confirmed. This novel submicronic AS respiratory fluid offers a promising, rapid-acting, non-invasive antidote, addressing crucial gaps in emergency OP poisoning management.
