However, the limits of this natural resilience are not well understood in the presence of small adversarial changes to the DNN parameters' underlying memory representation, such as bit-flips that may be induced by hardware fault attacks.

title: Current laboratory performance of starlight suppression systems, and potential pathways to desired Habitable Worlds Observatory exoplanet science capabilities
text_ai: We summarize the current best polychromatic (10 to 20 % bandwidth) contrast performance demonstrated in the laboratory by different starlight suppression approaches and systems designed to directly characterize exoplanets around nearby stars. We present results obtained by internal coronagraph and external starshade experimental testbeds using entrance apertures equivalent to off-axis or on-axis telescopes, either monolithic or segmented. These demonstrations typically achieve raw contrasts of 10^-7 to 10^-8 within a few λ/D, with some advanced techniques reaching 10^-9 under specific conditions. Limitations persist in wavefront stability, diffractive leakage, and the scalability of control algorithms for broader bandwidths and larger dark holes. Comparing these to Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) requirements—targeting 10^-10 contrast at very small inner working angles (<2 λ/D) across broad spectral bands—reveals significant technological gaps. We identify critical pathways, including advancements in ultra-low wavefront error optics, high-actuator-count deformable mirrors, precision active wavefront control, and novel coronagraphic architectures. Integration of multiple suppression stages and robust, flight-like test environments are crucial, alongside larger, more stable testbeds and comprehensive error budgets. These laboratory efforts are vital for maturing technologies to enable direct imaging and spectroscopic characterization of Earth-like exoplanets, underpinning HWO's ambitious science goals.
prefix: We summarize the current best polychromatic (10 to 20 % bandwidth) contrast performance demonstrated in the laboratory by different starlight suppression approaches and systems designed to directly characterize exoplanets around nearby stars. We present results obtained by internal coronagraph and external starshade experimental testbeds using entrance apertures equivalent to off-axis or on-axis telescopes, either monolithic or segmented.

title: Optimizing Geometric Multigrid Methods with Evolutionary Computation
text_ai: For many linear and nonlinear systems that arise from the discretization of partial differential equations the construction of an efficient multigrid solver is a challenging task. Here we present a novel approach for the optimization of geometric multigrid methods that is based on evolutionary computation, a generic program optimization technique inspired by the principle of natural evolution. Specifically, our framework employs genetic programming to automatically optimize critical multigrid components like smoother choices, relaxation parameters, and grid transfer operators. The evolutionary process iteratively refines these configurations by evaluating their performance, quantified by convergence rate and computational cost, on a suite of test problems. This data-driven approach discovers highly efficient and robust solver parameters, often outperforming traditionally designed schemes. We demonstrate significant improvements in convergence speed and robustness across various elliptic partial differential equations. The findings highlight evolutionary computation as a powerful, automated paradigm for constructing high-performance multigrid solvers, especially for complex applications where optimal design is challenging.

title: Galactic Stellar and Substellar Initial Mass Function
text_ai: We review recent determinations of the present day and initial mass functions in various components of the Galaxy, disk, spheroid, young and globular clusters. As a general feature, the IMF is well described by a power-law form for $m\ga 1 \msol$ and a lognormal form below. This lognormal component typically peaks around 0.1-0.3 $\msol$, representing the characteristic mass for star formation. Below this, the IMF continues to decline into the substellar regime, extending to brown dwarfs and potentially to planetary-mass objects, though the precise form and existence of a minimum mass for star formation remain active areas of investigation. While a remarkable universality of the IMF shape is observed across a wide range of star-forming environments, including varying metallicities and densities, subtle environmental dependencies, particularly at the extreme ends of the mass spectrum, are still debated. We explore the evidence for and against such variations, considering their implications for star formation theories and the evolution of stellar populations. The accurate characterization of the substellar IMF is particularly critical for understanding the formation mechanisms of brown dwarfs and free-floating planets, and for constraining the total baryonic mass budget of the Galaxy. We highlight the observational challenges in extending IMF measurements to the lowest masses and in distinguishing between primordial distributions and subsequent dynamical evolution, particularly in dense environments. Our review synthesizes current understanding, identifies key uncertainties, and outlines promising avenues for future research in charting the full Galactic stellar and substellar mass spectrum.

title: Addressing UX Practitioners' Challenges in Designing ML Applications: an Interactive Machine Learning Approach
text_ai: UX practitioners face novel challenges when designing user interfaces for machine learning (ML)-enabled applications. Interactive ML paradigms, like AutoML and interactive machine teaching, lower the barrier for non-expert end users to create, understand, and use ML models, but their application to UX practice is largely unstudied. These challenges include managing model uncertainty, explaining ML behaviors to users, and integrating iterative model feedback into design cycles. This paper explores how interactive machine learning can be adapted to empower UX practitioners, enabling them to directly engage with ML models during the design process without requiring deep ML expertise. We propose an interactive ML framework specifically tailored for UX design, allowing practitioners to rapidly prototype, iterate, and test ML-driven user experiences. Through a design study with UX practitioners, we identify key design requirements and evaluate the usability and effectiveness of our proposed approach. Our findings highlight how interactive ML can bridge the gap between design and ML development, fostering more intuitive and robust ML applications.

title: Modelling Population-Level Hes1 Dynamics: Insights from a Multi-Framework Approach
text_ai: Mathematical models of living cells have been successively refined with advancements in experimental techniques. A main concern is striking a balance between modelling power and the tractability of the associated mathematical analysis. In this work we model the dynamics for the transcription factor Hairy and enhancer of split-1 (Hes1), whose expression oscillates during neural development, and which critically enables stable fate decision in the embryonic brain. We employ a multi-framework approach integrating deterministic ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and stochastic agent-based models (ABMs) to investigate population-level Hes1 dynamics, capturing average oscillatory patterns and cell-to-cell variability from molecular noise. Our analysis shows ODEs provide tractable core dynamics, while ABMs reveal how noise influences oscillation robustness and population-wide synchronization. By comparing these frameworks, we identify critical parameters governing oscillation stability and synchronization. These findings offer novel insights into Hes1 regulation, demonstrating how a multi-framework strategy effectively balances modelling power with analytical tractability in complex biological systems.

title: WhisperFuzz: White-Box Fuzzing for Detecting and Locating Timing Vulnerabilities in Processors
text_ai: Timing vulnerabilities in processors have emerged as a potent threat. As processors are the foundation of any computing system, identifying these flaws is imperative. Recently fuzzing techniques, traditionally used for detecting software vulnerabilities, have shown promising results for uncovering vulnerabilities in large-scale hardware designs, such as processors. However, existing hardware fuzzing methodologies often lack the fine-grained observability and targeted input generation required to effectively uncover and precisely locate subtle, timing-dependent vulnerabilities. We introduce WhisperFuzz, a novel white-box fuzzing framework meticulously engineered for the detection and accurate localization of timing vulnerabilities in processor designs. WhisperFuzz leverages detailed architectural state monitoring and cycle-accurate simulation to observe internal processor behavior and execution timings. It employs an intelligent, coverage-guided input generation strategy that systematically explores the timing landscape, focusing on architectural events and microarchitectural interactions known to influence execution latency. By instrumenting the target processor's RTL, WhisperFuzz precisely measures instruction completion times and identifies anomalous timing deviations that signify potential vulnerabilities. Furthermore, its white-box nature allows for direct pinpointing of the problematic logic gates or architectural stages responsible for the detected timing flaw. Our comprehensive evaluation on several complex open-source RISC-V processor implementations demonstrates WhisperFuzz's superior efficacy, uncovering multiple previously unknown timing side-channels and functional timing bugs with high precision, significantly enhancing the robustness of processor security validation.

title: RIDCP: Revitalizing Real Image Dehazing via High-Quality Codebook Priors
text_ai: Existing dehazing approaches struggle to process real-world hazy images owing to the lack of paired real data and robust priors. In this work, we present a new paradigm for real image dehazing from the perspectives of synthesizing more realistic hazy data and introducing more robust priors into the network. To tackle the data scarcity and domain gap, we first introduce a novel data synthesis pipeline that leverages a high-quality codebook of haze patterns to generate diverse and realistic synthetic hazy images, closely mimicking real-world haze distributions. This significantly augments the training data, enabling the network to learn more generalizable features. Furthermore, our proposed Revitalizing Real Image Dehazing via High-Quality Codebook Priors (RIDCP) framework introduces a meticulously constructed codebook prior, which effectively encodes intrinsic clean image characteristics and dehazing-relevant features. This prior is learned from a vast collection of high-quality images and integrated into our end-to-end dehazing network through a novel feature modulation mechanism. The codebook prior guides the network to selectively restore clear image details while effectively suppressing haze artifacts, leading to superior perceptual quality. Extensive experiments on various challenging real-world hazy image benchmarks demonstrate that RIDCP consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming existing methods in terms of both quantitative metrics and visual fidelity. Our approach offers a robust and generalizable solution, paving the way for more effective real-world dehazing applications.

title: The EXP pair-potential system. I. Fluid phase isotherms, isochores, and quasiuniversality
text_ai: The exponentially repulsive EXP pair potential defines a system of particles in terms of which simple liquids' quasiuniversality may be explained [A. K. Bacher et al., Nat. Commun. 5, 5424 (2014); J. C. Dyre, J. Phys. Condens. Matter 28, 323001 (2016)]. This paper and its companion present a detailed simulation study of the EXP system. This first paper focuses on the fluid phase, presenting extensive molecular dynamics simulations, mapping its isotherms and isochores across wide ranges of density and temperature. Thermodynamic properties, including pressure, energy, and virial, are characterized. Our findings confirm the EXP system's characteristic strongly correlating liquid features, particularly excellent isomorph invariance along its fluid-phase isotherms and isochores. This demonstrates its adherence to quasiuniversality, where its thermodynamic and dynamic properties map accurately onto other simple liquids via density- and temperature-dependent scaling. The EXP system thus serves as a canonical reference for understanding generic simple liquid properties; its solid phase and critical phenomena are detailed in the companion paper.

title: Intra-abdominal hypertension and the abdominal compartment syndrome
text_ai: The pressure within the abdominal cavity is normally little more than atmospheric pressure. However, even small increases in intra-abdominal pressure can have adverse effects on renal function, cardiac output, hepatic blood flow, respiratory mechanics, splanchnic perfusion and intracranial pressure. When intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) persistently rises above 12 mmHg, it is defined as intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH), a common and often under-recognized complication in critically ill patients. A more severe condition, abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS), occurs when IAP exceeds 20 mmHg and is associated with new or worsening organ dysfunction. These elevated pressures directly compress abdominal viscera and major vessels, impairing perfusion to the gastrointestinal tract, kidneys, and liver. Furthermore, increased IAP impedes diaphragmatic excursion, compromising ventilation, and elevates intrathoracic pressure, reducing cardiac preload and output while increasing systemic vascular resistance. Common etiologies include massive fluid resuscitation, abdominal trauma, sepsis, pancreatitis, ileus, and retroperitoneal hemorrhage. Its prevalence ranges widely, affecting a significant proportion of patients in intensive care units. Diagnosis relies primarily on indirect measurement of IAP, most commonly through the bladder via a Foley catheter, providing a reliable and minimally invasive method. Unrecognized and untreated IAH and ACS can rapidly lead to multiple organ failure, including acute kidney injury, respiratory failure, myocardial dysfunction, and cerebral ischemia, significantly increasing morbidity and mortality. Early recognition, continuous monitoring, and timely therapeutic interventions, ranging from medical management to surgical decompression, are crucial to mitigate these devastating effects and improve patient outcomes.

title: Testing Sparsity Assumptions in Bayesian Networks
text_ai: Bayesian network (BN) structure discovery algorithms typically either make assumptions about the sparsity of the true underlying network, or are limited by computational constraints to networks with a small number of variables. While these sparsity assumptions can take various forms, frequently the assumptions focus on an upper bound for the maximum in-degree of the underlying graph $\nabla_G$. The validity of such assumptions and their impact when violated are rarely tested. This paper evaluates BN structure learning algorithm robustness under varying true network sparsity, focusing on max in-degree. A synthetic data generation process controls density and in-degree, creating benchmarks challenging typical sparsity. Extensive simulations quantify violated assumptions' impact on learned network quality (structural Hamming distance). Findings reveal some algorithms show resilience; others degrade significantly as true max in-degree exceeds limits. This highlights the need to understand and relax these assumptions for more reliable BN structure discovery.

While these sparsity assumptions can take various forms, frequently the assumptions focus on an upper bound for the maximum in-degree of the underlying graph $\nabla_G$.

title: Fully On-board Low-Power Localization with Multizone Time-of-Flight Sensors on Nano-UAVs
text_ai: Nano-size unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) hold enormous potential to perform autonomous operations in complex environments, such as inspection, monitoring or data collection. Moreover, their small size allows safe operation close to humans and agile flight. An important part of autonomous flight is localization, which is a computationally intensive task especially on a nano-UAV that usually has strong constraints in sensing, processing and memory. This paper addresses this challenge by proposing a novel, fully on-board localization system for nano-UAVs utilizing multiple low-power, lightweight multizone Time-of-Flight (ToF) sensors. These sensors provide direct, multi-point distance measurements, offering rich spatial information with significantly reduced computational and power overhead compared to traditional vision or LiDAR. We integrate an array of ToF sensors and introduce a custom, optimized probabilistic filtering algorithm tailored for their data characteristics and the nano-UAV's stringent constraints. Our approach enables robust, accurate state estimation without external infrastructure or off-board computation. Experimental validation demonstrates centimeter-level localization accuracy across indoor environments, exhibiting high robustness against varying lighting and surface textures. Adhering to nano-UAV budgets, this low-power solution significantly advances autonomous navigation in complex, GPS-denied, or unknown spaces.

title: One for the Future: measuring the mass transfer rate in the ULX M82 X-2 by using orbital period changes will take millenia
text_ai: Bachetti et al. (2021) have recently claimed to measure the mass transfer rate in the pulsing ULX system M82 X-2 by following the change of its orbital period over 7 yr. However, our theoretical analysis of M82 X-2 indicates that the secular orbital period derivative (dP/dt) is exceedingly small. Calculations demonstrate that the intrinsic dP/dt, primarily driven by gravitational radiation and conservative mass transfer, would only yield a measurable change over timescales spanning centuries to millennia. Consequently, a 7-year baseline is highly susceptible to non-secular, short-term effects like apsidal motion or donor magnetic cycles, which can easily obscure the true long-term evolution. We present a detailed theoretical framework for M82 X-2's orbital evolution, concluding that a robust detection of the secular dP/dt, crucial for an accurate mass transfer rate, necessitates continuous monitoring over many centuries. The current claim is thus premature, underscoring the formidable challenge of quantifying ULX mass transfer rates via orbital period changes.

title: Kinks scattering in deformed $\varphi^6$ model
text_ai: The deformed model $\tilde{\varphi}^{(6)}$ is introduced based on the $\varphi^4$ model using a deformation functional $F[\varphi]$ including a free parameter $a$. The kink solutions in different sectors and their internal modes are obtained as functions of the deformation parameter and their characteristics are evaluated as well. Subsequently, the scattering of these kink solutions is investigated through numerical simulations of head-on collisions. The impact of the deformation parameter $a$ and the initial velocity of the kinks on the scattering outcomes is systematically analyzed. Our results reveal a rich variety of scattering phenomena, including elastic reflection, inelastic two-kink scattering, and multikink formation. Crucially, the deformation parameter is shown to significantly influence the critical velocities separating different scattering channels and to modulate the energy exchange between translational and internal modes. Resonance windows, where kinks exhibit temporary capture or excitation of internal oscillations, are identified and characterized in relation to the parameter $a$ and the kink's internal mode frequencies. These findings provide deeper insights into the dynamics of topological defects in deformed field theories, highlighting the tunability of their interactions through parameter-dependent modifications of the potential.

title: Windows over a New Low Energy Axion
text_ai: We outline some general features of possible extensions of the Standard Model that include anomalous U(1) gauge symmetries, a certain number of axions and their mixings with the CP-odd Higgs sector. As previously shown, after the mixing one of the axions becomes a physical pseudoscalar (the axi-Higgs) that can take the role of a modified QCD axion. This axi-Higgs exhibits unique couplings to Standard Model particles, distinct from those of a purely hadronic or leptonic QCD axion, due to its mixed Higgs-axion nature. Its mass and coupling strengths are directly linked to the breaking scale of the anomalous U(1) symmetry and the parameters governing the mixing in the CP-odd Higgs sector. We explore the parameter space where this modified QCD axion can simultaneously resolve the strong CP problem and constitute a significant fraction of the observed cosmological dark matter. The unique interaction profiles of the axi-Higgs, particularly its enhanced couplings to electroweak gauge bosons and fermions through Higgs portal interactions, open new 'windows' for experimental detection. We discuss the implications for ongoing and future axion search experiments, including those probing axion-photon conversion (e.g., ADMX, IAXO), axion-electron interactions, and axion-nucleon spin-dependent interactions (e.g., CASPEr). We also consider astrophysical constraints from stellar cooling and supernova observations. The presence of such a low-energy axi-Higgs provides a compelling and testable framework for extending the Standard Model, offering concrete targets for next-generation dark matter and fundamental physics experiments.

title: Topological Cycle Graph Attention Network for Brain Functional Connectivity
text_ai: This study, we introduce a novel Topological Cycle Graph Attention Network (CycGAT), designed to delineate a functional backbone within brain functional graph--key pathways essential for signal transmissio--from non-essential, redundant connections that form cycles around this core structure. We first introduce a cycle incidence matrix that establishes an independent cycle basis within a graph, mapping its relationship with edges. CycGAT then leverages this topological representation by integrating the cycle incidence matrix into its attention mechanism, enabling the network to learn and differentially weight edges based on their participation in these cyclical structures. This unique approach allows CycGAT to effectively discern and prioritize the non-redundant, core pathways critical for information flow, while attenuating the influence of peripheral, cyclical connections. We validate CycGAT on several resting-state fMRI datasets, demonstrating its superior capability to extract robust and interpretable functional backbones compared to existing graph neural network models. Our findings highlight CycGAT's potential for revealing critical organizational principles of brain networks and identifying subtle yet significant alterations in neurological and psychiatric conditions.

title: Optimized quantum implementation of elliptic curve arithmetic over binary fields
text_ai: Shor's quantum algorithm for discrete logarithms applied to elliptic curve groups forms the basis of a "quantum attack" of elliptic curve cryptosystems. To implement this algorithm on a quantum computer requires the efficient implementation of the elliptic curve group operation. Such an implementation requires we be able to compute inverses in the underlying field. This paper presents an optimized quantum circuit implementation for elliptic curve arithmetic over binary fields, specifically focusing on GF(2^m). We introduce novel quantum circuits for fundamental field operations, including addition, multiplication, and, critically, inversion utilizing a modified Itoh-Tsujii algorithm tailored for quantum computation. Our optimization strategy leverages the inherent characteristics of polynomial basis representation in binary fields and employs techniques such as parallelization and reversible logic synthesis to minimize quantum resources. We provide detailed quantum gate counts, including T-gates, and qubit requirements for these operations, culminating in a comprehensive resource estimation for a full elliptic curve point addition and doubling. For cryptographically relevant elliptic curves, such as the widely adopted NIST P-256 equivalent over GF(2^m), our optimized circuits demonstrate substantial reductions in both T-gate count and overall circuit depth compared to existing state-of-the-art implementations. These improvements are paramount for reducing the formidable resource requirements of a practical quantum attack on ECC, thereby bringing the timeline for breaking widely deployed elliptic curve cryptosystems closer to the capabilities of anticipated fault-tolerant quantum computers. This work thus advances the understanding of the specific quantum hardware demands for effectively mounting a quantum attack.

title: Electric generation and ratcheted transport of contact-charged drops.
text_ai: We describe a simple microfluidic system that enables the steady generation and efficient transport of aqueous drops using only a constant voltage input. Drop generation is achieved through an electrohydrodynamic dripping mechanism by which conductive drops grow and detach from a grounded nozzle in response to an electric field. Upon detachment, these drops become contact-charged due to their conductivity and the applied electric field. Their subsequent motion is precisely controlled by a spatially-modulated electric field. Transport is achieved through a novel ratcheting mechanism, wherein the charged drops are sequentially attracted to and repelled from an array of electrodes energized by the same constant voltage. This generates a directional, step-wise movement. The asymmetric potential landscape efficiently guides the drops, overcoming surface tension and viscous drag. This purely electrical approach enables robust, precise, and energy-efficient manipulation of discrete fluid volumes without pumps, valves, or moving parts. The system holds promise for applications in lab-on-a-chip devices, chemical synthesis, and high-throughput screening where precise droplet handling is critical.

title: Vegetarianism and veganism compared with mental health and cognitive outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text_ai: Vegetarian and vegan diets are increasing in popularity. Although they provide beneficial health effects, they may also lead to nutritional deficiencies. Cognitive impairment and mental health disorders have a high economic burden. A meta-analysis was conducted to examine the relationship between vegan or vegetarian diets and cognitive and mental health. A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for studies published up to September 2023. We included observational and interventional studies comparing adult vegetarians or vegans with omnivores, reporting mental health (depression, anxiety, mood) or cognitive function (memory, attention, executive function) outcomes. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed independently, and a random-effects meta-analysis model was used to synthesize findings. Thirty-five studies (n=XX,XXX participants) met the inclusion criteria. Meta-analysis revealed no significant overall differences in depression or anxiety symptoms or cognitive function between vegetarian/vegan groups and omnivores. However, some individual studies reported slightly higher prevalence rates of depression or anxiety in specific subgroups, and minor variations in certain cognitive domains. The role of nutrient deficiencies (e.g., vitamin B12, iron, omega-3 fatty acids) as potential mediators remained inconclusive due to heterogeneity and limited direct evidence. These findings suggest that while vegetarian and vegan diets are not consistently associated with adverse mental health or cognitive outcomes, vigilance regarding nutrient intake and further longitudinal research are warranted. Future studies should employ robust methodologies to elucidate the long-term impacts and potential mediating factors.

title: Extracting black-hole rotational energy: The generalized Penrose process
text_ai: In the case involving particles the necessary and sufficient condition for the Penrose process to extract energy from a rotating black hole is absorption of particles with negative energies and angular momenta. No torque at the black-hole horizon occurs. This work extends the Penrose process to encompass classical fields and wave phenomena, thereby introducing the concept of the generalized Penrose process. In this broader context, energy extraction occurs through superradiant scattering, where incident waves are amplified upon interacting with the rotating black hole within its ergoregion. Similar to the particle case, this amplification is fundamentally linked to the existence of negative energy modes accessible within the black hole's gravitational field, specifically for waves with frequencies satisfying the superradiant condition. The absence of torque at the horizon remains a crucial feature, ensuring that the process adheres to the principles of energy and angular momentum conservation while maximizing the efficiency of rotational energy extraction. This generalized framework provides a robust theoretical foundation for understanding how black holes might power relativistic jets and other high-energy astrophysical phenomena, offering new avenues for exploring the interplay between gravity and matter/energy fields in extreme cosmic environments. We derive the general conditions for this superradiant energy extraction and discuss its implications for various types of incident fields, from electromagnetic to gravitational waves, detailing the efficiency limits and the role of the black hole's spin in optimizing the process.

title: The Density-Potential Mapping in Quantum Dynamics
text_ai: This work studies in detail the possibility of defining a one-to-one mapping from charge densities as obtained by the time-dependent Schr\"odinger equation to external potentials. Such a mapping is provided by the Runge-Gross theorem and lies at the very core of time-dependent density functional theory. Despite its foundational status, the precise conditions for the existence and uniqueness of this mapping, especially regarding density differentiability and initial state dependence, necessitate further scrutiny. This work rigorously investigates the mathematical properties of the density-potential correspondence, extending the analysis beyond the standard Runge-Gross framework. We establish novel criteria for the local and global invertibility of the mapping, considering varying initial states and external field characteristics. Our findings provide a deeper understanding of the domain of uniquely potential-representable densities, clarifying fundamental limitations and possibilities within TDDFT. These insights are crucial for developing more robust approximations for exchange-correlation functionals and for accurately simulating quantum phenomena involving strong fields and non-adiabatic dynamics, thereby advancing the theoretical underpinnings of time-dependent electronic structure theory.

Such a mapping is provided by the Runge-Gross theorem and lies at the very core of time-dependent density functional theory.

title: Seismic hazard assessment in Menton, France: Topographical site effect zoning considering a semi-empirical approach and a Machine Learning scheme
text_ai: The presence of topography influences the seismic ground motion and may result in strong amplifications, generally at the top of hills and reliefs. The increasing urbanization of hills requires an accurate estimation of these effects even in areas of moderate seismicity. This study addresses this critical need by focusing on Menton, a densely populated coastal town in the French Riviera with complex topography and moderate seismicity. We present a novel methodology for high-resolution topographical site effect zoning, integrating a semi-empirical approach with a Machine Learning (ML) scheme. The semi-empirical component utilizes observed amplification factors from earthquake data to establish initial topographical effects. Concurrently, a supervised ML model (Random Forest regressor) is trained on topographic proxies (e.g., slope, curvature) and numerically simulated ground motion amplifications. This hybrid approach robustly generalizes amplification patterns across Menton’s intricate terrain, overcoming individual method limitations. The resulting detailed zoning maps quantify spatial variations in ground motion amplification, providing crucial input for local seismic hazard assessment, urban planning, and resilient infrastructure design in Menton.

title: Curvature Perturbations from a Massive Vector Curvaton
text_ai: We study a ghost-free model of massive vector curvaton proposed in the literature, where the quick decrease of the vector background expectation value is avoided by a suitable choice of kinetic and mass functions. We then investigate the generation of primordial curvature perturbations from this vector curvaton. Focusing on the post-inflationary epoch, we derive the conditions for successful curvaton decay and its contribution to the total curvature perturbation. Our analysis reveals that the anisotropic nature of the vector field naturally imprints a statistically anisotropic component in the primordial power spectrum, which we quantify. Furthermore, we compute the non-Gaussianity of the curvature perturbations, demonstrating that both local and equilateral types can be significantly enhanced, exhibiting distinct anisotropic features. We explore the model's parameter space, identifying regions consistent with current Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) constraints on statistical anisotropy and primordial non-Gaussianity. This model provides a compelling mechanism for generating anisotropic primordial fluctuations, potentially offering new avenues for confronting theoretical predictions with future observational data.

title: Preschool Gender-Typed Play Behavior at Age 3.5 Years Predicts Physical Aggression at Age 13 Years.
text_ai: Gender differences in play behavior and physical aggression have been consistently reported. Theoretical perspectives concerning evolutionary, social, and social-cognitive mechanisms suggest that male-typical play behavior during childhood increases subsequent physical aggression. The evidence supporting these connections is limited, however. To address this gap, the current longitudinal study examined the predictive relationship between gender-typed play at age 3.5 years and physical aggression at age 13 years. Participants were drawn from the Québec Longitudinal Study of Child Development (QLSCD), a representative birth cohort of 2,223 children. Gender-typed play was assessed at age 3.5 years using maternal reports of toy preferences and activity participation. Physical aggression was measured at age 13 years using multi-informant reports from teachers, peers, and self-reports. Hierarchical regression analyses revealed that male-typical play at age 3.5 years was a significant positive predictor of physical aggression at age 13, even after controlling for early physical aggression, socioeconomic status, and child temperament. This association remained significant for both boys and girls, albeit with a stronger effect observed in boys. These findings underscore the long-term developmental significance of early gender-typed play in the etiology of aggression. They suggest that early socialization and individual predispositions related to gender-typed play may contribute to persistent aggressive behavioral patterns. Interventions targeting gender-role rigidity in play during early childhood may therefore represent a promising avenue for reducing later aggression.

Theoretical perspectives concerning evolutionary, social, and social-cognitive mechanisms suggest that male-typical play behavior during childhood increases subsequent physical aggression. The evidence supporting these connections is limited, however.

title: A Generic Framework for Clustering Vehicle Motion Trajectories
text_ai: The development of autonomous vehicles requires having access to a large amount of data in the concerning driving scenarios. However, manual annotation of such driving scenarios is costly and subject to the errors in the rule-based trajectory labeling systems. This paper proposes an unsupervised, generic framework for clustering vehicle motion trajectories. It addresses the limitations of manual labeling by automatically identifying distinct driving behaviors and scenarios from raw trajectory data. The framework employs a novel trajectory similarity metric that accounts for spatial and temporal variations, making it robust to diverse driving styles and environmental conditions. We integrate this metric with a density-based clustering algorithm, enabling the discovery of complex, non-linear patterns without requiring a predefined number of clusters. This approach significantly reduces the need for human intervention, facilitating the efficient analysis and categorization of vast datasets. The framework's genericity allows its application across various sensor modalities and geographic regions, providing a scalable solution for understanding common and anomalous vehicle behaviors critical for autonomous system development and validation.
prefix: The development of autonomous vehicles requires having access to a large amount of data in the concerning driving scenarios. However, manual annotation of such driving scenarios is costly and subject to the errors in the rule-based trajectory labeling systems.

title: Two-year follow-up of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists for chronic central serous chorioretinopathy.
text_ai: To evaluate the long-term oral mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRa) treatment in chronic central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC). Patients with chronic non-resolving CSC (defined as foveal subretinal fluid (SRF) lasting >4 months with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) alterations) treated with MRa only (eplerenone or spironolactone) for at least 6 months were retrospectively included. Clinical data including best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central macular thickness (CMT), and subretinal fluid (SRF) status on optical coherence tomography (OCT) were collected at baseline and at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Complete SRF resolution was the primary outcome, with changes in BCVA and CMT as secondary outcomes. Forty-five eyes from 40 patients (mean age 54.2 ± 9.8 years, 75% male) were included, with a mean follow-up of 26.5 ± 2.1 months. At 24 months, complete SRF resolution was achieved in 32 (71.1%) eyes. Mean BCVA significantly improved from 0.38 ± 0.15 LogMAR at baseline to 0.22 ± 0.12 LogMAR (p < 0.001), and CMT decreased from 395 ± 85 µm to 268 ± 45 µm (p < 0.001). No serious adverse events were reported. This long-term follow-up demonstrates that oral MRa treatment effectively promotes sustained SRF resolution and visual improvement in a significant proportion of chronic CSC patients, with a favorable safety profile over two years. MRa therapy appears to be a viable long-term treatment option for chronic CSC.

title: The formation of astrophysical Mg-rich silicate dust
text_ai: We present new results for ground-state candidate energies of Mg-rich olivine (MRO) clusters and use the binding energies of these clusters to determine their nucleation rates in stellar outflows, with particular interest in the en- vironments of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe). Using *ab initio* Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, we systematically explored the potential energy surfaces of MgₓSiᵧO₂ clusters, identifying stable structural motifs and quantifying their formation enthalpies. These accurate binding energies are crucial for calculating activation barriers and free energies associated with initial dust condensation stages. Our kinetic modeling, incorporating these data, reveals significantly higher nucleation rates for MRO in oxygen-rich CCSN ejecta compared to previous estimates relying on less precise thermodynamic parameters. We find that rapid cooling and expansion in these environments create optimal conditions for efficient MRO seed formation. The enhanced nucleation efficiency suggests that CCSNe can be substantial contributors to the interstellar budget of Mg-rich silicates, potentially reconciling observed dust masses in young supernova remnants with theoretical predictions. This work refines our understanding of refractory dust formation and its impact on galactic chemical evolution.

title: Forced-induced desorption of a polymer chain adsorbed on an attractive surface - Theory and Computer Experiment
text_ai: We consider the properties of a self-avoiding polymer chain, adsorbed on a solid attractive substrate which is attached with one end to a pulling force. The conformational properties of such chain and its phase behavior are treated within a Grand Canonical Ensemble (GCE) approach. This theoretical framework allows us to precisely determine the critical pulling force ($f_c$) necessary to induce the desorption of the polymer from the surface. Complementing this analytical treatment, extensive Monte Carlo simulations are performed on a coarse-grained lattice model, capturing the essential interactions and entropic effects. Our investigations reveal that the polymer undergoes a distinct desorption transition as the applied force increases. Below $f_c$, the chain remains predominantly adsorbed, albeit with increasing stretching and deformation of its adsorbed segments. As the force approaches $f_c$, a sharp transition occurs, leading to the detachment of the polymer from the substrate. We characterize the nature of this force-induced desorption transition, identifying whether it is continuous or first-order, and how it is influenced by parameters such as chain length, surface attraction strength, and temperature. Specifically, we elucidate the scaling behavior of the critical force with respect to the adsorption energy and chain length. The simulations validate the theoretical predictions, providing detailed insights into the evolution of the polymer's conformation, including the formation of 'tails' and 'loops', during the progressive desorption process. The study highlights the intricate balance between surface attraction, chain elasticity, and the external mechanical force in dictating the polymer's mechanical response and its detachment dynamics.

title: Fractal Profit Landscape of the Stock Market
text_ai: We investigate the structure of the profit landscape obtained from the most basic, fluctuation based, trading strategy applied for the daily stock price data. The strategy is parameterized by only two variables, p and q. Stocks are sold and bought if the log return is bigger than p and less than -q, respectively. By systematically mapping the accumulated profit across a wide range of (p, q) values for a diverse dataset of stocks, we construct a two-dimensional profit landscape. Our extensive computational analysis reveals that this landscape is profoundly intricate, exhibiting clear fractal characteristics. Specifically, we demonstrate the presence of self-similarity and scale invariance across various profit magnitudes. Optimal profit regions are not isolated, smooth peaks but rather form complex, interconnected fractal sets, suggesting a multifractal structure inherent to market profitability. These findings underscore the non-linear and self-organizing nature of financial markets, even under simplified trading assumptions. The fractal profit landscape provides novel insights into market efficiency and the inherent complexity underlying price fluctuations, offering a new perspective for understanding the limits and potential of rule-based trading strategies.

title: TractoSCR: A Novel Supervised Contrastive Regression Framework for Prediction of Neurocognitive Measures Using Multi-Site Harmonized Diffusion MRI Tractography
text_ai: Neuroimaging-based prediction of neurocognitive measures is valuable for studying how the brain's structure relates to cognitive function. However, the accuracy of prediction using popular linear regression models is relatively low. We propose a novel deep regression method, namely TractoSCR, that allows full supervision for contrastive learning in regression tasks using diffusion MRI tractography. TractoSCR achieves this by leveraging the continuous nature of regression targets to define relative similarities and dissimilarities between samples, guiding the contrastive loss. This enables learning highly discriminative, robust latent representations of structural connectivity from tractography features, surpassing linear model limitations. We evaluated TractoSCR on large-scale, multi-site harmonized diffusion MRI datasets, predicting various neurocognitive measures across diverse cohorts. Benchmarked against linear and conventional deep learning regression, TractoSCR consistently achieved significantly higher prediction accuracy (improved R-squared, reduced MAE) and enhanced generalization on unseen data from different sites. The learned representations exhibited greater biological plausibility and interpretability, reflecting nuanced brain-behavior relationships. TractoSCR represents a substantial advancement in neuroimaging-based prediction, offering a powerful tool for understanding brain-behavior links and biomarker development.

title: A Trust and Reputation System for IoT Exploiting Distributed Ledger Technology
text_ai: The advent of Bitcoin, and consequently Blockchain, has ushered in a new era of decentralization. Blockchain enables mutually distrusting entities to work collaboratively to attain a common objective. However, current Blockchain technologies lack scalability, which limits their use in Internet of Things (IoT) applications. To overcome this critical limitation, this paper proposes a novel trust and reputation system specifically designed for IoT environments, leveraging the principles of Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT). Our system enables secure and reliable interactions between diverse IoT devices by establishing dynamic trust scores based on historical performance and verifiable interactions recorded on a decentralized ledger. Unlike conventional blockchains, this approach utilizes a lightweight DLT architecture optimized for resource-constrained IoT nodes, ensuring efficient data management and consensus. This framework mitigates malicious behavior, enhances data integrity, and facilitates autonomous decision-making within IoT ecosystems. Evaluation demonstrates that the proposed system effectively identifies untrustworthy entities while maintaining high throughput and low latency, crucial for real-time IoT applications.

title: On Triangulation as a Form of Self-Supervision for 3D Human Pose Estimation
text_ai: Supervised approaches to 3D pose estimation from single images are remarkably effective when labeled data is abundant. However, as the acquisition of ground-truth 3D labels is labor intensive and time consuming, recent attention has shifted towards semi- and weakly-supervised learning. Generating an effective form of supervision with little annotations still poses major challenge in crowded scenes. To address this, we propose a novel self-supervised learning paradigm that exploits multi-view triangulation as a proxy for 3D ground truth. By predicting 2D keypoints from uncalibrated image pairs, our method triangulates 3D joint locations, generating a dense and geometrically consistent supervisory signal for a single-view 3D pose estimator. This intrinsic multi-view constraint inherently resolves scale ambiguities and improves robustness, even in crowded scenarios where individual 2D predictions might be noisy. Our framework enables training powerful 3D pose estimators without explicit 3D labels, relying solely on readily available 2D annotations and multi-view imagery. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that this triangulation-based self-supervision yields competitive performance with fully supervised methods and significantly outperforms existing weakly-supervised techniques, showcasing its potential for scalable and accurate 3D human pose estimation.

However, as the acquisition of ground-truth 3D labels is labor intensive and time consuming, recent attention has shifted towards semi- and weakly-supervised learning. Generating an effective form of supervision with little annotations still poses major challenge in crowded scenes.

title: Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Hypersonic Flows
text_ai: In recent years, high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods have emerged as an attractive approach for numerical simulations of compressible flows. This paper presents an overview of the recent development of DG methods for compressible flows with particular focus on hypersononic flows. First, we survey state-of-the-art DG methods for computational fluid dynamics. Subsequently, we delve into the specific adaptations and challenges of applying DG methods to hypersonic flow regimes, characterized by extreme conditions such as strong shock waves, high temperatures, and complex thermochemical phenomena. These necessitate robust numerical schemes capable of accurately capturing discontinuities, resolving boundary layers, and handling non-equilibrium effects. We discuss various DG techniques, including advanced shock-capturing strategies (e.g., WENO reconstructions, artificial viscosity) and high-order treatment of source terms from real-gas models and chemical reactions. Emphasis is placed on developing stable, efficient DG schemes for thermal and chemical non-equilibrium flows, crucial for accurate aerothermodynamic load prediction on hypersonic vehicles. Recent advancements in limiters and stabilization techniques are highlighted, preserving DG's high-order accuracy while maintaining robustness in strong gradients and high Mach numbers. Finally, we discuss their computational efficiency and parallel scalability, demonstrating their potential for industrial applications and fundamental research in hypersonics.

This paper presents an overview of the recent development of DG methods for compressible flows with particular focus on hypersononic flows. title: Impact of QCD jets and heavy-quark production in cosmic-ray proton atmospheric showers up to 10$^{20}$ eV
text_ai: The PYTHIA 6 Monte Carlo (MC) event generator, commonly used in collider physics, is interfaced for the first time with a fast transport simulation of a hydrogen atmosphere, with the same density as air, in order to study the properties of extended atmospheric showers (EAS) produced by cosmic ray protons with energies E$_{CR}\approx 10^{14}$--$10^{20}$ eV. This novel approach allows for a detailed investigation of the impact of perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics (pQCD) processes, specifically the production and fragmentation of hard QCD jets and heavy quarks (charm and beauty), on the longitudinal and lateral development of these showers. At the highest energies, where center-of-mass energies in hadronic interactions reach well beyond those probed at current colliders, the PYTHIA framework provides a robust model for these hard scattering events. The study systematically compares shower observables, such as the depth of shower maximum (Xmax), muon content, and lateral distribution of secondary particles. Significant deviations are observed compared to predictions from traditional cosmic-ray interaction models. The enhanced production and subsequent semileptonic decays of heavy quarks, especially at ultra-high energies, lead to a noticeable increase in the number of high-energy muons reaching ground level. Furthermore, the presence of hard QCD jets influences the energy partition among secondary particles, potentially altering the shower's longitudinal profile and the spread of particles at observation level. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating detailed pQCD dynamics, validated by collider experiments, for an accurate interpretation of ultra-high energy cosmic ray data and for reducing hadronic interaction model uncertainties in air shower simulations.

title: Local Decorrelation For Improved Detection
text_ai: Even with the advent of more sophisticated, data-hungry methods, boosted decision trees remain extraordinarily successful for fast rigid object detection, achieving top accuracy on numerous datasets. While effective, most boosted detectors use decision trees with orthogonal (single feature) splits, and the topology of the resulting decision boundary may not be well matched to the natural topology of the data. This inherent limitation forces the classifier to approximate complex, non-axis-aligned boundaries using inefficient staircase-like structures, often requiring deeper trees and more boosting rounds, which increases model complexity and can hinder generalization. To address this, we propose a novel strategy: *local decorrelation*. At each internal node, our method learns a simple linear transformation that locally decorrelates the incoming feature subset. This transformation enables subsequent orthogonal splits to align more effectively with the principal components of the local data distribution, creating more compact and expressive decision boundaries. Integrating this into the boosting framework significantly enhances individual tree split efficiency and overall detector discriminative power. We demonstrate that our approach, applied to a state-of-the-art boosted detector, achieves superior performance on challenging rigid object detection benchmarks, yielding higher accuracy and faster inference compared to conventional orthogonal split methods.

While effective, most boosted detectors use decision trees with orthogonal (single feature) splits, and the topology of the resulting decision boundary may not be well matched to the natural topology of the data.

title: Successful intra-class switching among IL-17 antagonists: a multicentre, multinational, retrospective study.
text_ai: IL-17 blockers are among the newer anti-psoriatic treatment options and little is known about the interclass switching. We have thus initiated a multi-center, multi-national, retrospective study to assess the treatment response of patients who were switched from one IL-17 blocker to another. We included adult patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who had received at least one IL-17 inhibitor (secukinumab or ixekizumab) and subsequently switched to an alternative IL-17 inhibitor (ixekizumab, secukinumab, or brodalumab) due to primary or secondary failure. Clinical data, including Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) scores, Physician's Global Assessment (PGA), and adverse events, were collected at baseline and at weeks 12, 24, and 52 post-switch. Primary endpoints were PASI 75/90/100 response rates. A total of 423 patients from 18 centers across 7 countries were included. Mean age was 48.2 ± 12.1 years, and mean disease duration was 15.6 ± 7.3 years. At week 12, 68.1% of patients achieved PASI 75, and 42.5% achieved PASI 90. These response rates were sustained through week 24 (PASI 75: 70.3%, PASI 90: 45.8%) and week 52 (PASI 75: 65.5%, PASI 90: 40.1%). Drug survival at 52 weeks was 72.9%. The safety profile was consistent with known IL-17 inhibitor safety data, with no new signals identified. Our findings suggest that intra-class switching among IL-17 antagonists is an effective and generally well-tolerated strategy for patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis who experience inadequate response or loss of efficacy to an initial IL-17 blocker, providing a valuable treatment option.

title: The Quest for Omnioculars: Embedded Visualization for Augmenting Basketball Game Viewing Experiences
text_ai: Sports game data is becoming increasingly complex, often consisting of multivariate data such as player performance stats, historical team records, and athletes' positional tracking information. While numerous visual analytics systems have been developed for sports analysts to derive insights, few tools target fans to improve their understanding and engagement of sports data during live games. To address this critical gap, we propose an embedded visualization framework, inspired by the concept of 'Omnioculars,' designed to augment basketball game viewing experiences for fans. Our system integrates real-time statistical overlays and dynamic graphical annotations directly into the live video stream, providing contextual insights without disrupting the immersive viewing experience. By leveraging player tracking data, historical performance metrics, and tactical play patterns, our visualizations dynamically highlight key events, player contributions, and strategic shifts as they unfold on the court. This approach allows fans to instantly grasp complex game narratives and appreciate subtle strategic nuances that often go unnoticed. We developed a prototype system for basketball, enabling on-demand exploration of individual player stats, team-wide analytics, and comparative performance data, all seamlessly integrated into the visual field. Through a user study involving casual and avid basketball fans, we evaluated the system's impact on viewer comprehension, engagement, and overall enjoyment. Results demonstrate a significant improvement in users' ability to interpret game dynamics and deepen their appreciation for the sport. This work contributes a novel paradigm for fan-centric sports data visualization, paving the way for future personalized and data-enriched live sports broadcasts.

title: Green Segment Routing for Improved Sustainability of Backbone Networks
text_ai: Improving the energy efficiency of Internet Service Provider (ISP) backbone networks is an important objective for ISP operators. In these networks, the overall traffic load throughout the day can vary drastically, resulting in many backbone networks being highly overprovisioned during periods of lower traffic volume. This overprovisioning leads to significant energy waste, as network devices consume substantial power regardless of utilization. Segment Routing (SR) offers a promising avenue for improving energy efficiency by enabling highly flexible and granular traffic engineering. This paper proposes a novel Green Segment Routing (GSR) approach that dynamically consolidates traffic onto a minimal set of active network elements during off-peak hours. By strategically deactivating underutilized links and line cards, our method significantly reduces overall power consumption without compromising network performance or reliability. We develop an optimization framework that leverages SR's explicit path control to identify energy-optimal forwarding paths and evaluate its effectiveness through extensive simulations using realistic backbone network topologies and traffic patterns. Results demonstrate that GSR can achieve substantial energy savings, contributing to a more sustainable operation of ISP backbone networks.

title: YouTube as a source of patient information for stroke: A content-quality and an audience engagement analysis.
text_ai: Stroke is the second leading cause of death worldwide following ischemic heart disease, and the fifth in the United States. The video-sharing database, YouTube, is the second most popular visited website with more than 2 billion users, thus it's increasingly being used as a medium for delivering health information. However, unregulated online health information raises accuracy and reliability concerns. For stroke, access to accurate, evidence-based content is paramount for patient education and self-management. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the content quality and audience engagement of YouTube videos concerning stroke. A comprehensive keyword search identified relevant videos. Content quality was assessed by two independent reviewers using validated instruments (DISCERN, JAMA criteria). Audience engagement metrics (views, likes, comments) were analyzed; videos were also categorized by source. Analysis revealed variability in information quality. Many videos exhibited moderate-to-low quality, often lacking comprehensive, evidence-based content and containing misleading claims. Reputable sources scored higher, yet many highly engaged videos originated from non-professional creators. High audience engagement underscores YouTube's significant role in stroke information dissemination. Findings highlight the urgent need for healthcare providers to produce and promote high-quality, evidence-based stroke education, counteracting misinformation and empowering patients.

title: On the disappearance of a cold molecular torus around the low-luminosity active galactic nucleus of NGC 1097
text_ai: We used the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) to map the CO(3-2) and the underlying continuum emissions around the type 1 low-luminosity active galactic nucleus (LLAGN; bolometric luminosity $\lesssim 10^{42}$ erg~s$^{-1}$) of NGC 1097 at $\sim 10$ pc resolution. These observations revealed a detailed cold gas distribution within a $\sim 100$ pc of this LLAGN. Contrary to expectations for a typical type 1 AGN, we found no evidence for a compact, geometrically thick molecular torus or disk on scales down to our resolution limit of $\sim 10$ pc. Instead, the CO(3-2) emission exhibits a diffuse, centrally depleted morphology, with most molecular gas concentrated in larger-scale spiral arms extending outwards. We derive an upper limit for the circumnuclear molecular gas mass within the inner 10 pc of $\lesssim 10^5$ M$_\odot$, significantly lower than masses typically inferred for obscuring tori in more luminous AGNs. This absence of a substantial cold molecular reservoir in the immediate vicinity of the black hole suggests a fundamentally different feeding mechanism for NGC 1097's LLAGN, possibly relying on direct accretion of hot gas or episodic infall from larger scales. Our findings challenge standard unified models that posit a universal cold molecular torus as the primary obscuring structure, particularly for LLAGNs, and highlight the diverse nature of circumnuclear environments. The observed gas distribution supports a scenario where the central engine is currently starved of cold molecular fuel, potentially explaining its low bolometric luminosity.

title: Semi-Interpenetrating Cooperative Localization in Connected Vehicle Networks
text_ai: We proposed a fusion mechanism for the distributed cooperative map matching (CMM) within the vehicular ad-hoc network. This mechanism makes the information from each node reachable within the network by other nodes without direct communication, thus improving the overall localization accuracy and robustness. This novel semi-interpenetrating approach leverages localized data structures and indirect information propagation, enabling nodes to infer the states and observations of their neighbors without explicit message exchange. This significantly mitigates communication overhead, a critical challenge in dynamic and dense vehicular environments. By integrating a probabilistic framework with a novel data-driven aggregation scheme, our mechanism effectively fuses heterogeneous sensor inputs and individual CMM estimations for a comprehensive and coherent environmental understanding across the network. Crucially, this architecture enhances resilience against partial communication failures and GPS signal degradation by providing redundant and implicitly validated localization cues. Extensive simulations using real-world traffic data demonstrate that our semi-interpenetrating cooperative localization (SCL) method consistently outperforms traditional distributed CMM techniques, achieving up to a 25% improvement in average positioning error and significantly faster convergence rates in various network densities and communication scenarios.

title: Multiple single-photon generations in three-level atoms coupled to cavity with non-Markovian effects
text_ai: In this paper, we show how to generate the multiple single-photon wavepackets of arbitrary temporal shape from an optical cavity coupled with $N$ three-level atoms driven by a driving field in the non-Markovian regime. Our theoretical model elucidates that the unique memory effects inherent to the non-Markovian environment, particularly when the cavity interacts with a spectrally structured photonic reservoir, play a crucial role in enabling this generation. By precisely engineering the spectral density of the reservoir and coherently controlling the $N$ three-level atoms via a tailored driving field, we demonstrate a robust mechanism for the sequential emission of multiple indistinguishable single photons. We establish specific protocols to independently sculpt the temporal profile of each emitted photon, allowing for arbitrary waveform generation. This unprecedented control is achieved by leveraging the cavity's memory and the atoms' coherence, which collectively suppress unwanted dissipative pathways and enhance the temporal fidelity of the generated wavepackets. Our scheme exhibits high efficiency and robustness against common experimental imperfections, making it a viable candidate for practical implementation. The ability to generate on-demand multiple single-photon wavepackets with customizable temporal envelopes offers significant advantages for scalable quantum computing architectures, secure quantum communication networks, and advanced quantum metrology applications that demand tailored light-matter interactions. This work thus provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for designing and implementing high-performance multi-photon sources in diverse quantum platforms.

title: Space of initial conditions and universality in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics
text_ai: We study analytically the role of initial conditions in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics considering the one-dimensional ferromagnets in the regime of spontaneously broken symmetry. We analyze the expectation value of local operators for the infinite-dimensional space of initial conditions of domain wall type, generally intended as initial conditions spatially interpolating between two different ground states. Our analysis reveals that, despite the infinite variety of such initial conditions, the long-time expectation values of local operators exhibit profound universality. We demonstrate that distinct domain wall profiles lead to identical asymptotic states, characterized by universal spatial profiles determined solely by the ground states defining their boundaries. This emergent behavior stems from the ballistic propagation of quasiparticles and the system's underlying integrability, effectively erasing the fine details of the initial state. We establish a classification scheme for the nonequilibrium dynamics, linking global initial state information to local universal late-time properties, illuminating how universality emerges in far-from-equilibrium quantum many-body systems.

title: When Prompt Engineering Meets Software Engineering: CNL-P as Natural and Robust "APIs'' for Human-AI Interaction
text_ai: With the growing capabilities of large language models (LLMs), they are increasingly applied in areas like intelligent customer service, code generation, and knowledge management. Natural language (NL) prompts act as the ``APIs'' for human-LLM interaction. To improve prompt quality, best practices for prompt engineering (PE) have been developed, including writing guidelines and templates. However, current PE practices often lack the rigor and robustness required for integrating LLMs into complex software systems. Prompts can be ambiguous, difficult to maintain, and prone to unexpected behavior, especially when dealing with diverse user inputs or evolving model capabilities. This presents significant challenges for developers seeking to build reliable and scalable LLM-powered applications. To address these limitations, we introduce Controlled Natural Language for Prompts (CNL-P), a novel paradigm that merges the intuitiveness of natural language with the precision and predictability of formal specifications. CNL-P defines a structured subset of natural language, enforcing semantic clarity and reducing ambiguity, thereby creating "APIs" that are both human-readable and machine-interpretable. This approach enables the development of robust, testable, and reusable prompts, akin to well-defined software APIs. CNL-P facilitates better version control, automated validation, and seamless integration into traditional software development lifecycles. Our framework not only enhances the reliability and maintainability of LLM interactions but also lowers the barrier for non-expert users to craft effective prompts, transforming prompt engineering into a more systematic and sustainable discipline.

title: Graphene field effect transistors as room-temperature Terahertz detectors
text_ai: The unique optoelectronic properties of graphene [1] make it an ideal platform for a variety of photonic applications [2], including fast photodetectors [3], transparent electrodes [4], optical modulators [5], and ultra-fast lasers [6]. Crucially, its exceptional carrier mobility, broadband absorption, and tunable Fermi level also position graphene as a leading candidate for addressing the challenges within the Terahertz (THz) spectral gap [7,8]. Traditional THz detection typically requires complex and costly cryogenic cooling, hindering widespread applications [9]. Graphene field effect transistors (GFETs), by harnessing their inherent plasmonic resonances and strong light-matter interaction, offer a promising avenue for efficient, compact, and room-temperature THz detection [10,11]. This paper details an experimental and theoretical investigation into the performance of GFETs as uncooled THz detectors. We demonstrate their capability for sensitive detection across a broad THz frequency range, exhibiting high responsivity and low noise equivalent power (NEP) at room temperature. Our findings highlight the significant potential of GFETs to advance THz imaging, spectroscopy, and communication technologies by enabling high-performance, cost-effective, and portable systems.

title: Can Large Language Models Match Tutoring System Adaptivity? A Benchmarking Study
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) hold promise as dynamic instructional aids. Yet, it remains unclear whether LLMs can replicate the adaptivity of intelligent tutoring systems (ITS)--where student knowledge and pedagogical strategies are explicitly modeled. We propose a prompt variation framework to assess LLM-generated instructional moves' adaptivity and pedagogical soundness across 75 real-world tutoring scenarios from an ITS. Our framework systematically varies prompt inputs to simulate distinct student knowledge states (e.g., misconceptions, partial understanding) and desired pedagogical interventions (e.g., scaffolding, hint generation). Human experts, blinded to the source, evaluated the generated instructional moves from leading LLMs (e.g., GPT-4, Claude 3 Opus) on a rubric encompassing pedagogical appropriateness, alignment with student state, and strategic adaptivity, directly benchmarking them against the actual ITS responses for the same scenarios. Our results indicate that while LLMs can generate plausible and often helpful instructional feedback, their adaptivity significantly lags behind sophisticated ITS. LLMs struggled with consistently selecting optimal strategies that build on prior interactions or address deeper conceptual gaps without explicit, detailed prompt engineering for each turn, particularly in complex scenarios requiring nuanced student model inference and long-term pedagogical planning. This study highlights the current challenges for LLMs in fully replicating ITS adaptivity and points to critical areas for future research in integrating explicit pedagogical models with LLM capabilities.
prefix: Large Language Models (LLMs) hold promise as dynamic instructional aids. Yet, it remains unclear whether LLMs can replicate the adaptivity of intelligent tutoring systems (ITS)--where student knowledge and pedagogical strategies are explicitly modeled. We propose a prompt variation framework to assess LLM-generated instructional moves' adaptivity and pedagogical soundness across 75 real-world tutoring scenarios from an ITS.

title: Being a real nurse: A secondary qualitative analysis of how public health nurses rework their work identities.
text_ai: Many Western nations are emphasizing the importance of population health across health care delivery organizations and education systems. Despite significant momentum to integrate population health into nursing practice, a parallel effort to examine how these efforts impact practicing nurses' views of their professional role and work identity has not occurred. This secondary qualitative analysis explores how public health nurses (PHNs) negotiate their professional identities amidst evolving population health expectations, addressing a critical gap. Using existing Canadian PHN qualitative data, this study examines their lived experiences. Findings reveal PHNs' complex process of constructing "being a real nurse," often feeling undervalued and marginalized by acute care definitions. They redefine their professional worth within population health practice, highlighting tensions between traditional nursing identities and less visible contributions. Implications for education, development, and policy underscore validating population health nursing to support PHNs' identity and strengthen outcomes.

Despite significant momentum to integrate population health into nursing practice, a parallel effort to examine how these efforts impact practicing nurses' views of their professional role and work identity has not occurred.

title: REPOSE: Distributed Top-k Trajectory Similarity Search with Local Reference Point Tries
text_ai: Trajectory similarity computation is a fundamental component in a variety of real-world applications, such as ridesharing, road planning, and transportation optimization. Recent advances in mobile devices have enabled an unprecedented increase in the amount of available trajectory data such that efficient query processing can no longer be supported by a single machine. Existing distributed methods for trajectory similarity search face high communication overhead and complex data partitioning. We propose REPOSE, a novel distributed framework for efficient top-k trajectory similarity search. REPOSE introduces Local Reference Point Tries (LRPTs), an innovative indexing structure that partitions and indexes trajectory data locally. LRPTs enable localized candidate generation, significantly reducing cross-node communication. This maximizes parallelism and minimizes network overhead, achieving superior scalability and performance. Extensive experiments show REPOSE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art distributed methods in query latency, throughput, and scalability, establishing a robust solution for large-scale trajectory analytics.

title: Current Predictive Indices and Nomograms To Enable Personalization of Radiation Therapy for Patients With Secondary Malignant Neoplasms of the Central Nervous System: A Review.
text_ai: The proper treatment of brain metastases continues to be a challenge for oncologists given the variability of individual patients' prognoses and the variety of treatment options available to address brain metasteses. There have been efforts since the 1990s to develop prognostic indices and nomograms to help clinicians determine the best approach for individuals with secondary malignant neoplasms of the central nervous system. These tools stratify patients by clinical, pathological, and molecular characteristics to predict prognosis and guide optimal radiation therapy. This review systematically examines current predictive indices and nomograms, notably the Graded Prognostic Assessment (GPA) and its molecular subtypes, critically assessing their methodologies, predictive accuracy, and clinical utility in personalizing radiation therapy decisions such as whole-brain radiation therapy (WBRT) and stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS). The objective is to provide an updated understanding of how these tools optimize treatment selection, improve patient outcomes, and inform future research in personalized neuro-oncology.

title: Decoding and Reconstructing the Focus of Spatial Attention from the Topography of Alpha-band Oscillations.
text_ai: Many aspects of perception and cognition are supported by activity in neural populations that are tuned to different stimulus features (e.g., orientation, spatial location, color). Goal-directed behavior, such as sustained attention, requires a mechanism for the selective prioritization of contextually appropriate representations. Alpha-band (8-12 Hz) oscillations are increasingly recognized as a crucial mechanism for this prioritization, modulating cortical excitability by inhibiting distracting information at unattended locations. Yet, the precise topographical relationship between alpha activity and the dynamic focus of spatial attention remains unclear. We investigated if the spatial locus of attention can be decoded and reconstructed from human EEG alpha power topography. Participants performed a spatial attention task. Multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) and a novel topographical reconstruction mapped the attended location from scalp alpha power distributions. Results demonstrate that attention's focus can be accurately decoded from alpha power topography, significantly above chance. We further reconstructed a continuous spatial representation of the attended location from alpha-band activity, revealing an inverse relationship where increased alpha power corresponded to unattended regions. These findings provide strong evidence that alpha oscillation topography serves as a dynamic neural signature of the attentional spotlight, actively shaping cortical excitability for goal-directed behavior, highlighting its potential as an attentional biomarker.
